News.title: Girl, 16, dies after being ‘gang-raped and abandoned in field with broken neck’ as three men ‘who lured her’ arrested
News.content:
RAPE HORROR Girl, 16, dies after being ‘gang-raped and abandoned in field with broken neck’ as three men ‘who lured her’ arrested







Next

A 16-YEAR-OLD girl has died in hospital after allegedly being gang-raped and left for dead in a field with a broken neck.

The teen victim spent nearly a week fighting for her life on a ventilator before tragically succumbing to her injuries.

Three men – aged 20, 21 and 28 – have been arrested on suspicion of rape, abduction and murder following the sickening attack in northern India.

Cops say the schoolgirl was lured to an isolated field in Firozabad on November 1 by one of the suspects, whom she had reportedly known for several months.





When the youngster desperately fought back, the group allegedly gang-raped and strangled her before fleeing the scene, believing she was already dead.

She was later discovered lying semi-conscious in the dirt by locals and rushed to hospital.

A post-mortem examination confirmed the youngster was sexually assaulted and suffered a broken neck, crushed jaw and multiple fractured bones.

A heartbroken relative told the Times of India: “She was gang-raped, tortured and left to die…



“She was put on ventilator support and could not record her statement before her death.”

A police source told local media: “When she resisted, they strangled her and crushed her limbs and jaw.

“Believing her to be dead, they left. Two of them were arrested following a brief encounter on the night of November 1 – the third was held the next day.”

Cops initially launched an investigation into attempted murder and gang-rape of a minor, before upgrading the charges to murder following the girl’s death on November 6.



Senior officers have promised to fast-track the case and secure the maximum possible penalties against the alleged offenders.

Firozabad senior police superintendent Aditya Langesh said: “All three accused have been arrested. This case has been taken up on priority under Operation Conviction.

“Action will also be initiated against the accused under the Gangsters Act, including an investigation into their properties and steps for attachment or confiscation.”

Additional police superintendent Jaibind Gupta added: “I’m personally supervising the investigation. We’ve assured the family of severe punishment and justice.”

Sexual assaults on women have become disturbingly familiar in India.



Police recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024 as part of over 440,000 registered crimes against women, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.

The real figure is believed to be far higher due to the stigma surrounding sexual violence and victims’ lack of faith in police.

News.title: My dad & brother died in gangland massacre and I made millions from drugs but I’m glad I was jailed, says ex-Mafia boss
News.content:
Next

BOBBY Luisi Jr lived like a “movie star” selling cocaine for Colombian barons – but he “felt 100 pounds lighter” when he was finally nicked by the FBI.

The American former Mafia captain was raised in the underworld, with his brother and father dying in an infamous gangland massacre.



Bobby, 65, admitted to having a role in “half a dozen murders”, was linked to a £400million art heist and served 14 years in prison for trafficking cocaine.

He had a “reputation” for being able to handle himself in the bloody wars between Boston mobsters in the 1990s.



But he insists he didn’t want to follow his dad Bobby Luisi Sr into criminality and was “smiling” when justice came knocking in 1999.

Luisi Jr, who became a Christian preacher, tells The Sun: “I didn’t want to chase the money anymore.



“The day they came to arrest me they were walking me down the stairs I felt something break off my shoulders like a weight. I can’t explain it.

“Like a weight just came off my shoulders. I felt 100 pounds lighter. I said, wow, what happened? And I was smiling. I was smiling going into the cop car in the back.”

Bobby Luisi Sr, from the North End area of East Boston, Massachusetts, worked for the Patriarca crime syndicate, using a baseball bat to get his way, dealing cocaine and stealing drugs from rivals.

At first his son got involved, rolling “dime machines” – stealing cash from slot machines – when he was aged 11 years old.



But Luisi Jr found a love for carpentry and initially turned his back on crime, running a successful building firm with 20 men working for him.

That all ended when the building market crashed in 1989 and the following year he “went back on the street.”

By 1993, Luisi Jr was a millionaire from selling cocaine and running a loan shark operation.

He says: “I don’t know how many millions I’ve made. The money was coming in hand over fist.

“We had the houses, the beautiful cars, expensive suits. We had Armanis, Burberrys, $300, $400, $500 shoes.



“I was living like a movie star. That was one of the perks of it and that’s what really drove me, I think. It was really like ego, pride.”

Rival syndicates wanted their share of those lucrative markets and were willing to kill to get their hands on it.

Like his dad, he worked for the Patriarca family, but in the 1990s it split into two factions with Robert Carrozza taking on boss Frank Salemme for control.

Luisi Jr, who was part of Salemme’s crew, says: “There was a murder or two in that period. I can’t talk about that, really.

“We had rival gangs, in 1990 war broke out and it got really heavy about, 93, around 94. And there was a murder.



“There were rival gangs against us. They were trying to wipe us out, but praise God, I was the last man standing.”

But his dad Luisi Sr, brother Roman and cousin Anthony Sarro did not escape with their lives.

In 1995 they were slaughtered during lunch at the 99 Restaurant in Charlestown, Boston, as more than 50 regular diners dived for cover.



One of their other associates, Anthony Pelosi, also died.

Luisi Jr reveals that the shooting happened by chance, when two sets of rivals with a “beef” ran into other.

He recalls: “I lost my family in the 99 restaurant shooting. I had words with my father the night before.

“I just wanted to squash the beef and by accident, they all ran into each other at the 99. It wasn’t a planned thing. It was a coincidence.”

The two shooters – Anthony Clemente and his son Damian – were caught by off duty police officers who had been eating in the restaurant, and were later convicted of first degree murder.



Luisi Jr’s younger brother Roman had been acquitted of a double murder in Hollywood, California the year before and was heading for trouble.

Luisi Jr comments: “When he came back to Boston he was living in California and he killed a few people down there. I guess he got away with self-defence and he came back home.

“He was a bad kid, tough guy, would kill you in a minute. I’m still hurt what happened to him. I love my brother but what are we going to do?

“That’s why everybody was afraid. They knew how bad he was and how quick he was with the trigger. And that’s what really pushed that 99 meeting over the edge.”

Luisi Jr started dealing drugs for the Merlino mob in Philadelphia, which was to prove to be his undoing.



They were under surveillance by the FBI and one of the secret agents recorded him discussing a deal.

According to Luisi Jr he was already trying to wind down his involvement in the drugs trade by this point, having “found Christ” 15 months prior to his arrest in June 1999.

He recalls: “I saw a lot of evil that I did. I became a born again Christian. I always wanted to be the boss.

“Then I didn’t want it anymore. That’s why I smiled that day when I got into the cop car.”



Luisi Jr was found guilty in 2002 of cocaine trafficking and served 14 years behind bars.

It was tough in prison.

He says: “I got in many fights. I witnessed fights. I walked in a lot of cells going after people.

“I had a reputation so not too many people wanted to fight me. I was in there, 6ft, 250 pounds and a tough guy.



“Prison is prison. You’ve got to stand up for yourself.

“A lot of people died. A lot of people got killed.”

He also studied the Bible and gained a degree in theology while inside.

Luisi Jr says: “I taught in prison. I taught a Bible course in prison. I had a lot of followers in prison.

“So prison, it was just a good reform for me. I tell a lot of people I’m happy that I did that 14 years and they don’t understand it, but it changed me, changed my life.”



Although he had changed his life, it was alleged in court in 2012 that he had links to a gangster accused of the theft of 13 masterworks from Boston’s Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum.

Art by Rembrandt, Degas, Manet and Vermeer were stolen in the 1990 heist.

Luisi Jr claims he was told where the stolen artwork was hidden, but didn’t want to get involved in shifting the gear.

He recalls: “There was a lot of heat. I was told it’s buried under a slab in Florida. I said I’m really not into that and these stolen articles.

“I said I really won’t know what to do with them and I let it go and I stopped talking about it.



“To be honest with you I wish I would have tried to recover that five, ten million.”

After leaving prison, he made it his mission to help others steer clear of crime.

He started the Bobby Luisi Ministries and has his own YouTube program called the Bobby Luisi Show where he preaches the Gospel.

Luisi Jr does not believe the Mafia is as powerful as it used to be.

He concludes: “The Mob is diminished over here. Boston, Philadelphia, Chicago all the heavy big families, there’s no big numbers anymore.



“The Mafia is never going to be like it was. Its days are over. It lasted over 100 years, but it’s all done now.

“Doing drugs just brought heat. It brought a lot of bad things on. That’s how they end up getting me.”

Checkout Bobby’s You Tube channel

News.title: Inside Iran’s militant cell ‘CyberAv3ngers’ waging war on Europe’s supermarkets as ringleader with $10m bounty revealed
News.content:
Next

IRAN’S militant CyberAveng3rs hacker cell is feared to be behind a wave of attacks devastating Europe’s supermarkets and blood supplies.

A $10million (£7.4m) bounty has been placed on the ringleaders of the regime’s ruthless cyber gang, led by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).



France has blamed the hacking outfit for heating up fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across the country, destroying millions of euros worth of food.

Coolers were remotely dialled up to as much as 80C, while multiple blood banks were also infiltrated last week, with temperatures soaring to 110C.



Prosecutors in Paris have now launched a formal probe into the breach and are zeroing in on the IRGC-led Shahid Kaveh cyber unit, also referred to as CyberAveng3rs, which is the group’s propaganda arm.

At the heart of Shahid Kaveh is Intelligence Group 13, one of the most aggressive units in Iran’s cyber warfare network.

It uses cyber espionage, industrial sabotage and psychological warfare to strike at Western infrastructure.

The unit has spearheaded operations targeting Israeli electricity networks, American water facilities and fuel distribution systems.

Previous suspected attacks include disruptions to the Los Angeles transit system in March, water treatment plants in July and ships bound for the US in August.

Shahid Kaveh’s aim is to infiltrate vital systems and potentially cripple them from within.



One of its most alarming tactics is planting malware inside networks long before an attack is launched.

These digital implants can lie dormant until activated, allowing hackers to sabotage systems that may appear perfectly secure.

Shahid Kaveh’s operations are supported by phishing attacks, stolen passwords and intelligence gathered from publicly available sources.



These techniques help hackers identify weaknesses, break into networks and prepare targets for future disruption.

CyberAveng3rs spreads the group’s exploits through Telegram and Instagram, publishing screenshots of stolen information and taunting messages to spread fear and undermine confidence in Western security.

French foreign minister Jean-Nol Barrot slammed the supermarket hack for its “unprecedented scale and aggressiveness” adding that it was the first “large scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on French soil”.

Barrot said the breach represented a “major threat” to the security of the French people and vowed that “it will not go unanswered”.

French spy agencies named three associates connected with the attacks as Hamid Reza Lashgarian, Mahdi Lashgarian and Reza Salarvand by French spy and cyber agencies.



What is Shahid Kaveh? THE Shahid Kaveh Group - known online as CyberAv3ngers - are an elite gang of cyber criminals working for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC-CEC) Their name translates to “Martyr Kaveh” after a 25-year-old IRGC commander who was killed during the Iran-Iraq war. Shahid Kaveh’s exact founding date is unknown – but secret leaked docs suggest the gang has been active since at least 2020. Since then the group have repeatedly hacked targets across the US, Israel and Europe. Their first verified attacks in late 2023 exploited weak passwords to take over industrial control systems – similar to the French fridge attacks which used the username “Supervisor” alongside the password “12345” to send temperatures soaring. Early hacks mainly targeted Israel – but the group has increasingly started sabotaging US and European systems. In the US the Shahid Kaveh Group have primarily infiltrated energy, water and waste facilities. More than 30 water systems in Minnesota were targeted in July this year with other states also reporting hacks. The attackers often override control screens to show anti-Israel or pro-Iran propaganda. Leaked dossiers revealed that the group have also researched how cyberattacks could be used to sink cargo ships, blow up fuel pumps at petrol stations or breach building security systems.

The US has previously offered a $10million (£7.4million) bounty for both Lashgarians, as well as senior IRGC security officials Milad Mansuri, Mohammad Bagher Shirinkar, and Mohammad Amin Saberian.

France‘s Iranian ambassador has been summoned after investigators found IP addresses linked to Iran and the use of Farsi.

Last week, hackers infiltrated multiple blood banks across France and set temperatures soaring from -30C to 110C.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The attack was thwarted before it could do lasting damage to the critical blood donations – used in life-saving care.

France’s Foreign Ministry said: “France condemns in the strongest possible terms the unacceptable cyberattacks carried out on its territory by the Islamic Republic of Iran against French interests.”

News.title: Labour’s deputy Lucy Powell defends Ed Miliband’s interview with Russell Brand
News.content:
Next

LUCY Powell has defended Ed Miliband’s decision to cosy up to Russell Brand in 2015 – claiming it was a “different era”.

The Education Secretary insisted nobody knew Brand was a sexual predator when the then Labour leader appeared on his YouTube show during the general election campaign.



Ms Powell, who was in charge of Labour’s day-to-day campaigning, helped broker the bizarre interview in a bid to woo young voters.

But the stunt has come back to haunt her after Brand was jailed for ten-and-a-half years on Monday for rape and three sexual assaults.



Grilled about her role in arranging the meeting, Ms Powell told Sky News: “It was a long time ago, obviously and had I or Ed Miliband or anybody at the time had any sense at all that this was someone who was a sexual predator, who was involved in these sorts of crimes or any allegations around that that were known at the time, then of course…

“That interview, that… many platforms that he had at the time I’m sure would not have happened.

“The issue would have been very, very different. Those things unfortunately weren’t known at the time”.

She added: “I think like anybody who would have paid to go to his show, would have watched him on TV, who was his employer at the time, who had interactions with him – anybody, including those of us who were involved in that at the time – would look back and really regret that, knowing today what we now know.”

Brand had already been booted off BBC Radio 2 over lewd phone calls to actor Andrew Sachs about his granddaughter.

He had also been fired from XFM for reading pornography on air and had detailed his womanising in his autobiography.



Ms Powell also insisted that Brand had approached Labour about the interview rather than the other way around.

She went on: “We weren’t in the social media age at the time, where you could maybe search things up and see allegations or things about somebody.

“As I say, if there was any suggestion at all we were dealing with someone who was a known sexual predator at the time then of course, no one would have done that.

“But as I say, he was a well-known public figure. Lots of people, from Hollywood to the BBC to many others, gave this person a very, very powerful platform.

“We didn’t know at the time and unfortunately, maybe had people come forward or felt able to… it was a different era.”



Mr Miliband visited Brand’s east London home just days before the 2015 general election to film an interview for his online show The Trews.

The comedian, then a darling of the Left, had previously urged people not to vote, arguing that British democracy was broken.

During their kitchen-table chat, Mr Miliband tried to convince him that voting could bring about political change.

Labour went on to suffer a crushing election defeat to David Cameron’s Conservatives.

Andy Burnham also previously praised Brand in 2014 for using his celebrity to “help others”, urging him to “keep going” after a row over his tax arrangements.



But the PM condemned Brand’s crimes as “horrifying” after his conviction last week.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brand was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Monday after being found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009.

News.title: Exact day phones will be BANNED from schoolchildren’s bags and pockets under stricter crackdown
News.content:
Next

PHONES are set to be banned from pupils’ bags and pockets under new government plans next year.

Affecting secondary schools across England, the tougher regulations follow the smartphone ban rolled-out in June.

From September 1, 2027, pupils across the country will be subject to a new, tougher ban on mobile phones during the school day.



The stricter government guidance will build on existing “no see, no hear” policies in place in certain secondary schools, which allows pupils to keep phones locked away in sealed pouches, bags and pockets.



Now, education secretary Lucy Powell said: “Children should not be using smartphones at any point during the school day, full stop.

“That’s why we’re strengthening our guidance to take the next leap towards truly phone-free schools.

“School is for learning and friendship, not scrolling.”

Schools will be able to choose how to enforce the ban, which may see pupils handing in their mobiles at the start of the day.

Others have invested in secure lockers and even metal detectors to prevent schoolchildren stashing away phones in hidden pockets.

The ban is set to affect all state secondary schools across England from September 1 – although the exact date will vary depending when secondary schools re-open after the summer break.

In June this year, section 36 of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 was introduced in response to the rise in children using phones during lessons.



Under the new law, schools must be phone-free environments, ensuring pupils do not have access to smart phones throughout the school day.

This includes between lessons, at break times and during lunch, with a “no ifs, no buts” policy that is checked via Ofsted inspections to make sure schools are consistently enforcing the ban.

News.title: ‘Cauliflower symptom’ to watch out for as contagious dog cancer returns to UK for first time in over 50 years
News.content:
Next

DOG owners have been urged to look out for a “cauliflower symptom” in their pets as a contagious dog cancer returns to the UK.

While the unusual cancer has been almost absent in the UK for 50 years, a rise in cases has been recorded recently.

Canine Transmissible Venereal Tumour (CTVT) is a rare and contagious type of cancer that can spread between dogs via physical contact, primarily through mating, but also from birth, biting, and licking.



Dog owners have been urged to check their pets for key symptoms, as the disease has been appearing more and more in the UK, according to vets.



The most noticeable symptom of CTVT to watch out for is grey or pink cauliflower-like “masses” that can appear on your dog’s genitals.

These masses may bleed and can produce discharge.

Other signs to look out for in affected dogs include swelling, excessive licking of the genital area, and difficulty urinating.

A number of other symptoms can also be linked to CTVT, such as bad breath, dental problems, frequent sneezing, nosebleeds, facial sores and ulcers on the skin.

However, it is worth noting that these are common among many different conditions in dogs.

The spread of the disease is believed to have come from an increased popularity in importing dogs to the UK from CTVT-endemic areas, primarily Eastern Europe, according to Cambridge University’s The Transmissible Cancer Group.

While its name may be worrying, CTVT has a good prognosis for dogs if caught early, and is typically treated with chemotherapy.



CTVT can be prevented through a number of means, including keeping your dog on a lead when outside, neutering or spaying your dog, asking vets about pre-breeding checks and taking them for routine check-ups.

The University of Cambridge’s Transmissible Cancer Group is also offering testing for CTVT for free to vets across the UK in a bid to tackle the current rise in cases.

News.title: At least 12 dead & dozens injured after horror 50-vehicle pile-up on motorway in Bulgaria
News.content:
Next

AT LEAST 12 people have died in a horror 50-car pile-up on a foggy motorway in Bulgaria.

Emergency crews rushed to the scene on the busy highway, where a huge pileup of cars and trucks across six lanes left more than 50 people injured.



The mangled wreckage spanned both sides of the A1 in the east of the country, leaving numerous vehicles overturned, crushed, or completely forced off the road.

Prime Minister Rumen Radev confirmed the accident earlier in the day, calling it a “tragedy”.



An emergency aircraft has reportedly been deployed to evacuate the dozens of injured people as ground crews work to rescue victims still trapped in their cars.

Convoys ambulances arrived at the scene every few minutes in the immediate aftermath as emergency crews combed through the wreckage, according to local reports.

Health Minister Katya Ivkova said of the fatalities 10 died on the spot and two others died while being raced to hospital.

She said 46 people were transported to medical facilities for treatment, many of who have multiple injuries including severely broken limbs.



Over a of the dozen victims are seriously injured with some are fighting for life, local media reports.

General Secretary of the Interior Ministry, Lyubomir Nikolov, said that fog was the likely cause of the accident which started with a collision between a bus and a truck on the side of the highway heading towards Burgas.

Officials said their main priority is the rescue operation, adding, “Once it is completed, the procedural and investigative actions will be carried out.”



Todor Mishinev, head of the local traffic police, said many of the people trapped were in tanker lorries with rescuers forced to cut through metal to free them.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, who was visiting Bulgaria when the crash occurred, announced she would cut her trip short out to allow the Prime Minister to properly address the tragic accident.

She said: “I would like to express my deepest condolences and I would like to pay respects to the rescue teams.”

Senior officials have reportedly been dispatched to the scene at the Trakia highway in the section near Yambol.

The first emergency call came at about 7:10am local time.



The motorway has been closed in both directions between the Zimnitsa and Kabile junctions and traffic cops are currently redirecting all motorists along a detour route.

Bulgaria’s Road Infrastructure Agency said the closure would last for some time because of the heavy vehicles involved and the investigation.

News.title: Poland gunman’s sister, 21, pictured after he executed her with 2 bullets to the head before slaughtering 6 in shooting
News.content:
Next

A POLISH mass shooter’s sister, who he executed with two bullets to the head before slaughtering six more people, has been pictured for the first time.

Michal Oksinski, 24, gunned down Magdalena, 21, their parents and two pet cats at the family home before going on a rampage in Krakow’s packed market square.



He loaded his car with more than 500 rounds of ammunition before spraying at random, killing six people including a British national.

A further 15 people were injured before hero cops gunned Oksinski down.



His sister Magdalena, a student at the Krakow Academy of Fine Arts, is among the first two victims pictured since the tragedy.

Neighbours have described her as a “very talented girl” who had always been a “good student and a beautiful painter”.

One of her university professors, Andrzej Bednarczyk, paid tribute to the young student, lamenting: “Nothing will be the same again”.

An extra-curricular activity centre she attended described her as “an exceptionally gifted artist” and a “sensitive, hard-working, modest, and warm person”.



Her parents’ identities are yet to be confirmed, but Polish media have reported that her dad was Janusz, 53 and her mum was Renata, 52.

Painter and mum-of-four Izabela Woźna, 53, was another victim brutally murdered by Oksinski.

She had just opened a new art exhibition in Krakow and often contributed to local cultural events.



Jacek Gursz, mayor of Chodzież, said she was “in the wrong place at the wrong time” and expressed his condolences to the family for their “unimaginable pain”.

He told Polish news outlet TVN24 that Izabela infected everyone with her optimism and kindness.

A 32-year-old unnamed Brit was also among the dead, the UK’s consulate in Poland confirmed.

Oksinski died in hospital on Monday morning, where he had been taken in critical condition after being shot by police.

The two cops who stopped him – Artur Morański and Jakub ‘Kuba’ Kulik – reamin in hospital.



Both are conscious, with Morański emerging from a coma on Sunday afternoon.

Mayor of Muszyna Jan Golba revealed that his first words after waking up where “Is Kuba alive?”.

Meanwhile, thousands took part in a silent march through Krakow on Monday evening to grieve the victims of the massacre.

Heartbreaking photos show mourners placing candles at the spots where people had been killed.

Investigators are yet to establish a motive for the crime, with a probe set to clarify the circumstances of the attack.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Government sources previously suggested that the shooter had been motivated by “far right ideology” but investigators appeared to backtrack on Monday.

Government spokesperson Adam Szlapka said: “Until the matter is fully clarified, it is best to refrain from making comments, even if there are some initial indications.”

News.title: US military aircraft leave second UK base
News.content:
At least 10 US Air Force refuelling aircraft left a second airbase in Britain on Monday.

Flight tracking data seen by BBC Verify shows the aircraft left RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk and landed at other American bases in Europe and also at Prestwick Airport in Ayrshire.

The Wall Street Journal reported that this was in response to a threat from Iran but the BBC has not independently verified that claim.

Monday's departures come weeks after the US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford airbase over a suspected Iran-linked security incident.

Asked about Monday's flights, an MoD spokesperson told the BBC: "We do not routinely comment on the activity of other nations. Aircraft and other assets move regularly âaccording to operational ârequirements."

Using public tracking site Flightradar24 BBC Verify has been able to see USAF KC-135 tankers leaving Mildenhall throughout Monday.

Two aircraft that left initially flew to US bases in Germany and Italy. The first KC-135 then returned to Mildenhall before heading east and landing at Spangdahlem airbase in Germany. The other aircraft - having flown circuits over Aviano airbase in Italy - flew on to and landed at Spangdahlem.

Flight-tracking data also shows eight other US KC-135s left Mildenhall later on Monday.

An aircraft that landed at Prestwick in Scotland on Monday is with the Nebraska Air National Guard, meaning it may have been on a regular stop before heading back to its American base.

News.title: Met Police investigate several new reports on Russell Brand following his conviction
News.content:
The officer who led the investigation into Russell Brand has said the Metropolitan Police is "triaging" calls from people following his conviction and sentence.

Speaking to BBC Breakfast on Tuesday, Det Supt Andy Furphy said the force had "several reports in during the trial and since the trial".

He said that officers were in the "process of triaging" them and were "looking at exactly what we've got, whether they're information that points to behaviour or whether they could constitute a criminal offence, so our work isn't done."

Brand is already being investigated over rape allegations from two more women. He has been interviewed under caution in connection to those allegations.

On Monday, the disgraced entertainer was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison, after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

In his sentencing remarks, judge Joel Bennathan described Brand as a "sexual predator" and criticised his "staggering arrogance".

The 51-year-old was sentenced to nine years for rape, with an additional 18 months, nine months and eight months for three counts of sexual assault. The latter sentences are to run concurrently.

He was found guilty of the charges involving four women between 2004 and 2009.

News.title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England
News.content:
Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.

Statutory guidance came into force in June, making schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.

Ministers now say changes to that guidance will go beyond the current "no see, no hear" policies in place in some schools - where phones can remain in pupils' bags if they are not seen or heard - when it comes into force from September 2027.

But head teachers' unions said schools would struggle to implement stricter new policies without additional funding from government.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government's "clear message" to parents and pupils was that "school is for learning and friendship, not scrolling".

Access to phones "risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other", the government said.

Schools will be able to decide how to follow the guidance. Some schools have invested in sealed pouches or secure lockers. Others collect phones at the start of the day, or have prohibited them from sites altogether.

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".

Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent Â£20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.

While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.

"People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.

"It's also increased levels of focus in lessons because now there's less distraction, and people are achieving higher grades."

News.title: Edinburgh Academy pupils suffered decades of 'dreadful abuse'
News.content:
Pupils at Edinburgh Academy suffered decades of "dreadful abuse", a report has found.

Lady Smith, who chairs the Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry (SCAI), details more than 40 years of sexual, physical, and emotional abuse at the school in her latest report, external.

She says the school focused on protecting its reputation and ignored complaints.

Lady Smith also names four serial perpetrators of the abuse, including two who went on to offend at other schools.

Edinburgh Academy, which had previously apologised for "brutal and unrestrained" historical abuse, said it was committed to facing up to "the wrongs of the past".

The inquiry heard claims of historical abuse against 20 teaching staff at the private school, with most of the evidence covering the years between 1954 and 1995.

Nearly 50 witnesses gave evidence, including broadcaster Nicky Campbell - who said one teacher had abused children on an "industrial scale".

News.title: The superpower battle over energy – and what it means for your bills
News.content:
A gas rig in the North Sea. An oil field in Texas. A solar panel factory in China. They can feel a world away, but your energy bill says otherwise.

In January, it could jump by more than a quarter â around Â£460 extra a year for the typical UK household â according to the latest forecasts from the big suppliers British Gas, EDF and E.ON.

For the second time in four years, a war thousands of miles away is landing in British inboxes.

Since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, oil and gas prices have soared.

Winter is expected to push them higher still: demand for gas is rising just as Europe's winter gas stores are at their lowest since records began in 2011.

And there's a bigger threat looming over all of this: the warming climate. Cutting carbon emissions is essential to limit future warming and avoid the most damaging effects of climate change. But keeping bills down while cutting emissions is proving hard â and not just for the UK.

As world leaders gather this week in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the UN climate summit, the same tension is playing out around the world. Energy and climate policy has become the front line in a contest between the world's two energy superpowers, leaving everyone else squeezed in between.

America is betting on fossil-fuel molecules: pumping record volumes of oil and gas and pressing its allies to buy them. China is betting on electrons: flooding the world with the solar panels, batteries and electric cars that can replace those fuels.

Whether the bet on fossil fuels or renewables wins will shape not just what the world pays for energy, but how fast it can cut the emissions that are heating the planet.

The UK, which already buys nearly a quarter of its imported gas from America and much of its clean energy kit from China, is being pulled both ways. So which path will it take? Is there a middle way and what will it all mean for your bills?

News.title: Meghan joins Harry in Brussels in first public appearance since father's arrest
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has made her first public appearance since her father was charged with possession of child sex abuse material.

Meghan joined her husband Prince Harry at the European Parliament in Brussels on Tuesday, where he delivered a speech calling for greater protection for children online.

Harry gave the keynote address alone after Meghan reportedly withdrew from speaking alongside him because she did not feel emotionally strong enough.

The duchess was seen holding her husband's hand tightly as they arrived at the Paul-Henri Spaak building. She did not respond to questions from reporters about how she was feeling.

During his speech, Harry said he and his wife stood alongside parents who had lost children to online harm.

"I'm not here as an expert or a politician. I'm here as a father. My wife, a mother," he told the European Parliament.

The duke stressed the importance of preventing online harm and said children "deserve to feel safe wherever they are", including in classrooms and playgrounds.

He did not reference Meghan's father, Thomas Markle, who appeared in court in Florida on Friday charged with possession of child sex abuse images.

Markle, who is currently under home detention and subject to electronic monitoring, has previously denied the allegations.

Meghan has been estranged from her father for several years. He did not attend her wedding in Windsor in 2018 citing "ill health" at the time.

When reports emerged about Thomas Markle last month, including allegations he possessed child sex abuse images, Meghan released a statement saying she was "deeply distressed at the news" and hoped that "justice will be fully served".

News.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
News.content:
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.

Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.

After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.

"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.

"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.

Further evidence of stockpiling came from food firm Princes on Tuesday, which said demand for tinned tuna, meat and vegetables had risen following the government's campaign.

Princes interim chief executive Giuseppe Mastrolia said the jump in demand "further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions".

The "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need - for example, bottled water, and long-life food that doesn't need to be kept in the fridge such as dried fruit and nuts.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".

News.title: Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided at Wednesday meeting
News.content:
Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Bruno Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft later claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser.

The Portugal playmaker, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

He has scored just once - a penalty against Villa on Sunday - in the league since.

After the Ipswich win came a trip to Everton.

Twice United led, the second occasion when Sesko struck two minutes from full-time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

What happened next, however, was.

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before their rivals benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

The fine margins United benefited from during Carrick's interim spell were now going against them, and his coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

Carrick called Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom of the table a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The whirlwind was starting to pick up strength.

Lisandro Martinez, who scored an own goal against Fulham, was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back that eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role was in full swing.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 Champions League defeat for United. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea. United were beaten in both matches.

With just three wins in 15 matches in all competitions this season and United stuck in 18th in the Premier League, Carrick is set to pay the price.

News.title: Jemima Goldsmith accuses Russell Brand of violence and abuse against her
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content.

Jemima Goldsmith, the ex-girlfriend of Russell Brand, has accused him of "violence, coercive control and abuse" while the two were together.

Goldsmith, who dated the disgraced entertainer for roughly a year around 2014, alleged that she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.

In a lengthy statement on social media, the 52-year-old said she was "in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand's trial" and was "glad and relieved" he had "finally faced justice".

Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison earlier on Monday after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

He was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women.

The judge at the sentencing hearing told Brand that he harboured a "casual arrogant disregard to any woman's right to say no to you", while his fame meant he believed "you could act when you liked and how you liked".

News.title: Man who stole ambulance with patient inside jailed
News.content:
A drug addict who stole an ambulance with an elderly patient and paramedic inside has been jailed for 21 months.

Marshall Leese, a prolific user of monkey dust, was chased by police for two miles after taking the ambulance from outside the Royal Stoke University Hospital in Stoke-on-Trent.

He stopped at a petrol station on the A34 in Newcastle-under-Lyme and fled the vehicle but was found hiding nearby by a police sniffer dog.

The 32-year-old appeared at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court after previously admitting false imprisonment and aggravated vehicle taking following the theft on 25 March.

Recorder Ben Williams KC said Leese struck when the ambulance driver went into the hospital holding the keys.

"The driver had left it in a mode which meant it still was running while he went inside... leaving his colleague in the back with an elderly patient and that gentleman's carer," he said.

News.title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea
News.content:
Conservationists say thousands of rare flowers have been saved from falling into the sea on the Moray coast.

In the UK, the one-flowered wintergreen can only be found in pine woodlands in north-east Scotland.

More than half the entire population of the star-shaped flower have been lost over the last 50 years.

About 3,400 of the tiny plants have been rescued from an area of eroded beach at Culbin Sands, an area of dunes and forest near Findhorn, and moved to a safe location nearby.

News.title: Festival headlined by Andrea Bocelli scraps choirs fee after backlash
News.content:
Organisers of the Land of Song Festival have announced they are scrapping a controversial Â£42 charge per choir member.

The "cheeky" fee prompted some choirs to pull out of the event after realising they would be charged thousands of pounds to take part.

In a social media post, it was confirmed the fee had been scrapped, and those entering were only required to pay the flat fee of Â£150 per choir.

The two-day festival is set to take place in May 2027, with Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli featuring on the Saturday, marking the first time he has played in Wales for 22 years.

Several conductors threatened not to take part when the festival's pricing was revealed in September.

About 40 choirs or singing groups took to social media to say they would refuse to take part in the event because of the cost.

It led to concerns about the festival's viability, with a member of the Glynneath Male Voice Choir suggesting there was a "good possibility" it would not go ahead.

But, on the Land of Song Festival Facebook page, a message from the CÃ´r World Choir & Young Voices CEO said they had "got something important wrong" with the individual chorister registration.

"An event celebrating the joy, community and inclusivity of singing should not create unnecessary barriers to taking part," the post read.

"So we have changed it. If you've already paid an individual registration fee, you will receive an automatic refund. No action is needed."

News.title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women
News.content:
"I want to play my part in making the military feel like the welcoming, open and professional place I enjoyed and make it feel like that for everyone," writes Prince William, in his first intervention on this subject.

"At the moment, I don't feel that we meet those standards and, as a former serving officer, I really mind it when those who wear the uniform now don't feel safe, respected or valued."

According to royal sources, Prince William has been holding his own fact-finding meetings with service women of all ranks, across the Army, Royal Navy and the Royal Air Force.

He has now raised some of those concerns about the issues concerning women in the armed forces, in the article he commissioned for Country Life.

It cites a survey from the Ministry of Defence that found 67% of service women had faced unwanted "sexualised behaviour" every year and that 30% had considered leaving the armed forces because of such behaviour.

The article also references the experiences of Royal Artillery Gunner Jaysley Beck, who took her own life at Larkhill Camp in Wiltshire in 2021.

Gunner Beck had faced months of unwanted attention and had reported a sexual assault and an inquest heard about a complaints system that failed to adequately respond.

Earlier this year, four young women told the BBC they were sexually assaulted and harassed at an Army training college for teenagers - the Army Foundation College at Harrogate, North Yorkshire - with one saying she was raped by fellow junior soldiers in an attack that lasted hours.

News.title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded
News.content:
Twin sisters who were in Krakow when a gunman killed six people have told how they "ran for our lives" when they heard shots.

Sienna and Rimini Chapman, 20, from Northallerton, North Yorkshire, were part of a group celebrating a friend's 21st birthday in Poland when gunfire sounded in the city's Main Market Square at about 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) on Saturday.

The 24-year-old attacker, who died in hospital on Monday, fatally shot four Polish citizens, a British national and an Austrian woman, while a further 15 people, including two police officers, were injured.

Sienna told the BBC their experiences during the attack had been "terrifying".

The group of friends were walking towards a cafe in the square when they first heard gunfire.

"At first I thought the shots were to scare the pigeons away, but then everyone suddenly started running towards us," Sienna said.

"We realised something was wrong and ran in the opposite direction for our lives."

News.title: NHS boss received nearly £400,000 'redundancy' pay-off when she retired
News.content:
An NHS executive has received a near Â£400,000 redundancy pay-off after retiring from a health board, new figures show.

Following a 44-year career in the health service, Mary Morgan retired as chief executive of NHS National Services Scotland (NSS) in May.

But it has now been revealed Morgan received a Â£378,000 payment "under contractual redundancy terms" as part of an exit that came after NHS NSS was merged into a new quango called Public Services Delivery (PSD) Scotland in April.

A PSD Scotland spokesperson said Morgan retired after an "exceptional career" and all payments were in accordance with the terms and conditions of her employment.

The payment comes ahead of a planned major overhaul of Scotland's NHS which could see the number of health boards cut dramatically.

News.title: Watch: Meghan's first public appearance since father arrested
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has made her first public appearance since her father, Thomas Markle, was charged with the possession of child sex abuse material.

Meghan arrived at the European Parliament in Brussels with her husband, Prince Harry, who delivered a speech about online child safety.

During his address, Harry said he and his wife stood alongside parents who had lost children to online harm

The BBC's Jessica Parker has this report.

More on Harry and Meghan's Brussels visit.

News.title: 'I'm furious': Late Queen Elizabeth rages in never-before-seen letters
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The late Queen declared that she was “allergic to vets” in a furious letter about the care of her horses, it has emerged.

In July 1960, a “fuming” Elizabeth II wrote to her equerry, Brigadier Walter Morley Sale, after arguing with a vet over his diagnosis of her horse, Dove.

“I’m furious!” the keen equestrian wrote.

“There is absolutely nothing the matter with her foal ... I’m allergic to vets and I can’t help it.”

In another letter to Brigadier Sale, she asked if she could “sue” a carriage driver who had caused an accident.

open image in gallery Queen Elizabeth meets a horse at a Hertfordshire stable in 1959 ( Getty )

The collection of nearly 50 letters and notes, sent from Elizabeth to her equerry between 1954 and 1961, has been in the Sale family for the past 65 years.

It is now being sold by auctioneers Bonhams, of Knightsbridge in London, and is expected to fetch between £8,000 and £12,000.

Brigadier Sale was responsible for the Royal Mews, the royal family’s collection of stables.

In one letter, Elizabeth told him how she loved riding “challenging horses”, but feared letting Prince Charles ride one.

“Please make sure that the ponies are well-exercised... even [Princess] Anne apparently finds them hard to hold, and Charles will be put off for a certainty,” she said.

open image in gallery Some of the letters that are going up for auction ( Bonhams/BNPS )

In another letter, she downplayed her riding ability, saying: “Sea Breeze is too strong and too good for my sort of once a week riding.

“He might even be Olympic one day... he and I are not in the same equine category.”

In a further letter, sent following an undisclosed carriage accident, she asked Brigadier Sale: “Can we sue the woman for damage or dangerous driving?”

A memo that she wrote a year after her coronation in 1953 showed that she was still getting used to signing her name E.R (Elizabeth Regina).

Referencing a recent formal occasion in London in June 1954, she asked Brigadier Sale to make sure the carriages were open before they drew up in front of her and Prince Philip in the future.

She said: “When we returned to Westminster the other day the carriage was shut and it looked bad, I thought.”

open image in gallery Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip ride a carriage during their Royal Tour of the island of Sark, Channel Islands, in 1957 ( Getty )

She then hurriedly added on another piece of paper “Sorry! I forgot! ER.”

In total, there are seven letters signed 'Elizabeth R' and 37 memoranda.

Brigadier Sale, the son of a diplomat, served in the Second World War before his appointment as Crown Equerry in 1955.

He held the position until 1960 and was appointed Extra Equerry to the Queen in April 1961.

Brigadier Sale and the royal family remained in touch until his death, aged 73, in 1976, and the archive also contains 12 Christmas cards from the monarch.

The auctioneers said that the archive captured both the late Queen's love of horses and her impressive knowledge of them.

open image in gallery The Queen in 1960 riding on the racecourse before the opening of the third day of the Royal Ascot meeting ( PA Wire )

Bonhams manuscripts specialist Matthew Haley said that they offer an “unusual insight” into both her personality and the daily workings of the monarchy.

“The letters have remained in the family until now so they are probably unseen and it is pretty amazing to have such a substantial amount of material amounting to 80 to 100 pages of her writing,” he said.

“They have come down through a few generations and the family now feel it is appropriate to let people see their contents.

“We knew that the Queen loved horses but possibly no one realised she loved them quite this much.”

The Queen died in 2022, at the age of 96.

The sale takes place on 3 December.

News.title: I’ve tested dozens of advent calendars – but these are the ones I’d actually recommend
News.content:
Still good, but not good enough

Harvey Nichols beauty advent calendar 2026: Was £250, now £199 (worth £1,000), Harveynichols.com

( Harvey Nichols )

There are some lovely inclusions in Harvey Nichols’s 2026 beauty advent calendar. This includes the £120 MZ Skin eye cream and Davines Oi conditioner, the latter of which has one of the nicest scents I’ve encountered in haircare. That said, Color Wow’s dream coat, Caudalie beauty elixir and Vyrao’s fragrance are a little familiar from previous advent seasons, and I personally feel the Harvey Nichols tweezers are a disappointing filler item.

Charlotte's Hollywood beauty wonderland advent calendar: £170 (worth £325.50), Charlottetilbury.com

This year's offering features three more products than last year's ( The Independent )

Admittedly, Charlotte Tilbury’s advent calendar for 2026 is better than it was in 2025. It’s £5 cheaper year-on-year and now features launches from the past 12 months, plus items exclusive to the calendar. If previous years are anything to go by, it’ll likely be reduced in the Black Friday sales, too. But there’s one less full-sized item than last year and it doesn’t boast the best value (there’s a 47 per cent saving, but other retailers are offering up to 70 per cent).

Fenwick beauty 25 day advent calendar 2026: £250 (worth £1,000+), Fenwick.co.uk

( Fenwick )

The fragrance selection in Fenwick’s 2026 calendar is undeniably exciting, with luxe brands such as Amouage and Diptyque featured, while the beauty products span skincare, make-up and haircare. However, I’m not sure the beauty line-up alone makes this Christmas countdown stand out, especially given that a handful of the brands are the sort that you find in every advent calendar – namely, Rodial and Philip Kingsley.

Fortnums beauty advent calendar 2026: £275 (worth £1,225), Fortnumandmason.com

( Fortnum & Mason )

The Fortnum and Mason beauty advent calendar offers an exceptionally luxurious, fragrance-heavy lineup that leans into sensory self-care and niche British heritage. It features rare, elevated scents including the floral ambers of Clive Christian’s no1 feminine parfum, the woody universal Gallivant Abu Dhabi eau de parfum, and Ortigia’s aromatic and orange blossom zagara body oil. But, compared with the likes of Space NK and Liberty, this £275 spend won’t get you half as many big-name brands or buzzy products. It’s a great pick, but it’s definitely not for everyone.

Lookfantastic 12 days of K-beauty advent calendar: £50 (worth £140), Lookfantastic.com

It includes 12 days of Korean skincare to unbox ( Alice Reynolds/The Independent )

Compared to Lookfantastic’s main beauty advent calendar, it’s K-beauty offering – while lovely – doesn’t tick every box. There’s no make-up in the calendar, which is a missed opportunity to feature products like Erborian’s CC red correct. Plus the Aromatica rosemary salt and Laneige water sleeping mask are very mini, so not the most useful. That said, the five full-sized products are well-chosen with some of the most sought-after brands falling into the category.

Jo Malone Christmas Kist advent calendar: £375 (worth £597), Jomalone.co.uk

The limited-edition fragrance within drawer 25 was my favourite inclusion ( The Independent )

Whether your fragrance obsession lies in perfumes, candles or beautifully-scented bath and body products, Jo Malone’s advent calendar is made for those who like their Christmas countdown to come with a touch of luxury. Single-brand calendars like this are better for exploring scents without committing to £100+ full-sizes – though, when it comes to Jo Malone, you’ll still be spending several hundreds of pounds to embark on your exploration.

The White Company beauty advent calendar: £195 (worth £336), Thewhitecompany.com

The White Company advent packaging remains largely the same year on year ( The Independent )

There’s plenty to entice fans of the brand here and, for me, it wouldn’t be Christmas without a winter candle from The White Company. It’s a great pick for the home proud individual – with hand washes, reed diffusers and room sprays – but, unfortunately, it isn’t the best option for those looking to explore the wider world of beauty.

Lush advent calendar: £210 (worth not disclosed), Lush.com

( Sabrina Sahota/The Independent )

While not every item in the Lush advent calendar is is full-sized, the brand has been thoughtful about its choice of miniatures. For instance, a 50ml spritz of Santa’s favourite is well placed, given that a Christmas fragrance will likely fall out of favour once January rolls around. Though, I would’ve liked to have seen a sticky dates full-size, given its cult following. There’s also a pair of socks thrown into the mix once again, which I can’t imagine Lush fans will be chomping at the bit for.

Elemis the ultimate beauty advent calendar: £225 (worth £650), Elemis.com

Elemis The Ultimate Beauty Advent Calendar 2026 (Elemis/PA)

Within Elemis’s 2026 beauty advent calendar, fans will find no less than 16 items from the bestselling pro-collagen collection, including a full-size of the viral cleansing balm. There’s also inclusions from the superfood range, as well as two frangipani monoi items for marzipan obsessives (myself included). As always, this is a haul for true Elemis devotees and doesn’t offer the variety of a multi-brand line-up. Plus, some of the SPF marine creams might have been nice to cap off the regimen on offer.

Molton Brown decadent delights the advent calendar: £225 (worth £455), Moltonbrown.co.uk

( Molton Brown )

This year, Molton Brown’s selection looks better than ever with three bottles of hand wash and lotion, a full-size eau de parfum and all manner of shower gels to send you into 2027 smelling fresh. For me, the mesmerising oudh accord and gold candle is the star of the show for its rich, warm aroma. My main bug bear is that the brand has counted its admittedly aesthetic travel perfume case as one of the 24 items. Plus, costing similar to the likes of Sephora and Cult Beauty, I think it’s hard to justify such a high spend on a single brand – unless you’re an absolute mega fan, that is.

When do beauty advent calendars usually sell out?

November is proving to be the month of sell-outs for beauty advent calendars in 2026, with big names disappearing from shelves daily. Harrods and Selfridges were among the first major casualties, but they've since been joined by Cult Beauty's special edition, along with No7's 25 days of beauty calendar and Liz Earle's 24-day offering.

Of course, some calendars don't even make it to autumn. Harrods's 12-day fragrance countdown sold out on its August launch day. On the whole, however, October and November are typically when stock starts dwindling across the board.

With all of 2026's releases now on sale, I’m keeping tabs on any and all Black Friday beauty advent calendar deals as they emerge. Though I’d be wary of holding out for a discount on any calendar you’ve got your heart set on. After all, a saving is no good if your first choice sells out before you can buy it.

Are beauty advent calendars worth it?

In short, yes, beauty advent calendars are always worth more than what you’ll pay; however, you have to consider whether they’ll be worth it for you personally. I’ve been diving into the best beauty advent calendars since 2015 (my first was from M&S) and I can say with confidence that some brands undoubtedly offer a better haul than others. Key things to consider are:

Do you travel a lot – Minis are part and parcel of a beauty advent calendar, so having a place to use them will be key.

Are you unsure where to start in your skincare, haircare or make-up routine – Minis can also be a great way to introduce yourself to premium brands without forking out so much initially

Do you have the time – With everything from face masks to hair bonding treatments within, these products will seriously level up your beauty regimen, but you’ll need to set aside an extra five or ten minutes to use them

What’s your budget – If you’re looking to spend less than £100, you’ll definitely have less big-name brands to choose from your haul. I recommend tallying up the cost of the products you like the look of to ensure you’re getting more than £100 of value from those formulas specifically. Extra products aren’t valuable if you won’t use them.

What is the price range of beauty advent calendars?

Beauty advent calendars can range in price from £40 to £450, with brands such as Revolution (£37.50, Boots.com) sitting at the lower end, and luxury perfumers like Byredo in the premium price category. More typically, the core beauty advent calendars (from Boots to Harrods) cost between £100 and £285 – though I’d argue you don’t need to spend more than £250 to take home a seriously spectacular haul.

What is the cheapest beauty advent calendar?

While there are calendars from make-up brands such as W7 (approximately £24) that offer beauty advent calendars below £30, I’d recommend looking to the likes of Revolution (£37.50, Boots.com), Soap and Glory (£43.20, Boots.com) and Boots x Macmillan (£44, Boots.com) for more exciting yet affordable products.

For instance, W7 mimics packaging from Charlotte Tilbury and Estee Lauder products – to name a few – but doesn’t *actually* replicate the formula. However the Boots x Macmillan calendar boasts best-selling brands including Liz Earle and No7. After all, if your calendar costs less but you never use the products within, have you really saved money?

Why you can trust IndyBest reviews

As a senior shopping writer, this will be Lucy Smith’s third year reviewing the best beauty advent calendars for IndyBest. Prior to her professional coverage, Lucy has been purchasing beauty advents from M&S, The White Company and more since 2015, putting her experience in the category at more than 10 years. Elsewhere, Lucy covers the latest beauty launches year round, such as the Dyson supersonic travel dryer, so she knows which products and brands are worth looking out for in 2026. Plus, having reviewed everything from the best foundations to the best hyaluronic acid, she’s well versed in the brands that pop (and the ones that flop).

This is a constantly updated 2026 beauty advent calendar guide, and Lucy will be keeping it under review throughout the advent calendar season rather than treating it as a one-off roundup. That means monitoring prices, contents and overall value, as well as launch dates, pre-orders, waitlists, stock updates, product reveals, sell-outs and restocks. As calendars continue to launch and retailers reveal more of what’s behind the doors, this guide will be updated with the latest information to help you decide which beauty advent calendars are actually worth your money.

News.title: Russell Brand detectives receive string of new allegations in wake of rape and sexual assault conviction
News.content:
