Read our Privacy notice

Detectives investigating disgraced comedian Russell Brand have received a string of fresh allegations after he was found guilty of rape and sexual assaults.

The force has confirmed officers are assessing information from “several people” who came forward either during the star’s four-week trial or since he was convicted last week.

The 51-year-old was on Monday jailed for ten and half years for raping a fan and sexually assaulting three women at the height of his showbiz career from 2004 to 2009.

“Several people have contacted the investigation team during and since the trial to provide information or report a potential criminal allegation,” a Met spokesperson said. “Detectives are assessing this information as part of their ongoing enquiries.”

The fresh reports are on top of two further rape allegations, including against a 16-year-old schoolgirl, which are currently being reviewed by the Crown Prosecution Service. A charging decision could be announced within weeks, according to reports.

open image in gallery Russell Brand showed no emotion as he received his sentence ( Elizabeth Cook/PA )

His ex-partner Jemima Goldsmith also accused Brand of “violence, coercive control and abuse” against her when they dated around 2014 in a social media post last night.

Detective superintendent Andy Furphy, who led a three-year probe into the former Hollywood actor, previously warned his investigation remains ongoing and there is a “distinct possibility” more women will come forward in light of his conviction.

He has repeatedly encouraged any survivors of rape and sexual abuse to contact his team.

Met Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley also said he would not be surprised if “many more” accusers came forward following the high-profile trial.

Brand stared straight ahead, blinking in disbelief, as he was told he will serve at least two third of his of his sentence in jail at Southwark Crown Court yesterday by Mr Justice Bennathan, who accused the star of showing a “casual, arrogant disregard for any woman’s right to say no”.

open image in gallery Jemima Goldsmith used to date Russell Brand ( AFP/Getty )

However Brand’s wellness company is trying to cash-in on his incarceration by selling “free Russell” t-shirts.

Reborn, the comedian’s US-based alternative healthcare business, is advertising the $34.99 t-shirts emblazoned with the comic’s face on its website, which reads: “Stand with Russell against injustice. Silenced for speaking out.”

A message from Brand on the Reborn website, which also sells products including methylene blue tincture and adaptogenic mushroom super coffee, boasts that the firm is “my answer to a world that wants you sick, numb, and quiet”.

“They've tried to shut me up, shut me down, and squeeze me off every platform—but this is where we fight back,” the message adds. “Every bottle is about spiritual and physical resilience, and it's your direct way to stand with me and keep this mission alive.”

In recent years, the Essex-born convicted rapist moved to Florida’s Gulf coast and has used his social media channels to espouse anti-establishment rhetoric and conspiracy theories.

More follows on this developing news story...

News.title: Hand sanitiser or tinned meat? Demand surges for stockpiling essentials after UK government campaign
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A government drive urging households to stock up for emergencies coincided with a jump in sales of essentials last month, as grocery price inflation edged up again.

Figures from Worldpanel by Numerator show supermarket prices are now 2.6 per cent higher than a year ago, an increase from 2.5 per cent in September.

The latest data shows hand sanitiser sales climbed 83 per cent in the 10 days after its launch compared with the same period last year.

Bottled water sales rose 67 per cent over the same window, while tinned and jarred goods were up 37 per cent.

The number of people buying tinned meat each day after the launch rose by 43 per cent, equivalent to an extra 400,000 shoppers a day. The typical amount bought remained at about 500g, suggesting households are gradually stocking their cupboards.

Meanwhile, tuna maker Princes said demand for goods including tinned fish, meat and vegetables had risen since the Be Ready campaign began in October.

Giuseppe Mastrolia, interim chief executive of Princes Group, said: “The increase in demand for our ambient food products following the UK government’s Be Ready campaign further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions.”

open image in gallery Sales of essential supplies jumped from 22 October as shoppers responded to the Be Ready public awareness campaign encouraging households to prepare for up to three days in the event of disruption to essential services ( Getty/iStock )

Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel, said: “While prices are rising at a slower rate than at the beginning of the year, the direction of travel has changed.

“Household budgets have already taken a hit after the latest increase to the energy price cap arrived with the cold weather in October, and shoppers will be keeping a close eye on prices at the tills this winter.”

Shoppers began responding to the Be Ready public awareness campaign from 22 October.

The campaign encourages households to prepare for up to three days in the event of disruption to essential services.

Mr McKevitt added: “Shoppers clearly took notice of the Be Ready campaign, but this wasn’t panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October.

“Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government’s checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do.”

Halloween also played its part in October's shopping baskets.

Sales of pumpkins were up 10 per cent year on year, while tubs of sugar confectionery rose 28 per cent compared to last year.

open image in gallery In the 10 days after the campaign was launched, sales of hand sanitiser increased by 83 per cent compared to the corresponding period last year, while sales of bottled water rose 67 per cent and tinned and jarred goods were up 37 per cent ( Getty/iStock )

Online-only grocer Ocado grew sales by 12.3 per cent over the 12 weeks to November 1, reaching a record market share of 2.3 per cent.

Marks & Spencer, which part owns the Ocado retail business, separately increased grocery sales through its stores over the same period by 14.6 per cent.

Lidl lifted spending through the tills by 6.6 per cent, resulting in a market share gain of 0.4 percentage points, the greatest of any retailer.

That handed it 8.6 per cent of all sales.

Waitrose was the third retailer to increase share compared with last year, moving up to 4.5 per cent from 4.4 per cent as sales rose by 2.2 per cent.

Morrisons delivered market share of 8.3 per cent as its sales rose by 2 per cent, slightly ahead of the market.

Tesco and Sainsbury's took a 27.8 per cent and 15.5 per cent share respectively.

New Asda chief executive David Potts started his role with a market share of 11.3 per cent, as more than half of households shopped in its stores or online over the last three months.

Aldi, Britain's fourth largest grocer, saw sales up by 0.4 per cent, taking its share to 10.4 per cent.

Co-op's sales were 0.7 per cent higher than a year ago, giving it 5.3 per cent of the market.

News.title: Police officer dies after backpack explodes at scene of Spain shooting
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Spanish police officer was killed and another was seriously injured after a backpack containing an explosive device detonated as they responded to a shooting, local authorities said.

The officers had been responding to a violent dispute between two families on Tuesday, during which a young woman was shot and injured by a man on the outskirts ‌of Oviedo at around 7:30am, local authorities said.

The device exploded at around 8:30am, killing Juan José of the National Police’s canine unit, and leaving a bomb disposal officer in a very serious condition after losing a leg, police union ‌JUPOL said in a statement.

open image in gallery The explosion occurred at around 8:40am in the morning ( X/@mioviedo_ )

A three-year-old German shepherd who was being handled by Mr José, called Deny, was also killed in the explosion.

The JUPOL union said that upon ‌arriving at the scene of ​the shooting on Rafael Urrusti Street outskirts ‌of Oviedo, police ⁠found a backpack at the building's ⁠entrance containing the explosive device.

It detonated as ‌officers took ​it away from ‌the building to ​defuse it.

Police forces and political figures, including Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez, have paid tribute to Mr José, Deny and the injured officer.

“Deeply shocked by the death of a National Police officer in Oviedo. There are no words to ease the pain of his family and colleagues,” Mr Sanchez wrote on X.

open image in gallery Deny, a three-year-old German shepherd, was also killed in the explosion ( Policia Nacional )

“All my love to them and all my strength to the seriously injured officer. Your dedication and courage deserve the gratitude of an entire country.”

Spain’s Guardia Civil said it was “deeply saddened by the death in the line of duty of Juan José” and offered its “heartfelt love and support” to his family.

The Policia Nacional said it was “saddened” by his death and wished a “speedy recovery” to the injured officer.

The area has now been cordoned off as National Police deploy a large operation to find the suspect.

The EFE news agency reports that Alfredo Canteli, the mayor of Oviedo, is heading now to the scene to gather information on what happened.

Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the Spanish opposition leader and president of the People’s Party, said in a post on X: "What happened in Oviedo is heartbreaking.

"My condolences to the family of the officer who died and my best wishes for the recovery of the one who was seriously injured."

UME, a unit of the Spanish armed forces that provides disaster relief throughout Spain and abroad, said: “On behalf of the #UME, we extend our deepest condolences to Juan José’s family, friends and colleagues.

“We also send all our strength to the injured TEDAX-NRBQ agent and wish him a speedy recovery.”

News.title: Donald Trump delivers ultimate snub to UN by making US first country to totally boycott human rights review
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The United States is expected to become the first country on Tuesday to refuse, in full, a scheduled examination of its human rights record by the U.N.'s top rights body since that body was created two decades ago.

The Geneva-based council examines the rights records of all 193 U.N. member states, generally about every four to five years, through a process known as the universal periodic review.

Under Donald Trump, the United States already skipped its review appointment a year ago. The scheduled November 2025 review was pushed back until Tuesday in hopes that the U.S. government might change its mind.

It did not.

open image in gallery The United States is to become the first country to skip a regular review of its human rights record at the U.N.'s Human Rights Council ( Reuters )

The Trump administration pulled the U.S. out of the Human Rights Council last year, accusing it of an anti-U.S. and anti-Israel bias, and alleging that it didn't uphold the very values it promotes.

“(W)e give no credibility to the agency,” a State Department spokesperson said in an email to The Associated Press.

“This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own ‘values’ as it pushes anti-American rhetoric,” the spokesperson said, alleging the council's “persistent failure to condemn the most egregious human rights violators.”

The council says the process requires participation from the country in question, and that if no national representatives are present, the review cannot go forward. As part of such reviews, national delegations, which at times can include a dozen officials or more, make a presentation, face questions and hear recommendations from other national envoys.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump said the war in Iran could end ‘fairly soon’ ( PA Wire )

It's supposed to be a sweeping and constructive process, akin to holding up a mirror to governments to improve their human rights policies.

Supporters back the council's mandate to keep tabs on human rights in all U.N. member states, including the U.S., which has drawn criticism for its policies, including strong-arm deportations and targeted killings of alleged drug-runners in the Caribbean and Pacific – which the administration has said are designed to protect U.S. workers and help keep the country safe.

Critics of the U.S. snub warn that the walkout could encourage other countries, many of which bristle about intense scrutiny from human rights monitors, to follow suit.

Jamil Dakwar, director of the American Civil Liberties Union's human rights program, said: “The administration is saying to the world, ‘we don’t care about whether you would review us or not, we’re going to continue to violate human rights unabashed’."

open image in gallery Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has consistently defended the Trump administration’s foreign policy ( AP )

"And we are saying: ‘No, enough is enough. This council should hold the United States accountable,” he told reporters Monday in Geneva, as part of a push by civil society to raise awareness about the U.S. rights record.

He said the ACLU and allies have called on the U.N. human rights chief to respond by presenting an update on rights in the United States early next year. Eric Tistounet, a visiting professor at the Geneva Graduate Institute who was the council's first secretary, said the U.S. walkout could affect the credibility of the council's review system.

“If the predominant global power — which has always claimed to adhere to the human rights norms — doesn’t show up and doesn’t even justify why, then you are in big trouble," he said.

News.title: Deputy Labour leader defends Ed Miliband appearing on Russell Brand's YouTube show
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Labour’s deputy leader said Ed Miliband’s interview with Russell Brand took place in a “different era” before the disgraced comedian’s predatory sexual behaviour had been exposed.

Mr Miliband, then the Labour leader, appeared on Brand’s online show The Trews as part of an attempt to win over young voters in his ultimately doomed attempt to become prime minister ahead of the 2015 general election.

Lucy Powell, who was vice chairwoman of Labour’s election campaign in 2015, said Brand had a “powerful platform”, and insisted Brand had approached Labour first as she faced questions over what role she played in setting up the appearance.

The Education Secretary told Sky News: “It was a long time ago, obviously and had I or Ed Miliband or anybody at the time had any sense at all that this was someone who was a sexual predator, who was involved in these sorts of crimes.”

She added: “I think like anybody who would have paid to go to his show, would have watched him on TV, who was his employer at the time, who had interactions with him – anybody, including those of us who were involved in that at the time – would look back and really regret that, knowing today what we now know.”

open image in gallery Ed Miliband, then the Labour leader, appeared on Brand’s online show The Trews as part of an attempt to win over young voters ahead of 2015 general election ( Russell Brand/YouTube )

By the time the interview took place, Brand had already lost his BBC Radio 2 show for leaving a series of lewd messages on actor Andrew Sachs’ answerphone about a romantic liaison with his granddaughter, been fired from XFM for reading pornography on air and detailed his womanising in his autobiography.

Asked about her role in setting up the interview, Ms Powell said: “Look, we were in very different times. We weren’t in the social media age at the time, so where you could maybe search things up and see allegations or things about somebody at the time.

“And, as I say, if there was any suggestion at all, we were dealing with someone who was a known sexual predator at the time then, of course, no one would have done that.

“But as I say, he was a wellknown public figure. Lots of people, from Hollywood to the BBC to many others, gave this person a very, very powerful platform.

“We didn’t know at the time and unfortunately, maybe had people come forward or felt able to… it was a different era.”

open image in gallery Russell Brand, 51, was jailed for 10-and-a-half years on Monday for raping one of his fans and sexually assaulting three TV and radio workers during his rise to international fame ( PA Wire )

Brand, 51, was jailed for 10-and-a-half years on Monday for raping one of his fans and sexually assaulting three TV and radio workers during his rise to international fame.

Ms Powell said: “What I would say to women now, off the back of that, is do come forward when these things happen to you.

“You will be supported. You will be believed. You will be taken seriously.

“Because actually, had we had an environment and a culture, 15 years ago, 20 years ago, where women felt that, then he would have been stopped in his tracks sooner and we would have had less victims as a consequence.”

In 2023, Mr Miliband said he agreed to the interview to encourage people to vote, but knowing what he did now, he "wouldn't have done that interview, and I regret doing it".

When asked at Politico’s Energy and Climate UK event whether he regretted the interview following the publication of allegations against Brand, said: “Yes, of course. I think the allegations that have come to light are horrific and my solidarity is with the women who have come forward to tell their stories.

“I did lots of interviews during that campaign. Russell Brand was going round saying people shouldn’t vote.

“I went and did an interview on his programme because I wanted young people to get out and vote.

“But obviously knowing what I know now, obviously I regret doing it.”

News.title: Ukraine strikes elite Russian ‘Rubicon’ drone unit in occupied territory
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ukrainian forces have struck Russia’s elite Rubicon drone unit overnight, Kyiv’s military said hours before peace talks got underway with Moscow in Abu Dhabi.

The Rubicon Center for Advanced Unmanned Technologies was formed in August 2024 by the Russian ministry of defence and is a sprawling unit operating in the heart of occupied territory.

Its key aims include hunting down Ukrainian drone teams on the ground and intercepting reconnaissance and strike drones. It serves as the heart of Russian drone missions against Ukraine.

According to a statement by Ukraine’s southern defence released on Monday, the Rubicon unit was hit in the occupied region of Berdiansk, Zaporizhzhia.

“The enemy facility was located 107 kilometres away from the line of contact,” read the statement on Telegram.

open image in gallery The facility was located 107 km away from the line of contact, according to the military ( Ukraine southern defence )

“The operation proves once again: there is no longer a safe rear for the Russian occupiers,” it continued.

“The defence forces of Ukraine are capable of detecting and striking enemy targets at a significant distance from the front line, acting in coordination and according to a single plan.”

Russia is reported to have “lost trained specialists who were engaged in training operators and passed on their experience to others”.

The operation is said to have been carried out through a joint effort involving Ukraine’s Harpy group and the unmanned aerial systems battery of the Pivden Operational Grouping of Troops, with support from Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service, the SBU’s Special Operations Centre and the 412th Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment.

Russia pulled Rubicon units from the front line in northern Donetsk back in September after suffering heavy losses during Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi, according to the Kyiv Independent.

open image in gallery Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet with Russian and Ukrainian representatives on Tuesday ( Reuters )

The news comes as US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to be picking up again this week after months of deadlock following the US-Israeli war against Iran.

Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to be mediating between the two warring sides.

Russian state news agency RIA reported the start of what is scheduled to be two days of talks, in which Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are to mediate between the two warring sides.

On the eve of the start of discussions Trump said that Washington was seeing a “very strong inclination” towards ending the war and said that both sides were “tired of fighting”.

Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that Russian forces were suffering “record losses”.

“Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine's negotiating position,” he said in his nightly address on Minday,

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

Sports.title: How Carrick’s Man Utd reign fell apart from slipping standards to petty backstabbing as proud 148-year record falls
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK was sitting at the front of the aircraft and on his own, scrutinising his tactics on a notepad, during Manchester United’s flight back from Como.

Someone on board said the atmosphere was so funereal that “you could hear a pindrop”. The mood on the outbound flight had been buoyant.



United players did not say a word on their return to Manchester after the 4-1 thumping. They still got stuck into their in-flight meal.

They had not got stuck in during the game. United players went into hiding in Como and it continued when they slunk into their vehicles at Manchester Airport.



At half-past midnight, several players pulled their sun visors down to conceal their faces from the waiting photographers.

Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes, the squad’s three most senior outfield players in Italy, all hid.

One player’s vehicle seemed to inch out so carefully to deny snappers a clear shot of Fernandes. Fernandes shot from the hip that night but didn’t manage one at the actual goal.

Chief executive Omar Berrada plonked himself in a rear-facing seat in his carrier. Director of football Jason Wilcox hid behind a seat.

Carrick did not avoid eye contact when he got behind the wheel of his Range Rover. He was at the wheel, but not for much longer.

When Carrick drove back into Carrington the day after the Bournemouth drubbing to watch the under 21s two weeks ago, he was not smuggled in, unlike a former teammate on the eve of a transfer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Carrick fronted up in every sense and will leave United with his dignity intact. He was applauded more fervently on his farewell tour than at his 2017 testimonial or a trophy presentation.

The Bournemouth surrender was the most toxic atmosphere ever witnessed at Old Trafford. As unedifying and sinister as much of it was, matchgoers levelled the blame squarely at those on the pitch and those in the directors’ box.

United supporters have repeatedly dubbed the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe “c***s” and Wilcox a “w****r”. A bedsheet on display against Aston Villa on Sunday also targeted Berrada.

They have told Ratcliffe to stick his new stadium up his backside. They reworked the ‘Build a Bonfire’ chant about Liverpool and Manchester City, replaced by the Glazers and Ratcliffe.

United supporters booed Berrada as he left Old Trafford after the Bournemouth debacle. A concerned steward rounded on an abusive fan, emphasising Berrada was accompanied by his family.



One senior player was astonished by the level of performances against Como and Bournemouth. The bewildered description from another during that nine-match winless run was “strange”.

Carrick is not short of sympathy. He exchanged heart-to-heart messages with former United managers Sir Alex Ferguson and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Jose Mourinho, who added Carrick to his coaching staff in 2018, is saddened by United’s recent demise.

“Our Man Utd,” a crestfallen former fan favourite messaged. “F**k. S**t.”



Carrick still managed to instill a belief in the majority of players. There was a bullishness heading into the away game at Chelsea on Halloween and United’s first half performance was encouraging, only there was no goal. They then conceded two inside the first 20 minutes of the second half.

As usual, the players and the executives survive the manager. Wilcox has mimicked Ed Woodward by promoting a former player from temporary manager to permanent. Ratclffe insisted he would not have “tolerated” Woodward. Wilcox’s position should be untenable.

At Ruben Amorim’s penultimate match in charge against Wolves last December, a senior United official confided in a friend how calmer the club was and that the chaos of the past was behind them.



Six days later, Amorim was gone. Carrick’s removal means this is the first time in United’s 148-year history that they will sack two permanent managers in the same calendar year.

Towards the end, Carrick became punchier in press conferences until the aftermath of the Bournemouth nadir. Then the air was one of resignation.

Carrick’s wife, Lisa, did not go into hiding, either. She was out in Alderley Edge the morning after the Como catastrophe and an onlooker said “she seemed happy enough”. She continued to attend games at Old Trafford.

Her husband dug in and gave a stirring monologue that lasted six minutes between the Como and Bournemouth games. Carrick looked journalists in the eye and then fielded questions for 15 minutes.

During Carrick’s address, it was impossible not to wonder why he was the one who felt compelled to say something. Wilcox says less than a mute. The aloof Berrada has a couple of favourite conduits.



The sense of crisis that has engulfed United was apparent at the Football Writers’ Association’s north west dinner in Manchester hours after the Bournemouth loss. United staff that had planned to attend withdrew between the Como and Bournemouth batterings.

Carrick’s agent, Jo Tongue, was in the Old Trafford directors’ box for the Bournemouth match but did not stay in Manchester overnight. That was an early hint that his defenestration was not imminent.

A staff member close to the first team made light of the club’s resistance to dismissing Carrick, sarcastically quoting United’s “business as usual” mantra.



Astonishingly, the same staff member quoted Amorim when they predicted a storm ahead of what would be Carrick’s last match in the dugout.

One of the United buses that arrived at Como’s Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium was not allowed to follow the first coach that ferried the squad into the ground. It had to pull into a dead end. How apt.

Seven months before Carrick entered United’s new £50million building at Carrington, he told this correspondent that his 11-day caretaker stint at the club in 2021 “didn’t really feel like such a big step or a big difference.

“I was used to being at the club for so long, and you get used to it once you’re there and once you’ve seen it.

“Being so close to Ole, it felt natural. It wasn’t anything too much and it felt quite comfortable doing the job.”



Carrick’s friend and former colleague Solskjaer was considered a soft touch by the majority of the United dressing room and that rubbed off on Carrick. United’s working environment became too lax amid an increased workload and there was mixed messaging over the infamous running stats as recently as three weeks ago.

Under Carrick, players almost always had a day off after a matchday. Under Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, the day after a match was a designated recovery day at Carrington.

The switch barely affected United in Carrick’s first four months in charge, mainly as they hardly had any midweek matches. But their running figures have plummeted and the injury toll has shot up.



Carrick, like Ten Hag, did not bring his own fitness coach with him. Amorim, Mourinho and Louis van Gaal did.

Insiders revealed that Fernandes played through the pain barrier to “miraculously” recover to start in Premier League games in September. It begged the question as to why Carrick gave Fernandes 90 minutes in the Champions League opener against Sabah, when United were 3-0 up at half-time, three days before the Manchester derby.

Perhaps it accounted for Fernandes’ worsening body language. In his final appearances under Carrick, Fernandes was injury-free but often playing walking football and he appeared to down tools in the hammering by Como.

Fernandes was benched for the surrender against Bournemouth – a “pure football” decision according to Carrick – and did not warm up until the 58th minute. Fernandes then reported at Carrington the following day – a day off – for treatment. More questions.

Youri Tielemans’ revelation that he was instructed to “chill” at United’s training camp in Ireland came back to haunt Carrick. United were scheduled to hold an open session at Carton House yet that was scrapped, with no specific explanation.



One player who made the trip half-joked that he was at least present for the round of golf. An innocuous comment at the time, it now gives the impression that United were too laid back.



The flies started dropping in the first weeks of the season. Two of United’s four summer signings arrived with injuries. Come Como, United were without eight players through injury or illness.

Supporters saw how lax players were yards away from them. One season-ticket holder who sits in the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand closely observed a player’s warm-up: “He stood for seven minutes with his hands on his hips watching the game. He barely moved.

“He did two ten-yard sprints and then got called on.”

One player has a penchant for heading into his local village for rich brunches and then stopping off at a nearby coffee shop for a large caffeine fix, occasionally accompanied by a sweet treat.

Another United player was spotted on a night out in the early hours of the morning that United were playing. A teammate also had a habit of enjoying stays in London close to games.



Some of the squad backstabbing was petty, with the representatives of one long-serving player briefing against his rival for the same position.

This all undermines the best-in-class high-performance mantras Ineos swear by. United claimed their £50million hub at Carrington that opened last year had medical facilities to rival any other Premier League club.

Yet they took an age to detect the severity of Sesko’s injury even though he last played more than five weeks ago. “Best in class, you’re having a laugh,” the Stretford End sang.



Shaw, starter of all 38 Premier League games last season, regressed and has missed more matches than he played in. High-ranking United figures privately rued the failure to sign Newcastle left back Lewis Hall.

Carrick should have been more selfish. Rather than fit square pegs Ayden Heaven, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui into a round hole at left back, play Harry Amass, an actual left back. Amass has made the bench once in the Premier League and has changed representatives twice already this season to secure a transfer in the new year.

It would have been sink or swim for a 19-year-old. If Amass sank, Carrick could have reminded everyone that the board settled with one out-and-out senior left back at the end of the transfer window.

But that is not the compliant Carrick’s style. He privately expressed sympathy with Shaw when they were teammates when he witnessed Mourinho’s tough love.

When Carrick was in Mourinho’s shoes, he was more Solskjaer than Mourinho. “Jose was his own man and he knew how to win big games,” Carrick told this correspondent last year. “That was his biggest asset.”



Carrick was true to his character but it heavily contributed to his undoing as his unwillingness to show a firmer side allowed complacency to spread.

The promotion of the Fletcher twins caused resentment among some academy talents and the siblings were subjected to nasty online abuse. One youth teamer’s parent has been particularly scathing about the pair.

Carrick’s aversion to confrontation led to his downfall at Middlesbrough, where some players noticed he would not look them in the eye when he decided to drop them.



They realised that Carrick would wait until they had exited the club’s gymnasium on their own so he could tell them one-to-one and avoid informing them of team news in a group environment.

A couple of players deliberately ended their gym sessions simultaneously to try and surprise the waiting Carrick. It was then that they noticed the lack of eye contact.

Those who know Carrick say he can be sensitive to criticism. There were flickers of it when his record at Middlesbrough was brought up during a press conference and accusations of a lack of “passion”.

Carrick’s own ghostwriter, Henry Winter, noticeably began to question his game management.

When this reporter interviewed Carrick at the start of his coaching stint under Mourinho, it was the day after a League Cup loss to Derby County in a penalty shootout. That was gazumped by Mourinho stripping Paul Pogba of the second captain’s status.



During the interview, Carrick looked frazzled and did not have the energy to defuse the ticking timebomb. Those six months alongside Mourinho have clearly informed Carrick’s style.

United’s crisis was effectively sparked by a 15-year-old. United had promised JJ Gabriel he would be in the squad for the League Cup defeat to Brighton, which raised the question as to whether Carrick had a selection foisted onto him.

Carrick insisted a “concrete” call on Gabriel had not been made, which contradicted the club’s briefing.



In happier times, Carrick retreated to the golf course with his coaching staff. A member once spotted Carrick at his local club nursing a drink.

United were homing in on Champions League qualification at the time and the sparse midweeks afforded Carrick and his coaches time for 18 holes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

When the fan asked for directions to the clubhouse, Carrick did not utter a word. His more outgoing assistant Jonathan Woodgate broke the silence.

Carrick can scribble on a scorecard rather than a tactics notebook now.

NOT even Florian Wirtz’s (£4.8m) loudest cheerleaders would claim he’s been at his best this season.

But the Germany international’s numbers suggest he’s been better than his critics would have people believe.

Wirtz’s doubters bemoan his lack of output but no Dream Team player has registered more assists across at this stage of the campaign.



MOST ASSISTS AMONG DREAM TEAM PLAYERS THIS SEASON



6 – Florian Wirtz

6 – Evanilson

6 – Pascal Gross

6 – Cody Gakpo

6 – Iliman Ndiaye

5 – Alysson

5 – Jaidon Anthony

5 – Matheus Cunha

5 – Charalampos Kostoulas

5 – John McGinn

5 – Declan Rice

5 – Morgan Rogers

It’s worth noting that Dream Team incorporates Opta-defined ‘fantasy assists’ which makes for a more generous process but this applies to all players, not just Wirtz.

The 23-year-old ranks joint-fourth in the top flight for chances created but stacks up less favourably when the quality of chances is taken into account.

He has created just three big chances in all competitions; Pascal Gross (£3.6m) leads the metric with 10, closely followed by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (£4.1m) and Granit Xhaka (£3.5m) on nine each — the latter pair have been let down by their team-mates’ wastefulness so far.



Wirtz has been rendered ineffective too often for some fans’ liking but it’s a measure of his talent that he has notched eight goal involvements (two goals, six assists) over the first 10 Gameweeks at half capacity.

Most recently, he took advantage of a favourable fixture last weekend in the form of a trip to Crystal Palace.

The Reds didn’t have it all their own way and were indebted to an in-form Alisson (£4.4m) but took the lead through an Alexis Mac Allister (£3.9m) header fives minutes before half-time.



Wirtz doubled the visitors’ lead within 10 minutes of the restart with a composed finish after some good work from Bradley Barcola (£4.5m) down the right flank.

The former Bayer Leverkusen playmaker then turned creator with a selfless lay-off for Alexander Isak (£6.5m) in the 89th minute.

When all was said and done at Selhurst Park, Wirtz received 14 points for his efforts, his best single-game haul of 2026/27.

Aston Villa’s Alysson (£2.7m) was the only midfielder to add more points to his total in Gameweek 10 — the Brazilian winger claimed 16 points during the farcical 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.



Dream Team managers are spoiled for choice in midfield at the minute and Wirtz’s overall tally of 76 points, while respectable, isn’t likely to convince many.

That being said, Liverpool’s Gameweek 11 double header of 18th-placed Manchester United (h) and Club Brugge (a) is a favourable one on paper.

Wirtz is due a price increase after his 14-point return and so some gaffers may feel he’s a viable a roll of the dice as he could always be sold for a tidy profit ahead of Gameweek 12, when all 20 Premier League clubs will play twice.

Liverpool’s No7 features in 4% of teams at the time of writing.

Sports.title: England call up James Hill for first time with Arsenal star Ezri Konsa ruled OUT of Croatia clash
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND boss Thomas Tuchel has added Bournemouth defender James Hill to his England squad.

Arsenal‘s Ezri Konsa will not face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday as he recovers from injury, but is set to return to full training later in the week.



Hill, 24, will give Tuchel another option at the back for the Nations League game, as well as Sunday’s clash with Spain.

Konsa picked up a knock in Arsenal’s Champions League victory over Slavia Prague, but Gunners chief Mikel Arteta didn’t seem too concerned.



He said: “He’s fine – he was feeling much better today. We took him out on Wednesday for a precaution, but yesterday and today he’s been feeling good.”

Arsenal also have Ben White, Eberechi Eze, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Declan Rice in the group and their manager is delighted to have a strong English presence at his club.

He said: “It’s a proud thing to have a big English core in the national team from our club. It’s something that is part of our identity.

“Not only the number, but as well the players that represent us and the national team. They are super happy to be back, you can see that.”

The Three Lions are struggling at the heart of defence after Marc Guehi pulled out of the squad through injury.

Dan Burn was called up as his replacement, joining Jarrad Branthwaite, Konsa and Jarell Quansah.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Lewis Hall, Djed Spence, Lewis-Skelly and White are also available at the back.

White could fill in at centre-back, but has been featuring on the flanks with Arsenal.

The 29-year-old was booed by supporters in the friendlies against both Uruguay and Japan after a self-imposed exile, and took the chance to defend himself after his call-up.

He said: “It’s something I haven’t spoken about and I won’t go into detail about it but it’s a decision that I don’t want to talk about anyone in a negative way.



“It wasn’t an ideal situation but it’s probably one I would make again. Obviously, it’s amazing to be here in a fresh moment ahead of the two amazing games.

“There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn’t great. I don’t want to throw anyone under the bus. A lot of people tried to do that to me so it’s something I wouldn’t want to do myself.

“I don’t think I am looking to win anyone over or say anything that helps them get back on my side. It is what it is. There are reasons for it and I am just looking forward to playing for England and doing well and looking for success.”

MLS star Jacob Shaffleburg has suffered serious injuries after being on the end of a nasty tackle.

The Los Angeles FC winger was victim of a very late challenge leaving him with a collapsed lung and several rib fractures.



As Shaffleburg recovered from one very late challenge, 6ft 6in Jackson Ragen flew in like a steam train, smashing the winger off the pitch.

The blatant foul, which only earnt a yellow card, was certainly felt by the 5ft 11in winger, who weighs roughly 18kg less than Ragen.

It seems very unlikely that the 26-year-old winger will be involved in the upcoming MLS play-offs.

MANCHESTER UNITED will have to splash the cash if they want to bring Mauricio Pochettino to Old Trafford.

The club are reportedly set for a change of direction after Michael Carrick‘s nightmare start to the season has left them in the relegation zone going into the November international break.



Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte are among the names that have been suggested as a potential replacement for the United legend.

But Pochettino seems to be the front-runner, despite signing a contract extension with the US national team over the summer.



Now The Athletic have revealed that deal included a buyout clause which could allow United to secure his services – if they are ready to pay up.

The outlet report that the Argentine’s clause is in the region of $10million (£7.5m).



But that number would likely balloon even more in the event of Poch getting the job, as United would have to fork out millions more for his long-time assistants.

Some of the sting will be taken out of that figure by the fact that Carrick’s deal includes a money-saving measure that United can trigger.

The ex-England man’s contract reportedly includes a one-year break clause that means the club won’t have to take the usual massive financial hit which sacking a new manager entails.

SunSport revealed on Monday that former Spurs boss Pochettino, 54, is open to a move to United despite their dire situation.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The Red Devils have approached Pochettino before, having tested the waters for him in 2021 before being blocked by Paris Saint-Germain.

He was under consideration again the following year, but the club decided to go with Dutchman Erik ten Hag.

He most recently led the US to the World Cup Round of 16, where they were dumped out by Belgium in a 4-1 thrashing.

Sports.title: Why has Tom Brady quit Birmingham City?
Sports.content:
Next

TOM Brady stepped down from his minority ownership role after three years at Birmingham City on November 9, 2026.

With the Blues currently sitting at the top of the Championship, it brings an unexpected end to The NFL legend’s involvement at St Andrew’s.



Why has Tom Brady quit Birmingham City?

Birmingham have confirmed Tom Brady’s exit but have not publicly explained the decision.

However, he was reportedly struggling to balance his commitments at the club with his work as an NFL pundit.



According to the Telegraph, Brady sold his shares and left the club’s advisory board, believing it was the right time to move on.

He currently works as an analyst for Fox Sports, while also holding stakes in the NFL’s Las Vegas Raiders and WNBA’s Las Vegas Aces.

On November 9, the Blues released the following statement on X: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the Club over the last three years.

“It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the Club, and the Club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.”

When did Tom Brady buy into Birmingham City?

The seven-time Super Bowl winner, 49, became a minority shareholder in August 2023, following the takeover by Knighthead Capital Management, led by American businessman Tom Wagner.

The former quarterback acquired a 3.3% stake and was appointed chairman of an advisory board.



Brady was a big part of the hedge fund’s ambition to deliver Champions League football to the club and was even involved in transfer discussions.

His role also included improving performance behind the scenes, with a particular focus on nutrition, fitness, player recovery and the club’s academy teams.

At the time, Wagner described the arrival of the seven-time champion as “a statement of intent”.

Brady had retired from American football earlier that year after winning six Super Bowls with the New England Patriots and another with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

His involvement later featured in the Amazon Prime Video docuseries Built In Birmingham: Brady & The Blues, which charted the club’s attempts to rebuild and was released in August 2025.



What happened at Birmingham City during Tom Brady’s time at the club?

Brady’s three years with Birmingham City were anything but straightforward.

In October 2023, the club sacked John Eustace while sitting sixth in the Championship, replacing him with Wayne Rooney.

But the former England captain lasted just 83 days before being dismissed, and the Blues were relegated to League One at the end of the season.

Brady later attracted criticism when the Amazon documentary showed him questioning Rooney’s work ethic and describing players as “lazy and entitled”.

Rooney called the criticism “very unfair”.



Under Chris Davies, Birmingham secured promotion straight back to the Championship as League One champions in 2025, finishing with an EFL-record 111 points.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Blues now lead the second tier on goal difference, level with Middlesbrough and Stoke on 29 points after 15 matches.

They moved top following a 2-1 home victory over Swansea on November 7, just two days before Brady’s departure was announced.

Sports.title: How Man Utd could line up under Mauricio Pochettino with Harry Kane and Cole Palmer spearheading new-look XI
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO has emerged as a serious contender to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.

And the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss, 54, could bring sweeping changes to Old Trafford.



On Monday evening it emerged that Carrick is set to be sacked following a dismal start to the season.

The Red Devils entered the international break 18th in the Premier League table following just one win from ten games.



Pochettino – who SunSport revealed is open to the Man Utd job – has a proven track record of picking up teams from low ebbs and improving them, having followed Tim Sherwood at Spurs and Graham Potter at Chelsea.

As speculation surrounding the Argentine intensifies, let’s take a look at what he could theoretically do at United.



Senne Lammens has had a shaky start to the season but will likely be given a chance to improve under a new boss.

Man Utd have long admired Newcastle full-back Lewis Hall and could finally get the move done under Pochettino.

Hall actually left Chelsea under Pochettino’s watch, but the boss did later claim that he had a “good future” ahead of him.

The left-back’s arrival would allow current boo boy Diogo Dalot to actually move to his favoured position on the right, although Noussair Mazraoui is also an option.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Lisandro Martinez could enjoy a redemption arc under compatriot Pochettino.

And he could be partnered by Marquinhos, who played under Poch at PSG and could look to emulate his former partner Thiago Silva’s stint at Chelsea.

Kobbie Mainoo would likely be empowered to shine under Pochettino, although the experienced boss would possibly not favour Youri Tielemans‘ languid style.

Andrey Santos may improve under Poch, while Carlos Baleba is popular with fans – although a major improvement for Manuel Ugarte may be possible.

The ex-Paris Saint-Germain star’s United stint has been a disaster thus far – although having been desperate to bring him to Chelsea in 2023, Pochettino may have an idea how to get the best out of him.



Bryan Mbeumo‘s goalscoring ability would surely be favoured on the right flank, while Pochettino has previously praised Marcus Rashford‘s game and the England star could be restored on the left.

Bruno Fernandes’ time with Man Utd appears to be winding towards its end.

The Portuguese star will require a splashy replacement, however, having provided such high output down the years.



A dream target would surely be Cole Palmer.

It may seem far-fetched, with the attacker having just extended his contract with Chelsea all the way to 2034.

But with United being his boyhood club, and having played the best football of his career under Pochettino, Palmer may feel inclined to push for the move.

Another player that could eventually reunite with Poch is Harry Kane.



The recent Ballon d’Or winner emerged as a superstar under Pochettino at Tottenham between 2014 and 2019.

Like Palmer, Kane has just signed a new contract – penning a two-year extension to 2029 with Bayern Munich.

So he wouldn’t come cheap, but the possibility of reuniting with Poch and having a chance to compete for honours, while also going for the all-time Prem goals record, may appeal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kane, 33, left Spurs in 2023 trailing Alan Shearer by 47 goals in the all-time Prem goals leaderboard.



Temptation to come back may grow if he manages to fulfil his dream of winning the Champions League with Bayern this term – and if United look like actually getting their act together.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson has been on 10-year charm offensive to land his dream Man Utd manager target
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED icon Alex Ferguson has reportedly been desperate for the club to appoint Mauricio Pochettino since his Tottenham days.

SunSport understands that the Argentine tactician has come close to the the Old Trafford job on numerous occasions since a lunch with Sir Alex in 2016.



With Michael Carrick on the brink of being dismissed during the international break, Pochettino once again finds himself making headlines.

Journalist and author Melissa Reddy detailed how United tried and failed to land him three times despite Fergie’s recommendation.



She claims the club “chickened out” of negotiations with Daniel Levy while Poch was at Tottenham, lost out to Paris Saint-Germain with a second attempt and refused to be patient during Ralf Rangnick‘s interim spell in 2022, with Erik ten Hag arriving instead.

Reddy added: “At every turn, United were in desperate need for someone who was proven at implementing an identity in the PL, creating a culture of excellence, maximising the tools at his disposal, fostering a family environment and trusting in youth but they fluffed their lines to go for an easier option. Which ended up being expensive mistake after expensive mistake.

“Sir Alex Ferguson has wanted Pochettino to be the manager at Old Trafford stretching back to his Spurs days – something he has repeatedly told the Argentine and mentioned at the club.

“Imagine if they had empowered Poch to build sustainable success back then instead of a break-glass option now when the club are in all kinds of tatters, especially off the pitch (Glazer debt & INEOS horrid decision-making), which informs everything on it.”

Fergie, who shares a great deal of mutual respect with Poch, may finally about to get his wish.

SunSport exclusively revealed that Pochettino would be open to making a Premier League return with United.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The ex-Spurs and Chelsea chief’s odds tumbled from 25-1 to 2-1 second favourite after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa saw United enter the international break in the relegation zone.

He agreed a new four-year deal after leading the USA to the World Cup last 16 on home soil, but admitted at the time that he may not finish the term.

He said: “Now we are thinking of spending four years with the USA but you can always break a contract, say you stop, and that’s it, you agree something.

“With a four-year contract, it’s different.



“We could lose Copa America or the Gold Cup, and they’re not happy with us, they can sack us, or we can say, ‘OK, it’s not in the way that we think’.”

The chance to rebuild things at Old Trafford could prove too good to turn down, especially after he spoke about the long-running links ahead of the World Cup.

Poch told Four Four Two: “United have always shown interest, but the ideal scenario to manage there has never quite materialised.”

Old Trafford chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada joined co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco with the managerial situation at the top of the agenda.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fans are growing impatient with protests taking place during the clashes with Villa and Roma at Old Trafford.



All signs point to a new man in the dugout for the clash with bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Sports.title: England Wheelchair rout Australia to reach World Cup final
Sports.content:
England Wheelchair scored a record points total against rival Australia to rout their opponents 86-18 and reach their fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final.

The game was all but over at half-time as England held a 40-6 lead, with Rob Hawkins leading the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance in his side's dominant victory.

The win means the defending World Cup champions will face France in the final in Wollongong on Friday, with a chance to claim their third World Cup title.

Image: Joe Coyd got in on the act in the first half

Mason Billington - who picked up Player of the Match - opened the scoring in just the third minute of the contest with a try, before Hawkins added two of his own and back Joe Coyd got in on the act to put England in firm control with a 30-0 lead after just 24 minutes.

Diab Karim eventually got the host nation on the scoresheet with a converted try, but their joy was short-lived after Billington went over twice to seal his hat-trick before half-time.

Interchanges Jack Brown and Nathan Collins scored three tries between them in the opening 10 minutes of the second half before Hawkins struck twice more to put England out of reach.

Karim and Dan Antsey went over for consolations just after the hour mark, but tries from Chris Haynes and the captain Lewis King put the finishing touches on a sensational victory for the two-time World Champions.

'I'm looking forward to Friday!'

Image: Nathan Collins (r) is congratulated by Billington on his try

England Wheelchair rugby league captain Lewis King:

I don't want to put a number on it but we are proud of that performance, we were super disciplined in how we wanted to play. We had a game plan and we executed it. I am super proud."

"I am grateful for the opportunity [to be captain] and I don't want to take putting this badge on as an opportunity because you don't know how many times you will get to do it.

"I am excited for the opportunity. The culture of this team is teammates we are like brothers. I am looking forward to Friday.

"When we meet France, it is always down to the finer details and margins, so I won't be thinking about France, we will be focused on us."

Sports.title: Tough-tackling Schlager proves his worth for Forest
Sports.content:
Xaver Schlager has been quietly impressive for Nottingham Forest this season but what was missing was that big moment. It came in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday when he dispossessed Elliot Anderson for Liam Delap's first goal.

The free transfer from Leipzig nipped in ahead of the £116m man that he has replaced in Forest's midfield and set Delap on the way to doubling the lead. Schlager is no Anderson but he has his own qualities and they made the difference at the weekend.

"It was a top team performance and it was a top performance by Xaver Schlager," said Forest boss Oliver Glasner in the press conference afterwards. He pointed out that "it must have been a fantastic performance" because City's midfielders are world-class.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the match between Nottingham Forest and Man City

Schlager was better. "He is so smart, anticipating and getting balls, one of the most for interceptions in the league. And he was physically so strong in his 50-50 balls. He always stayed on his feet and won these balls, because he can then play forward."

In fact, despite only coming on as a late substitute in Forest's opening defeat at home to Leeds, Schlager has made more tackles than any other player in the Premier League this season. It is a good illustration of the combative style that is his trademark.

Image: Schlager has made more tackles than any other player in the Premier League

Not every supporter has been enamoured by Schlager and perhaps that is inevitable given the team's underwhelming start to the season. When searching for explanations, new arrivals come under scrutiny and the 29-year-old Austrian is not one for the future.

But he has had a fine career. Before Leipzig, he worked with Glasner at Wolfsburg, having emerged at Red Bull Salzburg before that. Oscar Garcia spotted him in their feeder team Liefering, another of Glasner's former clubs, and gave him his senior debut.

"He had very good potential," Oscar tells Sky Sports. "Some players in midfield left and we wanted to give him the chance to play. In the structure of Red Bull there were other players ahead of him but we saw that he was a player who could do almost everything."

Not that the self-deprecating Schlager would admit that. Speaking in the summer, he acknowledged his limitations, revealing that "you will not see me too much" as he keeps the game simple. "I do the dirty things you do not recognise but someone has to do it."

Image: Schlager joined Nottingham Forest on a free transfer in the summer

Aside from his standout moment that was impossible to miss, that was exactly what he did in the win over City. In what was a particularly intense game, Schlager was the only outfield player on either side to win possession of the ball more times than he lost it.

As a result, the player who in that amusing introduction to the fans admitted that he was "not the quickest" and "not as skilful as some" is actually crucial. Maybe this was the key line? "The most important thing is I want to make my teammates around me better."

James McAtee, Schlager's partner in midfield for much of the season so far, is enjoying the best form of his Premier League career. Ryan Yates took the plaudits on his return to the starting line-up on Saturday. Schlager is a facilitator, a true team player.

Speaking to his former coach Oscar about him, he remains a huge admirer. "In midfield, he can have the ball, he can make the last pass, he can play with the left, he can play with the right, and he can recover the ball very well when the team is gegenpressing."

The passing aspect is not obvious but the statistics show that while his pass completion rate is 84.5 per cent, his expected completion rate is just 77.6 per cent given the difficulty of those passes under pressure. He is in the top 20 for overperformance on this metric.

Sports.title: McIlroy: I need to be at 'absolute best' to win Race to Dubai
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy feels he will have to be at his "absolute best" to match Colin Montgomerie's record of eight Race to Dubai titles as he aims to beat Eugenio Chacarra to this year's prize in the UAE.

McIlroy has topped the DP World Tour's Order of Merit for the past four seasons but heads into the 2026 DP World Tour Championship, live on Sky Sports from 7am on Thursday, second in the standings, over 500 points behind former LIV Golf player Chacarra.

The world No 2 hopes his experience at Jumeirah Golf Estates - he has won the season-ending tournament three times and also lost in a play-off to Ryder Cup team-mate Matthew Fitzpatrick last year - will give him the edge.

Image: McIlroy has won seven Race to Dubai titles, starting win an inaugural victory in 2012

McIlroy said during his media duties on Tuesday: "The last few years I played well much earlier in the year where I've maybe not had to play at my absolute best to get it done. This week's a little bit different.

"The course has evolved a little bit over the years. It's certainly a lot more penal off the tee this year. The rough is very, very thick. You get a lot of bad lies in the rough.

"I think when you come back to a golf course that you played a lot on and you've done well on, that always gives you a little bit of an advantage starting the week.

"I think there's a little bit there [in having experience of the course]."

Image: McIlroy is around 500 pointed behind Eugenio Chacarra (right) in the Race to Dubai with one event remaining

McIlroy 'excited' to be in contention

On having the chance to emulate Montgomerie, McIlroy, who finished third at last week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, four strokes behind winner Jon Rahm, said: "I'm very excited to be in contention for the eighth. I made some ground up last week, maybe not as much as I wanted, but I felt like it was a step in the right direction.

"It's been a course that's been very good to me over the years, and I have a lot of experience on it and a lot of experience up at the top end of the leaderboard.

"I'm excited to do it all over again, to try to play well enough to give myself a real chance at the weekend."

McIlroy completed the career Grand Slam in 2025 after finally claiming an elusive Masters title - 11 years after his previous major triumph - and then made it back-to-back victories at Augusta National in April of this year.

The 37-year-old told reporters he is "increasingly proud" of his "consistency" and "longevity" over the years as he targets what would be a 45th career title should he win the DP World Tour Championship in the Emirates this week.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy got off to a perfect start at the Abu Dhabi Championship when he holed an eagle putt from off the green at his second hole

McIlroy added: "I think this will be the 15th or 16th year in a row that I will have finished the year in the top 10 in the world rankings.

"I think maybe an underrated part of careers is that longevity piece.

"I've stayed pretty much injury-free and I've kept working and trying to get better at certain aspects of the game, always tried to see weaknesses or be critical of myself and try to get better at them.

"That approach has worked really well for me and hopefully will continue to work well for me for a few more years yet."

Rahm: Chacarra has a game that works on every course

Rahm, who sits sixth in the standings after his success in Abu Dhabi and has a chance of a second Race to Dubai title, after 2019, said of current leader, and fellow Spaniard, Chacarra: "Not much can be said about his golf game that isn't already known.

Image: Chacarra has won three times on the DP World Tour this season

"He's a phenomenal ball-striker, has a great ball flight and the type of game that works on every golf course on the planet, stable in any condition.

"If the putter is at an average level, he's always going to have a chance and mentally you can tell he's somebody that wants to be there.

"When it's a Sunday and he gets close, he is not usually a name that falls off. He stays there, puts the pressure on.

"He's brave enough to do that and has a lot of confidence in himself, which you need."

Sports.title: 'Pass to Steph!' - Butler issues wise words from bench as Warriors win again
Sports.content:
Injured guard Jimmy Butler dressed up as a member of the Golden State Warriors' coaching staff and held up a clipboard with the message 'Pass to Steph' as the team made it eight wins in a row in the NBA.

The Steph in question, the legendary Stephen Curry, scored 25 points as the Warriors beat the New Orleans Pelicans 138-87 - the largest win by any team so far this season.

Curry passed DeMar DeRozan (26,800) for 16th place on the NBA's all-time career scoring list, with the 38-year-old's tally now 26,803.

Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said of Butler's input: "I told [assistant coach] Khalid (Robinson] 'one of these days we should have Jimmy dress up like us'.

"He's always got some great outfit on, something fashionable, and we wear our quarter-zips and sweaters.

"I said: 'we should really get him to dress like a coach one day' and then he walks out and he's dressed like us.
