The conference, organised by the Foundation for Democracy in Africa in collaboration with the Abia Global Chamber of Commerce, would attract investors from the United States and other countries.

He said the state’s ministries, departments, Agencies and local governments would also showcase investment opportunities available in the state at the event.

Mr Kanu said the conference was expected to stimulate economic activities and create business opportunities for hotels, restaurants, transport operators and other service providers.

He also announced that the third Abia International Trade Fair would hold from 27 November to 6 December at the Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba.

He said the fair, organised by the state Ministry of Trade and Commerce, in collaboration with the Aba Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture, would focus on manufacturing, agriculture, fashion, leather works and renewable energy.

The commissioner said the theme of the fair would be “Abia Beyond Borders: Driving Innovation, Trade and Industrial Growth”.

Capacity-building programme for senior civil servants

Mr Kanu said the Abia State Civil Service Commission would organise a capacity-building programme for permanent secretaries, directors and deputy directors from 16 November to 28 November.

He said the training would cover change management, work ethics and professionalism, succession planning and talent management, as well as leadership and strategic management.

According to him, the programme is part of the government’s ongoing reforms aimed at improving efficiency and service delivery in the state civil service.

(NAN)

World.title: COP31: Climate, health take centre stage as funders mobilise over $375 million
World.content:
Climate change and its sweeping impact on human health are expected to feature prominently in discussions at the ongoing 31st session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, as global health and climate funders mobilise more than $375 million to address climate-related health challenges.

The funding, announced at the opening of the conference on Monday, is expected to support efforts to ramp up adaptation and mitigation measures, particularly in vulnerable communities at the mercy of extreme heat, air pollution, climate-sensitive infectious diseases and other health risks linked to global warming.

The announcement comes amid fresh warnings from international climate and health pundits that rising global temperatures, worsening extreme weather events and soaring greenhouse gas concentrations are heaping unprecedented pressure on public health systems.

In Nigeria and several other countries worldwide, surging temperatures have fuelled public health concerns in recent years. The emergence of El Niño—a natural climate pattern marked by the warming of ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean —is also stoking worries among world leaders.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the UN Climate Change, said the world is witnessing dangerous heat levels that expose hundreds of millions of people to extreme temperatures.

“As today’s important data from the WMO shows, the world is getting dangerously hot. Hundreds of millions of people are exposed to extreme heat across Southern Asia,” Mr Stiell said.

He said heatwaves during the Northern Hemisphere’s summer broke temperature records and killed an estimated 50,000 people across Europe.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, climate change has evolved into a global health crisis, with consequences ranging from toxic air pollution and extreme heat to climate-related disasters that overwhelm health systems and critical infrastructure.

Climate crisis is a global health emergency

Mr Stiell identified the effects of rising temperatures on pregnancy, newborns and maternal health as another emerging health disaster linked to climate change.

He attributed the worsening situation to continued dependence on fossil fuels and deforestation, warning that the consequences are becoming increasingly dangerous for vulnerable populations.

“The impacts of rising heat on pregnancy, newborns and maternal health are another unfolding health disaster which has the fingerprints of the climate crisis all over it,” he said.

He added that health will remain central to COP31 discussions, guided by Türkiye and Australia, building on the progress made at COP30 in Belém, Brazil.

The UN climate chief also highlighted the Climate & Health Funders Coalition, which he said has already awarded more than $200 million to back climate and health interventions before the latest funding announcement.

Mr Stiell said practical solutions, including electrification and the transition to clean energy, are crucial to reducing climate-related health risks and the economic pressures associated with fossil fuel dependence.

He urged governments to accelerate the transition to cleaner energy, warning that continued reliance on fossil fuels will expose households, businesses and governments, including health systems, to soaring costs.

WMO: Global temperatures set to rise further

Also speaking, Celeste Saulo, the secretary-general of the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), said the organisation’s State of the Climate Update 2026 presented fresh evidence of an accelerating climate crisis.

She remarked that the past 12 years have been the warmest on record, while the past four years, including 2026, are the four warmest years recorded.

According to her, the global average temperature between January and September 2026 was approximately 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average.

Ms Saulo observed that temperatures could rise further before the end of the year due to a strong El Niño event, adding that its greatest impact on global temperatures is likely to be felt in 2027.

She said the current El Niño is unusually strong, with forecasts indicating that sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific could approach four times the threshold used by the WMO to declare an El Niño event between November 2026 and January 2027.

The WMO chief also disclosed other alarming indicators, including ocean heat touching a record high for the tenth year in a row and sea levels jumping to unprecedented levels.

She said rising sea levels are increasing the risks facing approximately 900 million people living along low-lying coastal areas.

Ms Saulo added that millions of people experienced dangerous heat in 2026, contributing to tens of thousands of excess deaths in Europe alone, while India, Pakistan and large parts of Asia and North America also experienced severe heatwaves.

She further cited devastating floods in parts of South America and Africa, droughts across parts of Asia, the Pacific and Central America, and catastrophic high-mountain disasters in China and Nepal.

Despite the worsening situation, she said progress is being made in strengthening early warning systems.

According to her, the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early warning systems increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025.

She urged governments at COP31 to prioritise sustained investments in climate observations, data systems and early warning infrastructure.

“We cannot afford to fly blind,” she said, stressing the need for urgent decisions and funding to address the growing climate threat.

Wellcome: Coalition awards over $225m in first year

Similarly, Alan Dangour, director of climate and health at Wellcome, said the latest WMO climate assessment demonstrates the magnitude of the threat posed by rising greenhouse gas concentrations, record-breaking temperatures, melting sea ice and rising sea levels.

He said the effects of climate change are increasingly being felt by people across the world, yet human health remains insufficiently prioritised in international climate negotiations.

“At Wellcome, we focus on people – on human health. And we’re working night and day to bring the health and wellbeing of people into rooms like this and the big negotiating rooms out there so that the impact of climate change on people finally takes its place at the climate change table,” he said.

Mr Dangour cited findings from the Lancet Countdown annual report, which Wellcome funds, estimating that fossil fuel-related air pollution and extreme heat contribute to more than three million deaths annually.

He also noted that extreme drought affected nearly 52 per cent of the world’s land for at least one month in 2025, the second-highest level on record.

According to him, drought and changing groundwater conditions are worsening food insecurity and sanitation challenges, with significant implications for public health.

However, he said several proven interventions could help curtail the health burden of climate change.

These include cleaner energy, electrification, heat early warning systems and broader adaptation measures, which he said could prevent deaths and reduce healthcare costs.

On the coalition’s funding efforts, Mr Dangour said Wellcome has joined forces with more than 35 philanthropic organisations to establish the Climate & Health Funders Coalition at COP30 in Belém, with an initial joint commitment of $300 million.

He announced that the coalition awarded more than $225 million in its first year to support interventions addressing extreme heat, air pollution, climate-sensitive infectious diseases and data systems.

The coalition also attracted an additional $150 million in commitments from new and existing funders, bringing the total funding mobilised to more than $375 million.

Mr Dangour called on governments and businesses to strengthen their responses to climate-related health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups, including children, pregnant women, outdoor workers and older people.

He also highlighted the need for policies to protect pregnant women and newborns from extreme heat exposure.

At the Pre-COP31 meeting in Fiji, he said Wellcome and its partners launched a global call to action seeking improved health guidelines, information, plans and data to protect pregnant women from extreme heat.

He urged governments to put human health and wellbeing at the centre of climate action, arguing that the success of climate negotiations should be measured not only by emissions reductions and temperature targets but also by lives saved and improved health outcomes.

World.title: Nigerian Government urges Africa to turn resource wealth into economic prosperity
World.content:
The Nigerian Government has urged African countries to expand local manufacturing and raw-material processing, warning that the continent’s continued dependence on commodity exports limits its economic potential and participation in global trade.

Vice President Kashim Shettima made the call on Monday in Abuja, saying Africa must move beyond exporting raw materials and importing finished products to developing industries that generate higher economic value.

Mr Shettima, represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Economic Affairs, Tope Fasua, spoke at an international conference on the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the Geoeconomics of African States, organised by the International Centre for Regional Integration and Trade Research (ICRITR) of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka.

“Resources confer potential. It is the capacity to process, transform, innovate, and negotiate that converts potential into prosperity,” Mr Shettima said.

He noted that Africa continues to supply raw materials to industries elsewhere, but imports finished products at higher prices, losing much of the economic value generated from its resources outside the continent.

The vice president cited cocoa and crude oil as examples of commodities Africa exports without sufficiently developing downstream industries to manufacture products from them.

He said the Federal Government is supporting the establishment of three lithium-processing factories in Nasarawa, Kaduna and Abuja as part of efforts to develop Nigeria’s capacity in the critical minerals value chain.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also noted that Africa’s economic transformation would depend on its ability to move from primary production to processing, manufacturing, technology and knowledge-based services.

Africa’s resource wealth and global trade

The director-general of the World Trade Organisation, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, also enjoined African countries to bolster industrialisation and regional value chains to increase the continent’s share of global trade.

Represented by her Senior Adviser, Jean-Yves Remy, Mrs Okonjo-Iweala said Africa is strategically positioned to benefit from changing global supply chains on account of its natural resources, youthful population and connections to international markets.

According to her, the continent holds nearly 30 per cent of the world’s critical mineral reserves, including cobalt, lithium, manganese, copper, nickel and graphite, but accounts for only about three per cent of global exports.

She cited intra-African exports, which contributed about 17 per cent of the continent’s merchandise exports in 2024, as evidence of ample room to expand regional trade.

Mrs Okonjo-Iweala described the AfCFTA as a tool to expand production and develop regional value chains. She identified infrastructure gaps, institutional weaknesses, and non-tariff barriers as major obstacles to implementation.

She called for improved roads, ports, electricity, shipping connections and trade finance, alongside efficient customs procedures and predictable regulations to facilitate cross-border commerce.

The WTO chief also urged African universities and WTO chairs to strengthen research, training and policy engagement, saying intellectual capacity is essential to growing the continent’s economic influence.

Africa must convert market size into economic power

Ngozi Egbuna, WTO chair and Nigeria’s director of ICRITR at Nnamdi Azikiwe University, said Africa must move beyond talks about its population and natural resources to address how those advantages could translate into economic power.

She noted that Africa’s population of about 1.6 billion people, coupled with its enormous resource base, has not weaned it off dependence on foreign markets, technology, financing and value chains.

She also warned that signing trade agreements and establishing a continental market is not an automatic answer to economic integration, adding that the real measure of success should be whether African businesses can trade successfully across borders and generate jobs.

Former President Goodluck Jonathan also called for stronger economic cooperation among African countries, saying the continent needs to move beyond creating a single market to developing an integrated productive economy.

Mr Jonathan, represented by John-Kennedy Opara, the executive secretary of the Nigerian Christian Pilgrim Commission, said the AfCFTA offers an opportunity to overcome the fragmentation of African markets and strengthen cooperation among countries.

“Our task is not merely to create one African market. It is to create one African productive economy,” he said.

He argued that Africa’s bargaining power would depend less on the resources beneath its soil than on its ability to transform them into productive assets.

Mr Jonathan called for greater investment in agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, automotive industries, fertilisers, machinery and renewable energy equipment to strengthen regional value chains.

He also urged African governments to invest in education, technology and entrepreneurship while ensuring that women, young people and small businesses benefit from continental integration.

The AfCFTA, which entered into force in 2019, seeks to establish a single continental market for goods and services and strengthen economic integration among African countries.

The agreement is expected to reduce trade barriers, encourage investment and enable businesses to operate across national borders with fewer restrictions.

However, implementation has been constrained by infrastructure deficits, high transportation costs, limited access to finance, border delays and differences in standards and customs procedures.

The vice-chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Bond Anyaehie, said the continent must build competitive enterprises capable of manufacturing products, providing services and financing trade within Africa.

He stated the success of the AfCFTA should be measured by Africa’s ability to source inputs, manufacture products and finance trade through local institutions.

He warned that trade liberalisation without adequate infrastructure and a continental market without competitive African businesses can not deliver meaningful economic transformation.

World.title: Nigerians are hungry, but Tinubu’s reforms will bring relief – Orji Kalu
World.content:
Abia North Senator, Orji Kalu, has acknowledged that Nigerians are hungry and experiencing economic hardship under President Bola Tinubu’s administration but argued that such difficulties are inevitable when a government undertakes major economic reforms.

Mr Kalu, a member of the APC, said although the reforms had imposed significant hardship on citizens, the Tinubu administration had stabilised the economy at the macroeconomic level and was now expected to translate those gains into improved living conditions.

The former Abia State governor made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on ARISE Television’s Prime Time, where he defended the administration’s economic policies and argued that the government deserved another mandate.

“People are shouting poverty. Yes, people are hungry. Even President Tinubu himself knows that things are difficult. You can’t go into reform without things going difficult,” he said.

The senator said Nigeria could not undertake fundamental economic changes without some sections of the population bearing the immediate consequences.

He argued that the reforms were necessary to move the country away from an economic structure that had persisted since independence and align it with changing global economic realities.

“Nowhere in the world, you say I want to reform the way it’s been done since 1960 to go with the anthem of the world, which is what the president is singing about,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Tinubu has stabilised economy

Asked what the All Progressives Congress (APC) government had achieved to justify another mandate, Mr Kalu said the administration had stabilised the economy at the macroeconomic level.

He distinguished between macroeconomic stability and the difficulties Nigerians continued to experience in their daily lives, saying the government must now focus on translating economic reforms into growth and improved welfare.

“The APC has been able to stabilise this economy on the macro level. What we are battling now is the micro level,” he said.

The senator said the next phase should involve tackling insecurity, restoring agricultural production and expanding manufacturing to create economic opportunities.

He said farmers must be able to return to their farms without fear of attacks, urging the president and his team to intensify efforts against insurgents and bandits.

“The second thing is to present Tinubu and his team to fight for these insurgents and fight them out, so farmers can go back to farm,” he said.

Mr Kalu also identified manufacturing as an area requiring greater attention, arguing that increased access to raw materials and improved production capacity would help drive economic growth.

He said the government needed to ensure that manufacturers could operate their factories efficiently and increase production, adding that economic growth remained necessary to sustain the gains of the reforms.

Mr Kalu also acknowledged that businesses were still struggling under the prevailing economic conditions, disclosing that factories were not generating enough revenue to pay workers’ salaries.

However, he maintained that their operating conditions had improved compared with 2020.

“I’m not enjoying because factories are not producing enough money to pay salary, but the factories are better today than 2020,” he said.

He argued that the foreign exchange reforms had given businesses greater predictability, allowing manufacturers to plan their operations and estimate production costs.

According to him, businesses previously struggled to plan because of sudden fluctuations in the exchange rate, which made it difficult to determine the cost of importing raw materials and other inputs.

He also cited the stabilisation of fuel prices and foreign exchange as evidence that the administration’s policies were beginning to address longstanding economic problems.

“The light is at the end of the tunnel now because we have stabilised the fuel prices, we have stabilised the foreign exchange. You can now sit down as a manufacturer and plan,” he said.

Cites Brazil’s experience

To support his argument that economic reforms often come with hardship, Mr Kalu cited Brazil’s experience under former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

He recalled attending Mr Lula’s inauguration in 2003, saying the South American country had faced economic difficulties before the former president embarked on reforms.

He argued that reforms could produce different outcomes for different sections of society, with some experiencing hardship while others benefited.

Mr Kalu also said Nigeria had improved its international relationships under Mr Tinubu and attracted the attention of foreign investors.

He urged the administration to focus on economic growth, particularly manufacturing, to ensure that macroeconomic improvements translate into tangible benefits for citizens.

World.title: France blames Iran for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges
World.content:
France has accused Iran of being behind cyberattacks targeting refrigeration units in supermarkets across the country last month.

It linked the attacks, which raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers in the country, to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

French authorities have also launched an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit affiliated with the IRGC.

Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was “unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression,” according to Al Jazeera.

Mr Barrot also said those responsible would be hit with sanctions at a European level.

A cyberattack on French supermarket freezers occurred overnight last month.

Between 11 and 12 October, retailers discovered that freezers and cold rooms had overheated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Millions of euros’ worth of food was spoiled. In some cases, the raised temperatures sparked fires or melted equipment.

French supermarket groups such as E-Leclerc, Intermarché, Carrefour, Monoprix and Coopérative U were all hit.

Around 300 of Intermarché’s stores and its Netto brand were affected.

Coopérative U said more than 100 of its supermarkets were targeted, while Carrefour identified about 80 affected supermarkets.

Monoprix also reported that about 5 per cent of its roughly 490 stores were hit.

Al Jazeera reported that French Investigators said attackers used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices in Iran to carry out the attack.

The attacks gained internet access to the refrigeration systems and remotely raised temperatures to 122 degrees Fahrenheit overnight.

Supermarkets in several other European countries also reported similar refrigeration problems last week, but it remains unclear if these incidents are linked, according to the BBC.

These include Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden.

Mr Barrot said France has requested international arrest warrants for the leaders of the Shahid Kaveh group.

“This is the first large-scale cyberattack carried out for sabotage purposes on French soil. It represents a major attack on the nation’s interests and on the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.

“We will also take any other measures that are proportionate and necessary, whether public or private, to respond to this attack and deter anyone who might seek to repeat it,” he said.

Iran has yet to respond to the allegations as of the time of this report.

World.title: Carrick set to be sacked by Man Utd: reports
World.content:
Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick looks on during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP)

Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side’s dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday.

United’s hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club’s miserable form and it is believed that Carrick will shortly be relieved of his duties.

United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run.

Although it is said that no final decision has been made, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick.

United owners the Glazer family and influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe would then decide whether to act on that recommendation.

Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end.

The 45-year-old, hired on a permanent basis in the close season after a successful interim spell last term, had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

United’s surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively.

They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down.

It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday.

When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him.

But United’s powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle.

USA boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job.

United have the rest of the two-week international break to secure a replacement for Carrick before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

World.title: Wenger considers challenging Infantino for FIFA presidency — Report
World.content:
Wenger

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering a challenge against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, according to the BBC.

The 77-year-old Frenchman is giving serious thought to contesting the position following growing calls from influential figures in European football for him to enter the race.

Some of Wenger’s supporters have reportedly indicated that they would back him even if he chose to step down before completing the four-year presidential term.

His possible candidacy could pose a significant challenge to Infantino, whose leadership has faced criticism following the collapse of a plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Although the controversy has unsettled his position in parts of European football, Infantino retains considerable support in South America, Africa and Asia.

He recently maintained that he enjoys the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of the global football community.

Wenger, who currently serves as Fifa’s Chief of Global Football Development, is expected to enjoy the backing of the Union of European Football Associations (Uefa), which has led opposition to Infantino over the abandoned commercial proposal.

However, sources close to the Frenchman told BBC Sport that he has yet to make a final decision on whether to contest the election. They also believe Infantino remains the favourite to secure another term.

The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to challenge Infantino is November 18, ahead of the election scheduled for March.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega became the first candidate to announce his intention to run in October, while Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also indicated interest in the position.

World.title: Why I rejected US asylum offer before Abacha arrested me — Obasanjo
World.content:
Obasanjo

By Ayobami Okerinde

Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has revealed that he rejected an offer of political asylum from the United States despite being warned that he would be arrested if he returned to Nigeria under the late military Head of State, Gen. Sani Abacha.

Obasanjo also recounted how he ventured into farming after retiring from the Nigerian Army at 42.

The former president disclosed this while narrating his experience under the military government in an interview published by BBC News Pidgin on Tuesday.

He said, “When I was leaving government as military head of state, I was leaving too early. I didn’t join the army to retire at the age of 42.

“Now I had to retire at the age of 42. At the age of 42, I had become a four-star general. There’s nothing else I can do in the army. I’ve become the military head of state. That’s the highest political office I could rise.

Obasanjo said his farming business was progressing well until Abacha’s government moved against him. He said he rejected the US asylum because he had committed no crime.

“So what can I do? I decided I would go into farming. It really was going well, and it went well until I was arrested.

“Abacha had decided that I must be liquidated; otherwise he would not be able to have his way. I didn’t know that. I was travelling and coming back, and the American ambassador in Nigeria called me and said his country had offered me political asylum because they knew that I would be arrested if I returned home.

“This was difficult for me. I don’t— I haven’t done anything. What do they want to arrest me for? Um, I don’t want political asylum.”

He said his passport was later seized, after which he proceeded to his farm. On arrival, one of his security personnel informed him that government security operatives had surrounded the premises.

According to him, a police officer dressed in civilian clothes subsequently approached him, claiming that an Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) had invited him.

“And when I arrived, they seized my passport; I made for my farm. At the gate of my farm was my security. He waved me down. He said that security had surrounded the farm. And within 15 minutes, this man came in mufti, not in uniform, a policeman, and he said, ‘Well, you have been invited by the AIG to come and help him.’ I said, ‘You are a fool.’

“‘If the AIG wants me to help him, he will not be inviting me. He will come here,” Obasanjo lamented, adding, “So it was my own car that I used to take myself to the police station. We saw the AIG, and the AIG said, ‘I have been instructed to arrest you.’”

The former president also disclosed that former United States President Jimmy Carter intervened on his behalf by appealing to Abacha. He said the intervention initially resulted in his being placed under house arrest after he had been held at an undisclosed location.

“I didn’t know that it was a decision of Abacha that some of us must not be kept free; otherwise, he would feel unsafe. I was put in a place.

“Then President Jimmy Carter came. He pleaded, and then they put me under house arrest. Then they came one day; I was playing squash at about 1 am.

“They came and said they were taking me away. And they took me away, and from there, I went to prison,” Obasanjo stated.

World.title: ‘I didn’t tell them to go buy votes,’ Wike defends N10m reward for councillors
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said he never asked councillors to buy votes with the N10 million he promised those who deliver their wards in the 2027 general elections.

“I didn’t tell them, ‘Take this money and go and buy votes.’ I said, ‘Go and work. Show commitment. Demonstrate that you really mean what you are talking about. When you win, come, and we are going to reward you,” he said.

Wike spoke on Tuesday during an inspection of ongoing infrastructure projects in Abuja. He was responding to criticism of the promise, which he said was an incentive for hard work and not an attempt to buy votes.

Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali Area Council the previous day, Wike had explained that the initiative was part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level.

“For the councillors, you have a task. I will hold a meeting with you again, and I will now say the way I am going to mobilise you, but I will give you a bet, like what is happening in the stars; it’s a competition.

“Anybody who delivers his ward, if you deliver your ward, that is what the Rainbow Coalition has decided to do as mobilisation and support for Mr President; we have to start in the FCT (I couldn’t say so when the president came because they gave me only two minutes to talk). But now that I have time to talk, let me say that the Rainbow Coalition all over the federation, as a form of mobilisation for Mr President to win this election, is saying that any councillor that delivers his ward will come and take N10 million. We want to mobilise for Mr President. So, go to your wards, and go and see your leaders. I know only you cannot do it, but we are using you as an instrumentality for your leaders. Go and meet your leaders and say, ‘Look, oh, there is something that has come.’ We must not allow this thing to go. Let’s dedicate our ward for Mr President’. So, that is for that,” Wike had said.

Speaking on Tuesday, Wike drew a line between rewarding political commitment and offering money to voters in exchange for their support. He said the councillors were challenged to prove their commitment through effective mobilisation.

To make his case, he pointed to athletes who are promised houses or other benefits if they return from international competitions with trophies. He asked why a similar reward in politics should automatically be read as bribery.

He also faulted sections of the media for failing to tell legitimate rewards apart from vote-buying. Political parties and candidates, he argued, routinely spend money on campaign s without facing the same scrutiny.

Wike urged journalists to pay closer attention to the difference between financial inducements meant to sway voters and rewards promised to political mobilisers for hitting set targets. He insisted that mobilisation should rest on commitment, performance and the ability to convince voters.

On the projects he toured, the minister expressed satisfaction with the progress of Interchange Section 2 (ISEX 2), the Southern Parkway and the S1 Road, which incorporates a fire station.

He said the projects were on course for completion by December 15, ahead of the general elections scheduled for January 16, 2027. According to him, the infrastructure record of President Bola Tinubu’s administration would give it a strong basis for its re-election campaign.

Wike added that his support for the President Bola Tinubu administration was driven by development and not party affiliation. He said Nigerians who genuinely desire progress should back policies and programmes aimed at national development.

World.title: Tinubu orders implementation of youth confab resolutions
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed the Federal Ministry of Youth Development to translate outcomes of the 2026 National Youth Conference into concrete government action, demanding measurable results and clear accountability from officials.

Tinubu gave the directive on Monday at the conference’s closing ceremony at the State House Conference Centre in Abuja.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented him at the event.

The ministry said this in a statement signed by Nwachukwu Christian, Assistant Director, for the Director of Information and Public Relations, on Monday.

Tinubu directed Youth Development Minister Ayodele Olawande to work with relevant ministries, state governments, private sector organisations and development partners to prepare a framework for implementing the conference’s recommendations nationwide.

He said the framework must outline clear priorities, assigned responsibilities, realistic timelines and measurable indicators to ensure effective implementation of the conference recommendations and strengthen accountability across participating government institutions.

Tinubu also insisted that young Nigerians must participate actively in implementing and monitoring the decisions, emphasising that their involvement should extend beyond consultations to meaningful participation in actual government decision-making processes.

“The real test of this conference begins after today. I do not want the recommendations of this conference to become another report gathering dust on government shelves,” he said.

He said Nigerian youths must not merely be invited to discussions but should also occupy meaningful roles in implementing decisions affecting their future, ensuring their voices influence government policies and programmes.

Acknowledging challenges confronting young Nigerians, Tinubu identified unemployment, rising living costs, limited educational opportunities, inadequate access to finance and insecurity as major concerns requiring sustained government attention and practical interventions.

He said his administration understood their concerns, adding that ongoing reforms and investments in education, skills development, innovation and entrepreneurship were designed to expand opportunities for young Nigerians.

“These initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, Three Million Technical Talent programme, YouthCred and Nigerian Youth Academy are interventions aimed at empowering young people,” Tinubu said.

He, however, emphasised the need to ensure that skills acquisition translated into employment, innovation attracted investments and young entrepreneurs gained improved access to financing to establish and expand sustainable businesses.

Tinubu commended the ministry’s conference planning committee and participating young Nigerians, saying they had demonstrated their capacity to contribute meaningful ideas and practical solutions towards national development.

Earlier, Olawande said the conference produced an 18-point action agenda covering six priority areas, following nationwide virtual consultations and physical deliberations involving young Nigerians.

Olawande said the conference provided an important platform for strengthening youth participation in national decision-making and ensuring their concerns informed government policies, programmes and development priorities across the country.

“For the first time in the history of this country, the youth can feel the government, see the government, and touch the government,” he said.

He said the recommendations would be pursued through relevant executive, legislative and judicial channels, while the ministry would engage stakeholders to secure the necessary institutional support.

The minister appreciated Tinubu for providing the platform, describing the conference as an opportunity for young Nigerians to move beyond expressing concerns and contribute directly to solutions.

Delivering the keynote address, Finance Minister and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, urged young Nigerians to participate actively in shaping the country’s economic future through constructive engagement and innovation.

Oyedele warned that negative perceptions and distorted narratives about Nigeria could discourage investments, weaken economic confidence and undermine opportunities for employment, entrepreneurship and sustainable national development.

“A factory that is not built means jobs that are not created,” he said, urging participants to embrace constructive engagement, innovation and practical solutions to national challenges.

He emphasised the need to translate economic progress into tangible benefits through increased investments, production, job creation and shared prosperity, ensuring Nigerians experience meaningful improvements in their livelihoods.

The statement said the conference, convened by the Tinubu administration, brought together young Nigerians from across the country and the diaspora to deliberate on national issues and make recommendations.

It said the conference focused on strengthening youth participation in governance, economic development and nation-building, with its outcomes expected to guide policies and programmes affecting young Nigerians nationwide.

“With Tinubu’s directive, attention is now focused on developing an implementation framework to translate the recommendations into concrete government actions, with youths expected to participate in the process,” it said. (NAN)

World.title: CAF reschedules 2026 Awards ceremony to December 2 in Lagos
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has rescheduled the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony to December 2 in Lagos.

CAF announced the new date in a statement on Tuesday, with the event brought forward five days.

Although the football body gave no reason for the change, the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Art Theatre, in Lagos, remains the venue for the ceremony.

The event will mark the return of the CAF Awards to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition, bringing together leading players, coaches, clubs and other personalities in African football to celebrate their achievements.

A total of 18 categories will be recognised at the ceremony, with the CAF Men’s Player of the Year and CAF Women’s Player of the Year awards among the major honours.

Other categories will recognise outstanding coaches, goalkeepers, emerging talents, clubs and national teams for their performances during the year.

Meanwhile, voting for the 2026 awards is ongoing and will run from November 5 to 20 across the men’s and women’s categories.

World.title: Iran calls on US to meet its demands to end war
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi

Iran on Tuesday urged the United States to meet its demands in a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after President Donald Trump spoke of “positive momentum” to end their eight-month war.

“The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran’s IRNA news agency.

“The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.”

Tehran has proposed reopening Hormuz, which it has blockaded since the start of the war, within two days in return for Washington meeting a raft of conditions.

These include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump, whose Republican party last week lost midterm elections in part due to the war, said on Monday that there was “positive momentum” towards ending the conflict after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House.

In a post on social media, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded” but said further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”.

“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said.

Diplomatic efforts, led by Qatar and Pakistan, are underway to find a resolution to the war, which broke out in late February when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

On Tuesday, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to “surrender” to the Iranian demands.

“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks,” said Rezaei, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in a post on X.

World.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
World.content:
…As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September

By Juliet Umeh

Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024.

Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August.

The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent.

The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line.

The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August.

Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August.

Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent.

However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August.

Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none.

The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter.

Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators.

World.title: Wike: N10m Reward for Councillors Not Vote-buying
World.content:
.Says incentive for political mobilization for 2027 elections

Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, has defended his promise to reward councillors with ₦10 million each for successfully mobilising political support and securing electoral victories in their wards ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that the proposed incentive should not be misconstrued as vote-buying.

Wike, who spoke on Tuesday during an inspection of ongoing infrastructure projects across the FCT, dismissed criticisms trailing the pledge, arguing that the financial reward was intended to encourage political mobilisation, commitment and hard work among grassroots political actors, rather than induce voters to support a particular candidate.

The minister maintained that there was a fundamental distinction between rewarding political mobilisers for achieving agreed electoral targets and offering money directly to voters to influence their choices at the polling booths.

His defence followed the controversy generated by his reported promise of ₦10 million to each councillor who successfully delivers his ward in the political contest ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The pledge has raised questions about the propriety of financial incentives in electoral politics, particularly against the background of concerns over vote-buying and the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process.

However, Wike insisted that he neither instructed the councillors to distribute money to voters nor encouraged them to induce the electorate to vote for any candidate. Rather, he said, his challenge to the councillors was to demonstrate their capacity to mobilise support through political engagement, organisation and commitment.

“I didn’t tell them, ‘Take this money and go and buy votes.’ I said, ‘Go and work. Show commitment. Demonstrate that you really mean what you are talking about. When you win, come and we are going to reward you,’” he said.

According to the minister, the proposed payment was a performance-based incentive designed to recognise individuals who successfully undertook the responsibility of mobilising support and delivering electoral results in their respective political constituencies.

He argued that political mobilisation required dedication, time, resources and organisational capacity, adding that individuals who committed themselves to achieving specific political objectives should be entitled to recognition and rewards for their efforts.

To further explain his position, Wike drew a comparison between the proposed political incentive and the rewards governments and other institutions offer athletes who distinguish themselves at international sporting competitions.

He recalled that athletes who win medals and achieve outstanding performances are sometimes promised houses, cash rewards and other benefits as recognition of their achievements.

The minister questioned why a similar arrangement in the political arena should automatically be interpreted as vote-buying, maintaining that rewarding individuals for meeting agreed performance targets was different from paying voters to influence their electoral decisions.

He suggested that the criticism surrounding the pledge failed to appreciate the distinction between incentivising political workers and financially inducing members of the electorate.

Wike also faulted sections of the media for what he described as a failure to properly examine the circumstances surrounding the proposed reward, urging journalists to distinguish between legitimate political mobilisation and electoral inducement.

He argued that political parties and candidates routinely spend substantial sums on campaign s, publicity, logistics and other mobilisation activities without attracting the same level of scrutiny.

According to him, the resources committed to political campaigns are intended to promote candidates, communicate political messages and secure electoral support, and should be examined within the broader context of political organisation.

The minister urged journalists to interrogate the purpose and circumstances of financial incentives in political campaigns rather than conclude that every promise of monetary reward amounted to vote-buying.

World.title: Africa Risks New Colonialism Through AI, Data Extraction, Gabi-Williams Warns
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Founder and Curator of Living Sustainably Here: African Perspectives on the SDGs, Olatoun Gabi-Williams, has warned that Africa risks a new form of colonialism through Artificial Intelligence (AI), data extraction and foreign control of digital infrastructure, urging African countries to take concrete measures to protect their indigenous knowledge systems and cultural resources.

Gabi-Williams, who made this known at the launch of ‘Our Digital Lives and Indigenous Pathways,’ volume II of the Anthology, Living Sustainable Here: African Perspective on the SDG, at the CANEX book fair in Lagos, weekend emphasised Africa’s cultural heritage, digital technology and knowledge production.

She stated that the continent must take concrete, consistent and effective measures to prevent foreign interests from appropriating its intellectual and cultural resources.

Speaking with journalists, she explained that African countries must establish their own digital infrastructure, develop indigenous knowledge databases and ensure that local communities retain ownership and control of information about their cultural heritage.

According to her, the growing use of technology to document, preserve and disseminate indigenous knowledge presents opportunities for Africa, but also raises concerns about consent, intellectual property, community ownership and the terms under which such knowledge is collected, stored and used.

“What is paramount is ownership. We must ensure that we either own the digital infrastructure through which our knowledge systems are documented, preserved and disseminated, or we establish robust safeguards in our partnerships with non-African technology entrepreneurs seeking to support these efforts,” she stated.

On the implications of the repatriation of colonial-era artefacts to Africa, Gabi-Williams said indigenous knowledge experts must be identified and documented to help reconstruct the original meanings and significance of the objects.

She explained that many of the artefacts, which could include family heirlooms, totems and sacred objects, carried cultural, spiritual, ecological and social meanings beyond their physical appearance.

She warned that failure to involve African experts and institutions in the process could allow foreign technology companies to take control of initiatives aimed at interpreting and digitising the knowledge embedded in the artefacts.

“My concern is that if we fail to bring these experts to the forefront of conversations about repatriated artefacts, international technology companies and entrepreneurs may approach UNESCO and similar institutions, obtain access to databases of these experts and engage them in reconstruction initiatives without African institutions and communities having meaningful ownership or control of the process,” Gabi-Williams said.

She added that foreign companies could end up owning the initiatives, digitising and storing reconstructed knowledge in datasets over which they exercise control, while Africans remain excluded from the economic benefits derived from their own intellectual resources.

“We cannot afford to repatriate our artefacts only to watch helplessly as others, often our former colonisers, who remain outsiders to our pre-colonial ancestral experience, appropriate knowledge that gives these artefacts their meaning,” the founder warned.

To address the challenge, Gabi-Williams advocated government-led initiatives or public-private partnerships involving relevant institutions to compile and maintain databases of indigenous knowledge experts.

She said access to such databases should be regulated through consent-based arrangements, with different levels of access depending on the nature of the knowledge, particularly as some indigenous knowledge is sacred, restricted or communally held.

She cautioned that documenting such knowledge should not automatically confer the right to make it publicly available.

“Nature abhors a vacuum. So does economics. If we don’t mine our own cultural gold, others, even bad guys will move in and do it for us. The bad guys are often very powerful,” she stressed.

On education, Gabi-Williams called on African universities and schools to integrate Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics (STEAM) education into existing curricula, even where funding and infrastructure are limited.

She argued that the objective should go beyond resource-intensive practical sessions to cultivate interdisciplinary thinking, problem-solving, systems thinking and the ability of students to make connections across different fields.

On the second volume of the ‘Anthology, Living Sustainably Here,’ she explained that institutions could introduce lessons around real-world problems and case studies to encourage students to approach challenges from different disciplinary perspectives.

She also emphasised the potential of digital learning platforms to address literacy and educational inequalities, particularly in underserved African communities.

Although she expressed a preference for traditional approaches to teaching, including handwriting and reading printed books, which she said support cognitive development, she acknowledged that digital learning offers valuable alternatives where educational resources are limited.

Citing an essay by Kenyan EdTech strategist, Joan Mwachi-Amolo, in her book, she pointed to Worldreader’s work in East Africa as an example of how technology could help bridge literacy gaps.

She also emphasised the importance of parental engagement in improving children’s literacy, noting that digital platforms could expand access to learning resources and digital storytelling across geographically dispersed communities.

On the contribution of the CANEX book fair to Africa’s publishing industry, Gabi-Williams described the initiative of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) as an emerging platform for strengthening the continent’s literary and intellectual landscape.

She cited the CANEX Prize for Publishing in Africa, which offers $20,000 to the winner and $2,000 to each runner-up, as an important source of financial support for independent publishers.

World.title: NUJ Honours Olori Janet Afolabi With Media Icon Award
World.content:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) National Secretariat has honoured Olori Janet Afolabi, CNN award winning journalist and Queen of Apomu Kingdom in Osun State, with the prestigious Media Icon Award.

A letter jointly signed by Comrade Alhassan Yahaya, National President, NUJ, Achike Chude, National Secretary, NUJ and Gbenga Onayiga, Chairman Planning Committee, said, ” this is in recognition of your immense contributions to the development of journalism in Nigeria.”

The award was presented to Olori Afolabi at a colourful ceremony of the 4th Edition of Annual Milestone Recognition of Media Icons in Nigeria.

The event took place on November 7,at Abuja Continental Hotel (former Abuja Sheration and Towers). lt was well attended by senior journalists, media executives, government officials, among others.

Olori Afolabi expressed profound gratitude to God and to the NUJ for finding her worthy. She said her work in the media was driven purely by a passion to serve humanity and use reporting as a tool for development.

“This honour is proof that when you work faithfully, your work will speak for you and recognition will find you.”she said.

Olori Janet Afolabi, a seasoned journalist, author and humanitarian, is the founder of OJAF, a non-governmental organization focused on women empowerment, girl-child education, youth development and child welfare.

World.title: As NLC Squares Up with TUC Over N70,000  Transport Allowance…
World.content:
For decades, the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress have presented themselves as two pillars of one house – Organised Labour. Most times when they speak they do so with one voice and governments are compelled to listen. But when they disagree, it’s government that gains to the disadvantage of workers, writes Onyebuchi Ezigbo.

Recently the two labour centres – the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) disagreed over a seemingly simple issue which is should workers take N70,000 as a transport allowance for six months, or should they insist that the money be built permanently into their salaries?

What began as a difference in negotiating tactics has grown into a public rift, with statements, counter-statements and affiliate unions taking sides. Now, veteran labour leaders have stepped in, warning that the quarrel, if left unchecked, could undermine the unity, solidarity and strength that took decades to build.

Observers of the unfolding crisis of confidence within organised Labour family of the opinion that it will augur well for the workers whose interest are better protected when both labour centres join hands to confront the government and other employers of labour.

The bone of contention in this current misunderstanding was an agreement reached between the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment and NLC on October 27, 2026 with major focus on commencement date for negotiation of a new minimum wage, issues on public service welfare and adjustment of tax relief for workers.

The agreement also addressed the Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) issues on CONHESS Palliative to cushion the effect of challenges faced by the workers, demands by Joint National Public Service Negotiation Council (JNPSNC) and reduction in petroleum pump price.

Other issues include, demand for payment of hazard allowance for Agricultural workers. According to JNPSNC, the agreement was the product of more than six hours of tough negotiation presided over by the Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Mohamed Maigari Dingyadi.

The labour team was led by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, with participation from JNPSNC and the Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU). A major highlight of the deal was the N70,000 transport allowance to be paid for the next six months to public servants starting November 2026, to subsidize unbearable transport costs.

It also cemented implementation of the long-overdue 40 per cent peculiar allowance reflecting the N70,000 minimum wage, which ought to have started since July 2024. The allowance will be domesticated at sub-national levels from November 2026, while arrears from May 1, 2026 will be paid in three tranches.

Other gains listed in the JNPSNC circular signed by National Secretary, Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo, include: a tripartite negotiation committee comprising government, labour and NECA to commence immediately; resolution of the 13-year-old CONHESS adjustment demand, with the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) given three weeks to conclude work; payment of 19-month arrears of health workers’ allowances in three installments from December 2026; issuance of a circular for hazard allowance to agricultural professional officers within three weeks; and a one-month window to reconvene to evaluate implementation.

On its part, the Federal Government has said it is “fully committed to ensuring that the ongoing collective bargaining agreement negotiation is concluded as soon as possible and that its implementation can bring the expected relief and improved condition of service to your members.” It gave the undertaking through the Minister of Labour Alhaji Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi at the opening of the National Executive Council meeting of the Medical and Health Workers Union in Abuja.

For NLC, the N70,000 is not the end of the struggle. NLC President, Joe Ajaero said it is a starting point, a foothold that cannot be taken away. “Whatever we got for you, nobody can take away from us. The N70,000 you are hearing is just an intervention. Like I said somewhere, when you give glucose to someone and it is inside his mouth, if you want to bring it out and you put your hand there. You know what will happen. So now that we have N70,000 on top of N70,000 you know where we are going to start from,” he told the 52nd National Executive Council meeting of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) in Abuja. He said the agreement was negotiated with the mandate from affiliate unions, including handling of JOHESU and JNPSNC issues, and represents a landmark achievement. Already, the move has the backing of the leadership of JNPSNC which dismissed the notion that NLC is a union of junior workers, saying all its affiliates have members across Ministries, Departments and Agencies up to Directorate level.

JNPSNC scribe argued that TUC, which was not part of the negotiation, has no basis to reject what it did not negotiate, though he added it would be commendable if TUC could secure a higher amount.

“Rejection of any item by any trade union is inconsequential to implementation because wider spectrum of workers has applauded decision as right step in right direction,” the circular said.

On the other hand, TUC sees the same N70,000 through a different lens – basing it’s argument on previous lessons where government failed to religiously implement the wage award. In its communique after an emergency National Administrative Council (NAC) meeting on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, signed by Secretary General, Dr. Nuhu Toro, TUC reaffirmed its demand for a sustainable salary increase, not another wage award. Its argument is rooted in experience: the wage award palliative agreed on October 2, 2023 was to run until the new minimum wage was signed into law on July 29, 2024. Workers, TUC said, received an average of only three months out of the ten months agreed upon.

“A sustainable salary increase offers a more meaningful intervention to improve workers’ purchasing power and living standards,” the communique said, stressing that the minimum wage is a statutory floor and not a ceiling on workers’ earnings.

Secretary General of TUC, Dr. Nuhu Toro who spoke at the recent MHWUN NEC meeting, put it more plainly: “The NLC is saying pay N70,000 transport allowance. The TUC was not there when that was negotiated, and the TUC said, we think you should negotiate for the N70,000 to be component of the salary. For instance, if N70,000 is added to your housing allowance, it becomes part of your salary and will not be taken off after six months. So the TUC said no, let’s make it holistic so that they won’t take it off after six months. So that is the argument. It’s not any issue.”

TUC also acknowledged the positions of its public-sector affiliates — SSAUTHRIA, NUAHP and SSASCGOC — noting they are consistent with its earlier position.

It stressed that workers’ welfare cannot be advanced by disregarding the collective bargaining rights of affected unions. The Labour Centre further reaffirmed its mandate under ILO Conventions 87 and 98 to represent, defend and negotiate for its members, and resolved to pursue constructive, result-oriented engagement with government to implement the resolutions of its October 8 meeting, including the JOHESU agreement.

At it’s NAC meeting, TUC tasked it’s leaders to refocus efforts on securing a salary increase while refraining from public exchanges on the matter.

Intervention by Veteran labour leaders

Amid verbal exchanges by leaders of the two Labour Centres, concerned stakeholders especially former union leaders have stepped in to help broker peace and resolve this understanding between NLC and TUC.

Speaking at the NEC meeting of the Medical and Health Workers Union in Abuja, immediate past NLC President and former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC), Comrade Ayuba Wabba, said veteran leaders, including pioneer labour leader, Hassan Sumonu and other past presidents of NLC and TUC are intervening in the dispute

He said they have summoned both centres for dialogue and asked them to suspend further altercation in the media.

“The leaders have asked them to suspend any further altercation, we do not want to see any further statement. We the veterans have intervened”.

Wabba described most of the things trending in the media space about the disagreement as hype imported by third parties to undermine workers’ unity. He warned that the NLC was built by sweat and blood and must not be brought down.

He said: There are more important issues like inequality than those issues that are being imported by third parties to try to undermine workers’ unity, workers’ strength and workers’ solidarity. Anybody that wants to bring it down certainly we will not take it lightly. Unity is strength and all of us must advocate for unity of the working class.” Wabba explained that though the veterans have started preliminary engagement to settle the misunderstanding among the labour centres, there will be more meetings and consultations going forward to try to bring both parties to amicably work together to protect workers welfare.

In substance, both centres want the same thing: more money in workers’ pockets that government cannot easily withdraw. Whereas NLC argues that securing the allowance first creates a new baseline for the next round of negotiation, TUC’s position is that without embedding it in salary structure, the allowance will expire after six months, just as the 2023 wage award did.

Both arguments have merit. Both carry risk. Accepting a temporary allowance could become a substitute for real salary review. However rejecting it outright could leave workers with nothing while negotiations drag.

Considering the current mood of the workers, any suggestion that they should surrender the N70,000 transport allowance for another round of negotiation may not be an acceptable option. It may be that both NLC and TUC will have to present a common front to pressurise government to retain the N70,000 beyond the six months timeline and convert it into a permanent salary component in the ongoing Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiation that government says its committed to concluding soon. If they fail, the rift could deepen, with affiliates lining up behind one centre or the other, and government exploiting the division. For now, both sides have at least agreed to one thing: stop fighting in public. Whether that truce holds and whether it produces a better deal for workers will be the real test of veteran wisdom.

World.title: Civil Society Decries Osun NLC Strike
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Executive Director World Institute for Peace, Lamina Omotoyosi, yesterday warned the Osun State Government and the various labour unions on the three-day warning strike embarked upon by the Osun State chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) over the lingering local government crisis in the state.

The executive director noted that as an organisation committed to promoting peace, stability, development and social justice, “he considered this warning strike needless, barbaric, deceptive and a deliberate attempt to ground the state’s economy and potentially trigger civil unrest.”

According to him, “We have no reservation in concluding that the strike is being embarked upon in bad faith and is politically motivated, with the intention of blackmailing the judiciary and creating a possible atmosphere of anarchy in the polity. “

Omotoyosi, who stated this at a press conference addressed in Osogbo yesterday, contended that: “This position is informed by the trajectory of the local government crisis in Osun State and the plethora of litigations surrounding local government administration in the state.

“It is our expectation that the labour movement should serve as a fountain of knowledge, the voice of workers, and by extension, the voice of the downtrodden.

“Labour unions are expected to be populated by people with sound knowledge of the law and judicial processes, and this should reflect in their approach to sensitive issues such as the ongoing local government crisis in Osun State, particularly when the matter is still pending before several courts of competent jurisdiction.

“Unfortunately, the reverse appears to be the case in Osun State. As things stand today, the labour movement in the state appears to have chosen political patronage over honesty, integrity and the general interest of workers.

“As an organisation, we are equally disturbed and seriously concerned about the protracted nature of the local government crisis and the legal impediments affecting the release of local government allocations.

“We are genuinely interested in a timely resolution of the crisis and the release of funds to improve the lives of people at the grassroots. However, ignoring existing legal obstacles amounts to mischief, dishonesty and an affront to the judiciary, particularly when such a position is being advanced by a labour movement that ought to be a custodian of public institutions, including the judiciary.”

The Executive Director, however, considered the proposed strike as mere political grandstanding, either to patronise the state government, intimidate the judiciary or blackmail the Federal Government of Nigeria.

He posited that: “The fundamental questions that the Osun State NLC should provide answers to are: Who is withholding the local government allocations? Why are the allocations allegedly being withheld? And why were the allocations released recently to the 2022 elected local government administration in Osun State?

“The straightforward answer to these questions is the court, the court, and the court.

“Therefore, if the courts are yet to reach a final determination of the matter, who has the authority to either stop or authorise the release of the allocations? Certainly, no other institution can legitimately override the judicial process. Or is the Osun NLC suggesting that the Federal Ministry of Finance or the Central Bank of Nigeria should release the funds in flagrant disregard of subsisting court orders”?

“The foregoing raises serious questions about what the Osun NLC intends to achieve through this strike. “

“What cannot be obtained through the courts cannot be secured through industrial action.”

“This is similar to the situation in which local government workers embarked on one of the longest strikes in the state’s history, lasting about 20 months, after several attempts to obtain judicial redress proved unsuccessful.”

He recalled that the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE) dragged the local government council chairmen and councillors to court but subsequently withdrew the cases after approaching several courts.

He said: “It is therefore unfortunate that the labour movement now appears to be resorting to extrajudicial means of seeking redress. Such conduct is capable of encouraging anarchy and should not be condoned in a democratic society governed by the rule of law.

“For emphasis, protests and industrial strikes are fundamental rights and privileges guaranteed by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended. However, in the present circumstances, this warning and sympathy strike represents, in our view, a high level of dishonesty and an attempt to create an economic crisis in the state while inflicting unnecessary hardship on public and private business owners.

“The option we would have expected from the labour unions is constructive dialogue with all parties involved in the ongoing litigations. The unions should persuade the parties to either withdraw the cases or consider an out-of-court settlement that would pave the way for the resolution of the impasse surrounding local government funds in Osun State.

“Interestingly, the labour unions could have used the opportunity of their recent inclusion in the Campaign Council of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, as announced by the State Coordinator, Senator Ademola Adeleke, to engage the political parties involved in the litigations. Such engagement could help facilitate an amicable resolution and allow Osun State to breathe again over the lingering local government allocation crisis.”

World.title: NGF, GCNg to Host Health Innovation Exchange in Abuja
World.content:
* Eight maternal, newborn and child health projects to feature as stakeholders examine pathways to adoption and scale

The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) and Grand Challenges Nigeria (GCNg) are set to convene the 2026 Annual Meeting and Innovation Exchange on Friday, November 13, in Abuja, to explore ways of translating Nigerian-led health research and innovations into practical solutions for improving healthcare delivery.

The meeting, scheduled to hold at Lake Greenfield Hotel, will bring together state governments, research teams, government institutions, development partners and financing stakeholders to examine how evidence-based health innovations can be adopted, funded and scaled across the country.

With the theme, ‘Innovation to Impact: Evidence, Adoption, Uptake and Scale for Better Health in Nigeria,’ the exchange is expected to focus on the institutional capacity, policy decisions and sustainable financing required to assess how promising innovations can progress from research towards practical use.

Eight projects supported by Grand Challenges Nigeria, focusing on maternal, newborn and child health, will feature prominently at the meeting.

The projects address critical healthcare challenges, including newborn sepsis diagnosis, umbilical cord care, community-supported digital healthcare, emergency maternal referrals, birth-defect identification, perinatal asphyxia research, digital risk support and the prediction of severe pre-eclampsia.

According to the organisers, the programme will combine research evidence and practical implementation experiences with policy discussions on adoption, replication across states, financing and the evidence and conditions required for adoption and scale.

The NGF’s involvement is expected to bring state-level implementation priorities and opportunities for peer learning into the discussions, particularly as state governments remain critical to the delivery of healthcare services.

The African University of Science and Technology will also contribute a Policy Lab focusing on the institutional decisions required to translate research into practice.

Grand Challenges Nigeria was launched in November 2024 as a national platform supporting locally led research and innovation in health and food security.

Anchored by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria, the initiative operates in partnership with the Office of the Vice-President and the Federal Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology.

It is supported by the Gates Foundation, with technical assistance from the Science for Africa Foundation, and forms part of the wider Grand Challenges family of initiatives.

The organisers said the November 13 meeting would help identify the additional evidence, institutional engagement and financing required to assess promising innovations for their next stage of development.

Participation in the exchange and inclusion in the showcase do not constitute a decision to fund or adopt an innovation. Research findings should be interpreted within their stated limitations.

Attendance at the meeting will be by invitation. Media organisations seeking interviews or coverage arrangements are invited to contact the Grand Challenges Nigeria secretariat in advance.

World.title: CASER Condemns Rising Electoral Violence across Nigeria
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

A social rights group, the Citizens’ Advocacy for Social and Economic Rights (CASER), has condemned the rising wave of electoral violence and political intimidation across the country ahead of the 2027 general election.

The group noted that within days, incidents in Ado-Ekiti, Calabar and Asaba have raised urgent questions about the safety of candidates, campaign workers and ordinary citizens.

CASER in a statement issued by its Executive Director, Mr. Frank Tietie, said that Nigerians must be able to attend a rally, support a candidate or campaign for a political party without risking their lives.
