“So far, one Nigerian has been killed in Asaba, while others have been severely injured in the above three locations,” CASER said while extending its condolences to the bereaved family and its solidarity to the injured.

The group, accordingly, warned that it is documenting these incidents and at the same time putting Nigeria’s political class on notice.

“We will use appropriate national, regional and international mechanisms to pursue accountability for those who carry out, order, finance, organise or knowingly facilitate electoral violence. We will press for prosecution wherever the evidence warrants it and seek compensation and other lawful remedies for victims and bereaved families.

“We will follow the evidence regardless of party affiliation, political influence or public office.

“Section 40 of the Constitution protects peaceful assembly and association. That protection applies to supporters of every political party. The police and other competent authorities must act promptly on credible threats and provide protection impartially.

“Federal, state, FCT, and local government officials must discharge their respective legal duties to protect Nigerians’ right to gather peacefully for political rallies.

“Where public officials participate in attacks, use public resources to facilitate them or breach a legal duty to protect, CASER will pursue personal liability against each one of them wherever the evidence and the law support it,” the statement read in part.

CASER, however, disclosed that it would seek joint liability where officials or institutions share legal responsibility, and vicarious liability where the relevant government or public authority is legally answerable for the conduct of its officers.

The group added that where officials received credible warnings, they will demand the records showing who received them, what measures were available and what action was taken.

“Victims and witnesses should report every incident to law enforcement and notify CASER. They are urged to lodge a formal complaint with the Nigeria Police Force, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) or any other competent law enforcement authority. They are also to notify CASER at: complaints@citizensadvocacy.org OR; citizensadvocacy@gmail.com

“Such notifications to CASER must include a contact phone number, the date and location of the electoral violence, and a brief account of the incident. Where possible, such complaints should preserve original photographs, videos, threatening messages, medical records, receipts and witness details.

“Families may also report on behalf of victims who have died or are unable to report. CASER will track how complaints are handled, press for timely investigations, and pursue appropriate claims for compensation and other redress.

“We call on the Inspector-General of Police and the relevant Commissioners of Police to preserve evidence, protect witnesses, and provide public updates on these three investigations, or any others that may occur in the future, before and after the elections.

“Political parties and candidates must condemn attacks unequivocally, cooperate with investigators and answer for the conduct of anyone they direct or sponsor. Every Nigerian must be free to campaign, assemble and vote without fear.

“CASER assures the public that electoral violence is totally unacceptable, especially at a time when Nigerians are already being traumatised by some of the worst forms of violence by kidnappers, terrorists and bandits. ‘Enough is Enough!’,” the statement added.

World.title: WIM Leaders Seek Increased Access to Capital,Global Opportunities For African Women
World.content:
Jonathan Eze

Founder and Chairperson of Women in Management (WIM), Dr. Sulochana Segera, and Chairperson of Women in Management Africa (WIMAFRICA), Dr. Ngozi Oyewole, have called for greater economic opportunities, global recognition and increased participation of Nigerian and African women in trade, investment, entrepreneurship and leadership.

The duo made the call at a press conference in Lagos on Monday ahead of the maiden African edition of the WIM Global Economic Forum, themed “The Power Shift: Women Driving Africa’s Global Economic Influence,” scheduled for November 10–11, 2026, at the Federal Palace Hotel, Lagos.

They said the gathering would move beyond celebrating women’s achievements to creating practical opportunities for them to influence economic decisions, access capital, expand businesses, participate in international trade and establish strategic partnerships across continents.

Oyewole, who is also the founder of Commonwealth Business Women Africa, said the power shift being advocated by WIMAFRICA was about ensuring that women moved from being participants in economic activities to becoming influential decision-makers, business owners, manufacturers and investors.

She noted that African women were already sustaining local markets, building enterprises and contributing significantly to national economies, but needed greater access to finance, markets, infrastructure and leadership opportunities to maximise their potential.

“For me, the power shift is about who gets to make economic decisions. African women already build businesses, create jobs and sustain local markets. The next step is for more women to own the companies that grow, decide where capital goes and help set the terms on which Africa trades,” she said.

She explained that the conference would amplify the contributions of African women, particularly in manufacturing, agriculture, technology, trade and other productive sectors, while exploring how they could take advantage of opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

Oyewole stressed the importance of backward integration and local production, noting that women entrepreneurs could play a significant role in strengthening African supply chains by transforming locally available raw materials into finished products.

She identified access to finance as one of the biggest constraints facing women-owned businesses, arguing that many entrepreneurs have the capacity and market opportunities to expand but lack the working capital required to execute contracts and sustain production.

Drawing from her experience as a manufacturer and founder of NOXIE Limited, an office furniture manufacturing company established nearly three decades ago, she explained that businesses often struggle to finance materials, wages and production costs while waiting for customers to pay for completed contracts.

She therefore called on financial institutions to develop financing products that reflect the operational realities of women-owned enterprises, particularly manufacturers and small businesses.

Oyewole also urged government agencies and corporate organisations to make procurement opportunities more accessible to qualified women-owned businesses, ensure transparent bidding processes and promote timely payment for completed contracts.

On AfCFTA, she said many women entrepreneurs remained inadequately informed about rules of origin, documentation and the procedures required to access cross-border markets, despite the enormous opportunities offered by the continental trade agreement.

She further identified poor roads and unreliable electricity as major challenges affecting women in rural agriculture and food production, noting that inadequate infrastructure contributes to post-harvest losses and increases the cost of transporting goods to urban markets.

She called for stronger protection of women’s property rights, particularly land ownership, arguing that removing cultural and institutional barriers would enable more women to invest in agriculture, manufacturing and other productive ventures.

On her part, Segera said the decision to bring WIM’s global platform to Africa was driven by the need to recognise the contributions of African women and connect them to international business and investment opportunities.

She explained that WIM was established 16 years ago in Sri Lanka to identify, celebrate and promote women whose work contributes significantly to economic development and professional advancement.

She disclosed that the organisation now has members and award recipients in 29 countries, providing an international network through which accomplished women can collaborate, exchange expertise and establish business relationships across borders.

Recounting her relationship with Oyewole, Segera said they first met in India, where the Nigerian entrepreneur was representing Africa at an international conference. She said their subsequent engagements in Dubai, the United Kingdom, Malaysia and Sri Lanka strengthened their relationship and exposed them to the achievements and challenges of women across different economies.

According to her, Oyewole’s commitment to bringing the WIM Top 50 recognition platform to Africa provided an opportunity to showcase the continent’s women and demonstrate their capacity to contribute to the global economy.

Segera stressed that the recognition initiative would go beyond celebrating professional titles and positions to highlighting the talents, resilience, innovations and achievements of African women.

She described Africa as an increasingly important market in the global economy, adding that women remained central to unlocking the continent’s economic potential.

She emphasised that the gathering was not intended to be merely another conference and awards ceremony but a platform for business partnerships, investment, trade and long-term economic cooperation.

Segera also called for reforms in financial institutions, arguing that women entrepreneurs should be assessed on their business potential and capacity rather than traditional assumptions about their economic roles.

She further emphasised the need for shared family responsibilities, noting that women often combine professional commitments with domestic responsibilities, thereby limiting the time and opportunities available for business expansion and career advancement.

“You cannot keep half of your population inactive in the economy and expect the economy to grow,” she said.

Also speaking at the press conference, Seun Oyewole, Managing Director of NOXIE Limited and Founder of Legend of Legend Productions Ltd, described Nigeria’s hosting of the maiden African edition of the global gathering as an important opportunity to showcase the country’s achievements and Africa’s growing economic potential.

Seun, who is also a member of WIMAFRICA and oversees event planning for the organisation, particularly the Global Economic Forum 2026 and the 16th Professional & Career Awards Gala 2026, said the gathering would bring together women and men from different countries and professional backgrounds to celebrate women’s achievements and explore opportunities for collaboration.

He expressed pride that the first African edition was taking place in Nigeria, noting that Lagos, as the country’s commercial capital, offered an appropriate platform to showcase the entrepreneurial talent, commercial activities and business opportunities available across the continent.

He said the preparations had provided an opportunity to bring together stakeholders committed not only to highlighting the challenges facing women but also to showcasing their achievements across different sectors.

Providing further details of the programme, Dr. Ngozi Oyewole said the November 10 sessions would feature discussions on Africa Trade 2035, AfCFTA, resilient supply chains and the continent’s role in the next decade of global growth.

Other sessions would examine financial inclusion, economic power, ownership, capital mobilisation and wealth creation in the artificial intelligence economy.

The programme would also feature discussions on women’s leadership, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, the future of finance, sustainability, green capital and climate resilience.

Participants are expected to examine how digital transformation can strengthen Africa’s banking sector, improve global competitiveness and create new opportunities for women-owned businesses.

The conference will also feature sessions on global human capital, the future of business, talent development, leadership and productivity in the emerging economy.

A global forum recognition ceremony, executive networking and business matchmaking sessions are also scheduled as part of the programme.

The event will culminate in a gala night on November 11, during which outstanding women who have distinguished themselves in business, leadership, innovation and professional practice will receive awards and recognition.

The organisers said the ultimate measure of the gathering would be the partnerships and practical opportunities created after participants returned to their respective countries, particularly in expanding women’s access to capital, contracts, international markets and economic decision-making.

World.title: How Zimbabweans are allegedly recruited to fight for Russia
World.content:
Zimbabweans are being recruited to fight for Russia. Image: Facebook/Zimblogger

The arrest of nine Zimbabweans in South Africa has renewed concerns about recruitment networks allegedly targeting Zimbabweans with promises of lucrative employment in Russia, only for some to end up fighting in the war against Ukraine.

The nine men appeared in two Gauteng magistrates’ courts on Monday, 9 November 2026, after their arrest at OR Tambo International Airport and a hotel in Bruma, Johannesburg.

They face charges under South Africa’s Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act 15 of 1998.



The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) said they allegedly intended to leave South Africa to participate in the Russia-Ukraine war.

However, authorities have not disclosed who allegedly recruited the nine men or the arrangements made for their travel.

How recruiters allegedly lure Zimbabweans with job promises

An investigation by Zimbabwean news outlet CITE published in early 2026, detailed how recruiters allegedly convince the victims.



The recruiters reportedly use WhatsApp groups, private referrals and social media to attract Zimbabweans with promises of civilian employment and financial security.

Some prospective recruits were reportedly told they would secure jobs in Russia, with recruiters issuing invitation letters under the pretext of cultural visits.

Others were allegedly promised attractive salaries and assistance with travel arrangements.



CITE reported that some Zimbabweans based in South Africa, including people working as Uber drivers and in informal employment, were also approached with offers to travel to Russia.

One source interviewed by the publication, who was already in the Donbas region, claimed that some recruits received only seven days of military training before being deployed to the frontline.

The investigation also found that recruits were allegedly required to sign one-year contracts written in Russian, raising concerns about whether they understood the terms of their agreements.



In some cases, recruits reportedly had their passports confiscated after arriving in Russia, making it difficult to leave.

Zimbabwe investigates alleged recruitment networks

Zimbabwean authorities have also taken action against people suspected of facilitating the recruitment of citizens for the conflict.

In March 2026, four Harare men appeared in court facing human trafficking charges over allegations that they worked with a Russian national to recruit Zimbabweans using promises of firefighting jobs.



According to a separate CITE investigation published in August, prosecutors alleged that one of the accused received approximately US$8 167 (R133 700) in connection with the recruitment of six Zimbabweans.

The government has also acknowledged the scale of the problem.

In March, Information Minister Zhemu Soda said 15 Zimbabweans had been killed in the conflict, while 66 others were reported to be in Russia.



CITE subsequently reported that the death toll had been revised to 18.

The latest arrests in South Africa raise further questions about recruitment activities targeting Zimbabweans beyond the country’s borders, particularly those seeking employment opportunities abroad.

World.title: How Wandile Duba can break into the Bafana Bafana squad
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs forward Wandile Duba has been in fine form this season for the Glamour Boys.

In the 11 matches he has played, AK47 has scored seven goals. With newfound confidence and an impressive scoring record, many Amakhosi fans have called for his inclusion in the Bafana Bafana squad.

The 22-year-old is yet to earn a Bafana cap, and some believe his national team debut is long overdue.



Given his age, explosiveness and current form, Duba could add more firepower to Hugo Broos’ attacking options.

How can Wandile Duba break into the Bafana squad?

Duba has developed a reputation for scoring important goals. His big-game temperament could work in his favour, particularly if he inspires Kaizer Chiefs to Carling Knockout Cup glory this season.

Last year, he played a crucial role in Amakhosi’s Nedbank Cup triumph, scoring an important goal in the semi-final against Mamelodi Sundowns.

Delivering similar performances in high-pressure matches could strengthen his case for national team selection.

Consistency will also be key if Wandile Duba is to force his way into the Bafana squad.

While his seven goals in 11 appearances make for impressive reading, Duba will need to maintain that level throughout the campaign to convince Bafana coach Pitso Mosimane that he deserves an opportunity.



If he continues his current scoring form, a national team call-up could become increasingly difficult to ignore.

Chiefs supporters certainly believe Duba has done enough to warrant a place in the squad.

Following his hat-trick last month and another goal against Siwelele, several fans took to X to voice their support for the young striker.

World.title: How to watch Bafana Bafana vs Kenya: Channels, kick-off time
World.content:
Bafana Bafana vs Kenya will be broadcast by the SABC and on streaming platforms. Image: Bafana Bafana (X).

Bafana Bafana can get within touching distance of AFCON 2027 this weekend.

South Africa host Kenya on Friday in the first of two clashes in their qualifying group.

Here’s where to watch the game on TV on Friday if you’re not watching live.



South Africa not taking Kenya lightly

Pitso Mosimane’s boys welcome Kenya to the Orlando Stadium on Friday, 13 November.

SAFA has confirmed the kick-off time as 18:00.

The return leg will be played in Nairobi on 17 November, according to SABC News.

Bafana Bafana held their first training session at Milpark Stadium on Monday evening (9 November).

Several players currently stationed abroad have yet to report to the team’s camp.

Mosimane has already cautioned that Kenya are somewhat unpredictable due to their current struggles.



According to SAFA, he remarked:

“Be very careful when you are playing against an emotional team, especially when they have got nothing to lose.”

Bafana Bafana vs Kenya: Who will broadcast the game?

SABC 3 confirmed on Facebook that it would show the game live on Friday.

The match will be available for streaming on the SABC Plus website as well.

DStv will also broadcast the game via the SuperSport PSL channel (202) and its Maximo offerings.

In Kenya, viewers should be able to access the match through several platforms.

The Kenya Times previously listed SuperSport, Canal+, New World TV, and Azam TV as holding broadcasting rights for the AFCON 2027 qualifiers.

3 Days to go! 🇿🇦

​Bafana Bafana takes on Kenya at the Orlando Stadium on Friday 13 November 2026 for the first leg of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers.

Tickets are available on https://t.co/OckMQA4oRF#BafanaPride@adidasfootball @adidasza @rexona_sa @standardbankza… pic.twitter.com/4828dMxpvH — Bafana Bafana (@BafanaBafana) November 10, 2026

What’s at stake for South Africa?

Bafana Bafana are leading their qualification group with six points from two games so far.

Guinea are second on three points, having lost their game against South Africa.

Kenya, coached by Benni McCarthy, are third and lead Eritrea on goal difference.

However, the Harambee Stars are already through to the main AFCON 2027 tournament as co-hosts.

Next year’s edition will be hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania.

This means that Bafana, Guinea, and Eritrea are battling for one spot in their qualifying pool.

A win over Kenya, coupled with Guinea losing or drawing, would effectively see South Africa secure that place.
