World.title: Race Coast rolls out the welcome mat for raiders this Cape Summer Season
World.content:
Race Coast has increased its incentives for visiting owners and trainers as it looks to attract horses from across South Africa to the Western Cape for the 2026/27 Cape Summer Season. Image: Race Coast website

Race Coast is once again encouraging owners and trainers from across South Africa to bring their horses to the Western Cape this summer, with an enhanced package of raider incentives available throughout the 2026/27 Cape Summer Season.

Running from 1 November 2026 to 28 February 2027, the programme combines attractive win bonuses, free seasonal stabling and transport rebates, adding further value to an already lucrative summer of racing in the Cape.

Incentives doubled

Owners and trainers of visiting horses who win at regular Cape Summer Season meetings will each receive a R20 000 win bonus, doubling the R10 000 incentive offered last season.



The rewards increase further on designated Cape Summer Festival of Racing meetings, where winning owners and trainers will each receive a R50 000 bonus.

The owner’s R50 000 Festival bonus will not apply to races carrying a gross stake of R600 000 or more.

Visiting horses will also benefit from free seasonal stable rental, while Race Coast will assist qualifying raiders with transport costs.

A 50% transport rebate will be available to horses completing two runs in regular races during the qualifying period.

Horses competing in Listed and Grade 3 races will qualify for a 75% rebate, while those competing in Grade 1 and Grade 2 races will qualify for a 100% transport rebate, subject to a maximum transport reimbursement of R15 000.

Attractive proposition

Western Cape Racing Operations Manager Kurt Felix said the incentives were designed to make travelling to the Cape an increasingly attractive proposition for connections around the country.



“The Cape Summer Season has always attracted some of the best horses in South Africa, and we want to continue making it as attractive and accessible as possible for owners and trainers to be part of it. With increased stakes, enhanced win bonuses, free stabling and meaningful assistance towards transport costs, there is real value in bringing a horse to the Western Cape this summer.”

“Raiders add enormously to the quality and competitiveness of our racing and we want visiting connections to know that they are genuinely welcome. Whether you have a horse targeting one of our major Festival races or one that is suited to the broader summer programme, there are opportunities throughout the season.”

Prestigious fixtures

The Cape Summer Season runs through one of the most anticipated periods on the South African racing calendar, with racing at Hollywoodbets Kenilworth and Hollywoodbets Durbanville and a programme that builds towards some of the country’s most prestigious summer fixtures.

2026/27 CAPE SUMMER SEASON RAIDER INCENTIVES

1 November 2026 – 28 February 2027

R20 000 win bonus to the owner at regular Cape Summer Season meetings

R20 000 win bonus to the trainer at regular Cape Summer Season meetings

R50 000 win bonus to the owner at Cape Summer Festival meetings*

R50 000 win bonus to the trainer at Cape Summer Festival meetings

Free seasonal stable rental for raiding horses

50% transport rebate for horses completing two qualifying runs in regular races

75% transport rebate for horses competing in Listed and Grade 3 races

100% transport rebate for horses competing in Grade 1 and Grade 2 races

Transport rebates capped at R15 000

*The R50 000 owner’s bonus is not payable in races carrying a gross stake of R600 000 or more.

With increased stakes and enhanced incentives on offer, there has never been a better time to race in the Western Cape this summer.

World.title: ActionSA willing to work with DA – but there’s a catch
World.content:
DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille and ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba are at the centre of Johannesburg's coalition talks, with ActionSA refusing to back Zille as mayor. Image: X

ActionSA has ruled out supporting Helen Zille as Johannesburg mayor but says it remains willing to negotiate a coalition agreement with the Democratic Alliance (DA).

The party’s national chairperson, Michael Beaumont, confirmed its position as negotiations continue following last week’s local government elections.

The DA secured approximately 34% of the vote in Johannesburg, making it the largest party in the metro but leaving it short of the majority needed to govern alone.



ACTIONSA DRAWS THE LINE ON ZILLE

Beaumont said ActionSA’s objections were directed at Zille rather than the DA.

He accused the DA’s mayoral candidate of undermining previous coalition arrangements in Johannesburg.

ActionSA fears that a coalition led by Zille could face further instability.

“We are open to negotiating with the DA,” Beaumont said during an interview on Monday.

He confirmed that ActionSA had contacted the party and was awaiting a meeting date.

MASHABA PROPOSES COMPROMISE

ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba has reportedly offered to withdraw from the Johannesburg mayoral race if Zille does the same.



In a letter dated 7 November to DA federal leader Geordin Hill-Lewis, Mashaba proposed allowing the DA to nominate another mayoral candidate whom ActionSA could support.

The proposal would allow the DA to retain the Johannesburg mayoral position without Zille taking office.

It also forms part of broader discussions involving the leadership of Gauteng’s metropolitan municipalities, including Tshwane.

COALITION TALKS CONTINUE

ActionSA has already held discussions with the African National Congress (ANC) and Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) as parties negotiate agreements in municipalities without outright majorities.

Johannesburg remains a key focus after voters left the city with no single party able to govern independently.

The DA has maintained its position that Zille should become mayor.

However, ActionSA’s refusal to support her has placed the mayoral candidate at the centre of negotiations between the two parties.

The parties have yet to reach an agreement on Johannesburg’s next administration.

World.title: Why some parts of South Africa are sweltering while others stay cool
World.content:
From the hot Northern Cape to the cooler Highveld, several geographical factors explain South Africa's temperature differences. Image: canva

South Africans can experience dramatically different temperatures depending on where they live, with one province baking under extreme heat while another enjoys considerably cooler conditions.

It is not unusual for parts of the Northern Cape, Limpopo and North West to experience very high temperatures while coastal areas or parts of the Highveld remain relatively cool.

These differences are not simply down to the time of year. South Africa’s varied landscape, altitude, surrounding oceans and changing weather systems all play a role in determining how hot or cold different parts of the country become.



Here is why temperatures can vary so significantly between provinces, sometimes on the very same day.

South Africa’s geography plays a major role

One of the biggest influences on South Africa’s temperatures is its geography.

The country has a diverse landscape that includes a high-altitude interior plateau, low-lying coastal regions, mountain ranges, semi-arid areas and subtropical lowlands.



These different environments respond to heat and changing weather conditions in different ways.

For example, the Northern Cape is characterised by large, dry areas that can experience extremely hot daytime temperatures, while the Drakensberg and other elevated regions tend to be considerably cooler.

The National Climate Change Information System (NCCIS) notes that parts of the Northern Cape can experience summer daytime temperatures exceeding 36°C, while higher-altitude areas experience much cooler conditions.



This means that even when the country is experiencing the same broad seasonal conditions, local temperatures can differ considerably.

Altitude can make some areas considerably cooler

South Africa’s interior is largely situated on a high plateau, with an average elevation of around 1 200 metres above sea level.

Higher elevations generally experience lower temperatures because air pressure decreases with altitude, causing rising air to expand and cool.



This is one reason why Johannesburg, despite being inland, does not always experience the same extreme daytime heat as lower-lying areas.

Johannesburg sits approximately 1 694 metres above sea level, while parts of the Northern Cape are considerably lower.

The Drakensberg is another example, with its highest peaks reaching more than 3 000 metres.



The altitude of the interior plateau is identified as one of the main factors responsible for the country’s relatively moderate temperatures compared with other regions at similar latitudes.

The two oceans influence coastal temperatures

South Africa is surrounded by the Atlantic and Indian oceans, which have a significant influence on temperatures along the coastline.

However, the two oceans do not affect the country in the same way.



The east coast is influenced by the warm Agulhas Current, which flows southwards along the coastline. This contributes to the warmer, more humid conditions often experienced in KwaZulu-Natal.

The west coast, meanwhile, is influenced by the cold Benguela Current, which flows northwards along the Atlantic coastline.

This helps explain why areas along the Western Cape’s west coast can experience considerably cooler conditions than parts of the east coast.



The difference is particularly noticeable in coastal towns, where the temperature of the surrounding ocean can influence local weather.

The ocean also moderates temperatures because water heats up and cools down more slowly than land.

As a result, coastal areas generally experience smaller differences between daytime and night-time temperatures than inland regions.



Cold fronts can bring a sudden temperature drop

Another reason South African provinces can experience different temperatures is the movement of weather systems.

Cold fronts regularly move in from the Atlantic Ocean, particularly affecting the Western Cape and parts of the southern coastline.

These systems can bring cooler air, increased cloud cover, rain and strong winds.



As a cold front moves eastwards, its influence can spread to other parts of the country, although not every province experiences the same conditions or temperature drop.

For example, Cape Town may experience cloudy, rainy and chilly weather while parts of Gauteng, Limpopo or Mpumalanga remain sunny and warm. The timing, strength and direction of these weather systems determine which areas are affected.

Hot berg winds can push coastal temperatures higher

While cold fronts can bring cooler weather, South Africa also experiences hot, dry winds known as berg winds.



According to the South African Weather Service (SAWS), berg winds blow from the interior plateau towards the coast.

They typically develop when a low-pressure system occurs along the coast while higher pressure is present over the interior.

As the air moves down from the elevated interior towards the coast, it is compressed and warms up.



This can cause coastal temperatures to rise sharply, sometimes resulting in extremely hot and dry conditions.

Berg winds are particularly noticeable along parts of the Western and Eastern Cape coastlines and can also increase the risk of veld fires.

Cloud cover and rainfall make a difference

The amount of cloud cover over an area can also influence how hot it becomes during the day. When skies are clear, more solar energy reaches the Earth’s surface, allowing the ground to heat up.



Thick cloud cover, on the other hand, reduces the amount of sunlight reaching the surface and can keep daytime temperatures lower.

This is one reason why an area experiencing widespread thunderstorms or persistent cloud cover may be noticeably cooler than a nearby region enjoying clear skies.

Rainfall can also contribute to cooler daytime conditions, particularly when accompanied by cloud cover and cooler air.



South Africa’s rainfall patterns differ between regions. Much of the country receives summer rainfall, while the Western Cape generally receives most of its rain during winter.

These different seasonal weather patterns also influence how temperatures vary across the country.

Why temperatures can differ within the same province

It’s important to remember that these differences are not limited to provincial borders. A province can have several distinct climate zones, meaning temperatures can vary considerably between its own regions.



KwaZulu-Natal, for example, has a warm, humid coastline, while areas further inland and towards the Drakensberg experience cooler conditions because of their elevation.

Mpumalanga also has contrasting climates. Its Lowveld is generally subtropical and warm, while the Highveld experiences colder winters and occasional frost.

The Eastern Cape has similarly varied conditions, with its coastal areas often warmer than its mountainous inland regions.



This means that a provincial weather forecast may not accurately describe conditions everywhere within that province.

Ultimately, the country’s combination of high-altitude inland areas, warm and cold ocean currents, mountain ranges and changing weather systems means that temperatures can vary dramatically from one province to another.

World.title: South Africa’s unemployment rate rises as 8.6 million remain jobless
World.content:
South Africa’s unemployment crisis has deepened, with the official unemployment rate increasing to 33.7% in the third quarter of 2026. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South Africa’s unemployment crisis has deepened, with the official unemployment rate increasing to 33.7% in the third quarter of 2026, despite more than 100 000 additional people finding work.

Statistics South Africa (Stats SA) released its latest Quarterly Labour Force Survey on Tuesday, 10 November, showing that the official unemployment rate increased from 33.6% in the second quarter.

Unemployment number hit 8.6 million

The number of employed people increased by 101 000 to 16.8 million between July and September. However, the number of unemployed people also increased, rising by 97 000 to approximately 8.6 million.

This resulted in the country’s labour force growing by 198 000 during the quarter, as more people entered or remained in the job market.

Deputy Director for the Quarterly Labour Force Survey at Stats SA, Dimakatso Maloka, said finance, manufacturing and mining were among the industries that contributed to employment growth.

Finance recorded the largest increase, adding 111 000 jobs. Manufacturing added 33 000, while mining employment increased by 31 000.

However, employment declined in three industries.

Private households recorded the largest decrease, shedding 68 000 jobs, followed by agriculture, which lost 34 000, and construction, which shed 8 000.



Formal sector gains offset by losses elsewhere

The survey showed that formal-sector employment increased by 268 000 to 12.3 million in the third quarter.

However, informal-sector employment declined by 98 000, while the household sector recorded a decrease of 68 000.

Compared with the same quarter in 2025, total employment was down by 215 000.

The provincial figures were mixed.

The Western Cape recorded the largest employment increase, adding 48 000 jobs, followed by North West with 45 000, the Eastern Cape with 36 000 and Gauteng with 25 000.

Employment declined in the Free State and Mpumalanga.

Discouraged job-seekers increase

The latest figures also highlight the number of South Africans who have stopped actively looking for work.

The number of discouraged job-seekers increased by 70 000 to 3.7 million in the third quarter.

These are people who are available to work but are no longer actively seeking employment, often because they believe there are no suitable jobs available.

The broader measure of unemployment, which includes people in the potential labour force, increased to 44%, from 43.8% in the previous quarter.

Youth unemployment remains high

Youth unemployment remains one of the country’s biggest labour-market challenges.

The unemployment rate among people aged 15 to 34 edged down by 0.1 percentage point to 47.3%.

The number of unemployed young people decreased by 23 000 to five million. However, youth employment also declined, falling by 5 000 to 5.5 million.

The latest figures underline the difficulty South Africa faces in creating enough jobs to absorb people entering the labour market, with the modest quarterly increase in employment failing to prevent the overall unemployment rate from rising.

Are you currently employed?

Let us know by clicking on the comment banner below …

World.title: City of Cape Town gives political parties deadline to remove election posters
World.content:
The City of Cape Town has reminded political parties and independent candidates who contested the 2026 Local Government Elections to remove their election posters. Image: Fotor

The City of Cape Town has reminded political parties and independent candidates who contested the 2026 Local Government Elections to remove their election posters and swivel banners by Wednesday, 18 November.

The deadline applies to all election posters and banners, as well as the string and plastic fasteners used to put them up.

Could face additional costs

The City said it had distributed its Rules for posters and swivel banners during voter registration, general election, and by-election processes, 2026 to all registered political parties a few weeks before the elections.



Parties and independent candidates are required to ensure that all election material is removed by the deadline.

Those who fail to comply could face additional costs.

The City has warned that it will remove posters and banners left behind after 18 November and charge the relevant political party R123.48 per poster or banner, excluding VAT.



Report any posters

Residents are also encouraged to report contraventions or complaints about political posters and swivel banners in writing to the Deputy Municipal Electoral Officer, Catherine Overmeyer, at Catherine.Overmeyer@capetown.gov.za.

World.title: 'Off the record' | Madlanga Commission hears clash over Matlala's legal consultations
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Madlanga Commission’s proceedings were delayed on Tuesday after businessman Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala’s lawyers alleged that his legal privileges had been violated.

Matlala’s lawyer, Adv. Annelene van den Heever, told the Commission there had been an agreement between his legal team and the Commission’s legal team that certain parts of their consultations with him would remain off the record.

Van den Heever alleged that during Matlala’s testimony on Monday, Adv. Adila Hassim disclosed information that was covered by the alleged agreement.

However, the Commission’s Adv. Mahlape Sello denied the allegations.

Sello told the Commission that the legal team had gone to great lengths to obtain Matlala’s testimony while he was being held at various correctional facilities, including Ebongweni in KwaZulu-Natal.

She said Matlala’s lawyers were present during consultations at Kgosi Mampuru Correctional Centre in Pretoria.



However, they were not present at Ebongweni, and the consultation there did not proceed.

Sello said the Commission’s team would not have gone to such lengths to secure Matlala’s testimony and conduct an investigation if the information was not intended to be presented publicly.

This is the second consecutive day that Matlala’s testimony has been delayed.

On Monday, his lawyer argued that he could not continue testifying because there was a possibility that he could incriminate himself. Despite the objection, his testimony proceeded.

Following the 11am tea break on Tuesday, it emerged that Sello had not been party to any agreement as alleged by Matlala’s lawyer.

Van den Heever was ordered to apologise for suggesting that Sello had been aware of the alleged agreement.

World.title: LIVE | Matlala returns to Madlanga Commission after explosive allegations
World.content:
PRETORIA - Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala made a series of serious allegations during his appearance before the Madlanga Commission on Monday.

These included claims of false statements, prison-related deals and alleged coercion by officials from the Investigative Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC).

Matlala is expected to return to the Commission on Tuesday to continue his testimony.

On Monday, Matlala disputed several details contained in his statement and repeatedly invoked his right against self-incrimination.

World.title: NPA confirms Perumal's hospitalisation
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) has confirmed that Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) Chief Investigator Dylan Perumal is in hospital.

Earlier this month, reports emerged that Perumal had been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of a hospital in the Eastern Cape.

The NPA has dismissed rumours that he attempted to take his own life.

World.title: Australia to adopt 'mandatory' AI safeguards
World.content:
MELBOURNE - Artificial intelligence companies will have to abide by new "mandatory" safeguards when operating in Australia, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.

Global unease about the power of advanced AI is growing after a string of hacking incidents involving leading companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Australia would establish a new AI safety regulator tasked with implementing measures designed to keep the booming industry in check, Albanese said.

"Our task is to make sure that we shape AI, rather than AI shape us," Albanese told reporters.

"You can't turn it off and pretend it isn't happening. But what we can do is make sure you shape it in Australia's interest."

The measures would include "mandatory" reporting of AI security breaches and the independent evaluation of frontier AI models, Albanese said.

"Australia is a first mover in this space and we want to make sure that we reap the potential benefits of AI," said Albanese.

"But we need to ensure that we get it right, and social licence is absolutely critical."

Australia voiced deep unease earlier this year after a prototype OpenAI model bypassed safeguards during training and hacked into a government website.

The model sought access to a health statistics portal in June, sidestepping restrictions to breach a section hosting private files.

OpenAI did not raise the alarm with the Australian government until September, when it sent a message to a generic email inbox that is only checked once each day.

- Can't 'run away' -

Defence minister Richard Marles said AI companies should open themselves to external scrutiny to make sure their tools are safe.

"There needs to be greater risk management of AI capabilities," he told reporters.

"It's important that there is independent assessment of AI models."

Marles said it was pointless to pretend that AI would not reshape the world.

"This is not a technology that we can run away from.

"AI is part of our lives today and it will only grow as part of our lives going forward."

With immense renewable energy potential and vast stretches of uninhabited land, Australia has billed itself as a prime location for the data centres needed to power artificial intelligence.

OpenAI is involved in the construction of a massive data centre on the outskirts of Sydney.

But AI companies also face a growing local backlash, as many Australians question their ethics and the environmental footprint of their power-hungry data hubs.

A major point of contention is whether Australia will water down its copyright laws so that chatbots can be trained on songs, books and other works of art.

World.title: Cricket Australia chief rules out reopening 'sandpapergate' probe
World.content:
SYDNEY - Cricket Australia chief Todd Greenberg on Tuesday ruled out reopening the investigation into the sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal, saying he did not see "any compelling reason" for a new probe.

Opening batsman Usman Khawaja said in his autobiography that the 2018 plot had been common knowledge throughout the team and not limited to a small number of players.

The book, released on Tuesday, has reignited the debate over the cheating controversy, in which Australian players were caught using sandpaper to make the ball swing against South Africa.

Greenberg said he would consider Khawaja's revelations -- which were on Monday backed as "100 percent accurate" by fellow opener David Warner -- but said there was no need for further action.

"We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," he told radio station SEN.

"I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that."

Captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace after the ball tampering was exposed.

A Cricket Australia investigation found they were the only three players with prior knowledge of the plot.

But Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, tells a different story in a chapter dedicated to the scandal in his book "Sabr".

"It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he told the Sydney Morning Herald at the weekend ahead of the book's release this week.

World.title: 'You Can See Everything' captures weirdness of 'post-truth era'
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Breakout hit documentary "You Can See Everything" has spawned a cultural moment.

The three-hour-long film plunges audiences into the surreal world of Elizabeth Holmes, one-time doyenne of Silicon Valley imprisoned for fraudulent claims about her supposedly revolutionary blood-testing tech.

A smash box office success, the film -- which begins one month before Holmes heads to prison -- has spawned ubiquitous internet memes, lookalike contests and commentary from influencers enamoured by the darkly comic, deadpan style of her mock inquisitor, Nathan Fielder.

Holmes's legend as a rare woman tech founder has proven fertile ground for numerous media postmortems of her sham business's implosion.

"I've followed this story a lot over the years," said filmgoer Alexandra Lesnik, 29, at a packed afternoon screening in Brooklyn, the first time she had watched a documentary in a theatre.

"This was a new, different perspective of her."

Another cinemagoer, Nathan Sayers, said he had "read a lot about her" ahead of the film's release.

"What brought me was a lot of buzz among friends," added Sayers, 53, who concluded the A24 film was in his "top five movies."

World.title: Unemployment rate increases to 33.7%
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa’s official unemployment rate rose slightly to 33.7% in the third quarter of 2026, from 33.6% in the previous quarter.

According to Statistics South Africa’s latest Quarterly Labour Force Survey, 101,000 more people found jobs, bringing the total number of employed people to 16.8 million.

However, the number of unemployed people also increased by 97,000 to 8.6 million.

The total number of people in the labour force increased by 198,000, or 0.8%, during the quarter.

The survey also found that the number of discouraged job-seekers -- people who have stopped looking for work -- increased by 70,000 to 3.7 million.

Meanwhile, the number of other people available for work decreased slightly by 1,000 to 860,000.

The number of people unavailable for work remained unchanged at 44,000.

World.title: Home Affairs expected to roll out digital asylum registration system
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Home Affairs digital asylum registration system is expected to go live on Tuesday.

The system aims to modernise the asylum process, reduce administrative backlogs and improve the management of applications.

But asylum seekers will still need to verify their fingerprints at refugee reception centres.

And now, it appears they may have another obstacle to overcome: March and March.

The group is mobilising its supporters to block asylum seekers from accessing these centres.

Last month, the Durban High Court restricted the group’s protests, imposing strict conditions on its activities.

World.title: Ruto to Gachagua: 'Wait until 2032, we will leave the stage'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto flags off the construction of the 22-kilometre Kenyoro SDA-Riana Market-Kerina road in Bonchari Constituency, Kisii County, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has challenged former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua to leave young politicians alone, saying his generation will exit the political stage in 2032 after serving the country.

Speaking at a rally in Bonchari Constituency, Kisii County, on Tuesday, November 10, Ruto accused Gachagua of targeting emerging leaders and interfering with their political growth.

The President named South Mugirango MP Silvanus Osoro, Nyaribari Chache MP Zaheer Jhanda, Kisii Woman Representative Dorice Donya, Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro, Kikuyu MP Kimani Ichung’wah, Kericho Senator Aaron Cheruiyot and Kitutu Chache North MP Japheth Nyakundi among the young leaders he accused Gachagua of targeting.

“Wachana na vijana wa Kenya. Hawa vijana viongozi hawa. Si tuko na vijana viongozi ambao wanakuwa? Hawa kina Osoro. Hawa kina Zaheer Jhanda. Hawa kina Donya,” Ruto said.

He said he would bring together politicians of his generation and leave younger leaders room to continue building the country.

“Mimi na wao tutaondoka 2032. Niwaachie hawa vijana uwanja waendelee na taifa letu la Kenya,” he said.

Ruto also took aim at Gachagua, repeatedly referring to him as “Mr Texas” and “Mr Chuki” and accusing him of using ethnic divisions to mobilise political support.

He dismissed Gachagua’s claim that he would teach him politics, describing the former Deputy President as a one-term MP and a political failure.

“Ati anasema atanifunza siasa. Sasa wewe, mtu one-term MP, political failure. Mtu muongo... ati utafundisha nani siasa?” Ruto posed.

The President also questioned Gachagua’s remarks about relocating to Texas if political instability affected Kenya, asking why a leader would threaten to leave the country instead of working towards its stability.

The remarks came amid an escalating political exchange between the two leaders, with Gachagua challenging Ruto to prepare for a political contest ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader had also criticised the President’s development record in Kisii and Nyamira counties, accusing his administration of relying on promises and handouts instead of delivering projects.

During his tour of Bonchari, Ruto launched the construction of the 22-kilometre Kenyoro SDA-Riana Market-Kerina road in Bonchari Constituency, Kisii County.

The road is expected to improve access to markets and create opportunities for trade and investment in the region.

Ruto dismissed the criticism, accusing his former deputy of spreading falsehoods about government projects and programmes. He cited the Rironi-Mau Summit highway, Bomas of Kenya, the Social Health Authority (SHA) and the proposed modern market at Gikomba as examples of projects he claimed Gachagua had misrepresented.

On Bomas of Kenya, Ruto dismissed claims that the government had sold the facility to a Turkish investor, insisting it remained government property. He announced that the government would hold a meeting at the facility in January.

He also defended SHA against claims that the programme would collapse within six months, saying 33.5 million Kenyans had registered and that the government had sent Sh190 billion to hospitals across the country.

The President cited Sh8.7 billion in payments to health facilities in Kisii County as evidence of the programme’s progress.

On the Rironi-Mau Summit highway, Ruto maintained that construction was progressing despite criticism from his political opponents.

He also dismissed claims that the Gikomba market land had been sold, saying the government was preparing to open a modern market at the site within one or two months.

World.title: Sakaja defends Sh43.7b drop in Nairobi County's pending bills before Senate
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja tells Senate that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors. [File, Standard]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has told the Senate that pending bills in the city have been reduced from Sh118.79 billion to Sh75.07 billion through verification and payment.

Sakaja revealed that internal verification established that the Sh43.73 billion reduction was not achieved solely through payments but also involved legal assessments, court-ordered adjustments and the verification of disputed claims.

The governor, who appeared before the Senate County Public Accounts Committee at Parliament Buildings in Nairobi on Monday, said addressing the inherited debt required establishment of a verification committee to scrutinise the entire outstanding amount and establish the validity of the claims.

“The reduction of Nairobi County pending bills by Sh 43.73 billion was not achieved entirely through cash payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court-ordered reductions and disputed claims,” said Sakaja.

He told the Senate Committee chaired by Homa Bay Senator Moses Kajwang that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors and that he had constituted a committee to undertake an internal verification of the entire amount before payments were done.

Sakaja explained that the verification established that the reduction was not solely through payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court decisions and disputed claims.

“I would like to inform Senators that my administration has provided a detailed schedule accounting for the Sh43.73 billion pending bills reduction through adjustments and reconciliations,” he said.

The governor said that of this amount Sh1.63 billion related to legal assessments, while Sh19.14 billion represented government-guaranteed loans whose servicing had been suspended due to a lack of supporting documentation and loan schedules.

Sakaja told Senators that Sh19.2 billion related to LAPFUND interest and penalties which the County said had been reduced following a court consent that brought the claim down to approximately Sh8.2 billion.

He said that they had provided a signed indemnity form, in accordance with County Treasury rules governing misplaced payment documents, alongside a financial memo confirming that the works had been undertaken and payment made.

“The audit further raised concerns over Sh16.04 million in receivables from non-exchange transactions, which lacked sufficient supporting documentation,” said Sakaja.

The governor told senators that beyond the verification of pending bills his administration had also strengthened the county’s legal department to reduce expenditure on external legal services and protect public resources.

Sakaja noted that through the reforms, Nairobi saved approximately Sh8.48 billion in legal costs over two financial years by expanding its in-house legal capacity, handling more litigation internally and negotiating reductions in legal fees claimed by private advocates.

According to the County Assembly’s Justice and Legal Affairs Committee, of the 174 court cases concluded during the period under review, 84 were handled by the County’s in-house legal team, with 47 determined in Nairobi’s favour, representing a 56 per cent success rate.

Kajwang, commended the County for reducing its pending bills but asked the Governor to provide additional documentation supporting the payments and processes undertaken to account for the Sh43.73 billion reductions.

“The Senate County Public Accounts Committee requires further clarification on the verification exercise and the adjustments made to the outstanding debt,” said Kajwang.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses opposition divisions as 'polygamous family' rivalry
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County on November 8, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims of divisions within the Opposition, describing the disagreements among its leaders as normal sibling rivalry in a polygamous family, while insisting that the coalition remains united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.

Gachagua said the Opposition leaders were committed to working together to challenge President William Ruto, despite their differing opinions on the timing of selecting a joint presidential flagbearer and occasional disagreements among their political camps.

Speaking during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County, the former Deputy President likened the political differences to children from the same father competing for attention but eventually uniting whenever an external threat emerges.

“The Opposition is united to a man, and we have agreed that we will have a single presidential candidate. Everybody is committed, and we talk on a daily basis. The only challenge is normal petty problems,” he said.

He added that the disagreements should not be interpreted as a breakdown of the coalition, maintaining that such differences were healthy and expected in a broad political alliance.

“Ile shida kidogo ni ya boma, watoto wengi wa baba mmoja. Watoto huko ndani, oh, baba anakupenda kuliko mimi. Mbona ulinunua kiatu kabla mimi? Si hiyo ni kawaida kwa polygamous family?” he posed.

Gachagua said the bigger threat to Opposition unity was not necessarily disagreements among its principals but the conduct of their supporters, social media influencers and political bloggers, whom he accused of fuelling unnecessary tensions through insults and online confrontations.

He cautioned Opposition leaders against allowing overzealous supporters to dictate their political relationships, warning that unchecked political attacks could eventually weaken the coalition and undermine its common objective.

“If there is anything to separate us, it is our supporters and social media bloggers. Wanawakisha moto hakuna, watu wangu na wa Matiang'i wanatukanana na sisi tunakula breakfast pamoja,” he said.

He further claimed that some political influencers associated with his DCP party had been recruited and allegedly paid by individuals opposed to him to attack his leadership and the party.

Gachagua urged coalition principals to exercise restraint and avoid reacting to every provocation from supporters, insisting that political leaders must remain focused on the bigger picture.

“I want to ask leaders in the Opposition, be careful. Don't listen to overzealous supporters and influencers; they will lead you astray. Remain focused,” he warned.

On the question of selecting a joint presidential candidate, Gachagua revealed that differences remained over the appropriate timing, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka proposing that the flagbearer be identified before December, while Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna favoured February and Narc Kenya leader Martha Karua suggested May.

Gachagua, however, argued that selecting a candidate too early could expose the individual to political pressure and possible frustration from the government.

He proposed April next year as a more suitable time, maintaining that the coalition was united on the principle of having one candidate even if its leaders differed on the timing.

The DCP leader also dismissed arguments that academic qualifications, experience or political credentials should determine who becomes the coalition's presidential candidate, insisting that electoral numbers and the support of ordinary Kenyans would ultimately decide.

“As others say they have experience and an agenda in the Opposition, the deciding factor is the numbers. I'm with the people. You say you have capacity, but the person to decide is the voter,” he said.

He added: “Akili nyingi ni nzuri, but bila kura unaweza kaa nayo nyumbani.”

World.title: Mudavadi urges Western Kenya to unite, says region cannot remain on sidelines
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi. [File, Standard]

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi has urged Western Kenya to unite ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying the region must strengthen its political representation to have a greater say in national decision-making.

Speaking during a UDA delegates' meeting in Shitoto village, Mumias East, Kakamega County, he said Western Kenya could not afford to remain on the sidelines while decisions affecting the country were being made.

"2027 is the moment we must change the narrative. We must make sure that we are at the table where decisions are made. We cannot afford to remain spectators when the future of our country and our region is being determined," he said.

Mudavadi said parliamentary influence depended on numbers, arguing that electing more MPs would give the region a stronger voice in key parliamentary committees, including the Budget Committee.

"Parliament exercises authority in its own right. We want more MPs so that we can have a say in the Budget Committee and other important committees. These positions are secured through numbers, and numbers matter when decisions affecting the country are being made," he said.

Turning to the opposition, Mudavadi described its leaders as divided and challenged them to present clear manifestos outlining what they would offer Kenyans.

He said the divisions within the opposition would work in President William Ruto's favour as he seeks re-election in 2027, expressing confidence that he would win in the first round.

"We want Ruto to win without a petition. We want to thrash them in the first round," he said.

World.title: Family identifies two security officers involved in Abshir Abdi abduction
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

LSK president Charles Kanjama leads members in a protest over the disappearance of lawyer Abshir Abdi. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The family of Nairobi lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi has identified two security officers alleged to have taken part in their kin's abduction, even as his colleagues threatened mass protests to push for his release.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) said the two names have been forwarded to the police to aid in investigations and demanded that the office of the Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, speed up the probe into the abduction.

"One is named Siad and the other is Hussein, and we want them released for investigation, arrest, prosecution, conviction, sentencing and imprisonment," said LSK.

The revelation came during a demonstration led by (LSK outside the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police and other towns yesterday .

Abshir was forcibly taken on November 1 along Muchai Road, his vehicle was pursued and intercepted by armed individuals in two vehicles before he was seized.

While state security agencies have denied holding him in custody, court filings and colleagues suggest his abduction may be connected to his professional work representing clients in high-profile cases involving senior police officers.

Furthermore, the LSK presented additional names of security personnel linked to the incident, demanding immediate legal action against Chief Inspector Vitalis Kibet, Inspector Kennedy Kimani Karanja, Siad Mohammed, Abdurahman of the Anti-Terrorism Police Unit (ATPU), and KDF officer Ali Hussein.

The leadership voiced their frustration over the state's inaction and the alarming pattern of extrajudicial actions targeting officers of the court. Representatives insisted that lawyers must be allowed to execute their duties without fear of intimidation, torture, or abduction.

"We demand that the officers involved be handed over, arrested, prosecuted, and convicted. We will stand in the courts, in the streets, and in the boardrooms until abductions come to an end," they said in a statement.

The LSK has issued a stern ultimatum to the police command, including the president, DIG Gilbert Masengeli, Inspector General Douglas Kanja, and senior commanders. If Abshir is not released safely and the identified suspects are not formally charged in court by Monday, the LSK warned it will initiate private prosecutions itself.

Furthermore, the society threatened to bring activities to a complete shutdown and demand the immediate resignation of Kanja, Masingeli and Minister for Security Kipchumba Murkomen, carrying their demonstrations to Parliament and State House if necessary.

As court proceedings continue under a habeas corpus application at the Milimani High Court, the legal fraternity remains resolute: the protest at Jogoo House is merely the beginning of an unyielding campaign for justice and the rule of law.

In Nakuru, lawyers protested within the Law Courts, calling for his production.

“It is shocking that one of our colleagues was picked and today we do not know where he is. Unless we voice our concern, there will be complete lawlessness in the country,” said LSK member Ekaterina Handa. “Our lives matter and silencing lawyers is silencing justice. we will not relent until we get justice.”

Rift Valley LSK Chair Wangari Mwangi said it was shocking that the alleged abduction was captured on CCTV.

She rubbished the narrative that the missing lawyer was involved in a crime syndicate, maintaining that he should have been arrested and charged in court. [Additional reporting by Daniel Chege]

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Scientific records document 5 species of whales in Egypt’s Red Sea
World.content:
The recent circulation of videos showing a massive whale near Umm Qamar Island, north of Hurghada, has renewed interest in what types of whales inhabit the Red Sea—a range stretching from the Gulf of Aqaba in the north, past Hurghada, Safaga, and Quseir, down to the areas of Shalateen and Abu Fandira in the south.

Questions have arisen regarding the nature of their presence, the species previously observed, and whether the Red Sea serves as a migratory corridor, a foraging ground, or merely a temporary stopover for them.

The Red Sea Protected Areas Authority explained that this incident is significant because it aligns with existing scientific records documenting various whale species in the Egyptian Red Sea—some of which appear repeatedly in specific locations, while others have only been sighted on rare occasions.

Five major species

Scientific records indicate the presence of five whale species in the Egyptian waters of the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba – including the humpback whale, Bryde’s whale, Omura’s whale, the pygmy blue whale, and the killer whale, also known as the orca.

The humpback whale stands out as one of the species that has particularly captured the interest of both maritime professionals and researchers.

Sightings were recorded in various locations during the years 2006, 2009, 2011, 2016, and 2021.

Humpback whales are known for behaviors such as breaching—leaping above the water’s surface—and producing complex vocalizations. They also undertake long seasonal migrations between their feeding and breeding grounds.

Their appearance in the Red Sea is a scientifically significant event, warranting the documentation of the time and location of the sighting, as well as prevailing environmental conditions.

There are both historical and relatively recent records of the Bryde’s Whale in the Red Sea, dating back to 1950, 2008, 2009, and 2012.

This species belongs to the group of baleen whales, which feed by filtering small marine organisms and fish from the water using baleen plates—located inside the mouth—instead of teeth.

The Omura’s whale is another species whose sightings hold particular scientific significance. Its appearance near Safaga in 2009 drew considerable interest from researchers, given the rarity of such records in the region. Its presence in the Red Sea has prompted scientific questions regarding the species’ distribution range and migratory movements.

Records also document the appearance of a pygmy blue whale near Taba, in the Gulf of Aqaba, in 2018—a finding that underscores the importance of the northern Red Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba as areas warranting further monitoring and study.

Rare sightings

Additionally, records include an instance involving an orca (killer whale) that stranded near the Abu Galum area in South Sinai in 2017.

Such incidents highlight the importance of documenting marine mammal occurrences—whether through live sightings or cases of stranding and mortality—as they provide valuable data on species distribution, as well as their health and environmental status.

Historical records and references point to even earlier accounts of whales in the Red Sea, dating back to 1878 and 1893.

This indicates that the presence of these creatures in the region is not a new phenomenon, but rather one that requires a comprehensive scientific analysis—linking historical records with modern-day observations.

A specialized scientific review titled “Cetaceans of the Red Sea”—published as part of the technical series for the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals—confirms that 16 species of cetaceans have been recorded in the Red Sea, including three species of baleen whales and 13 species of dolphins and toothed whales.

The Director General of the Red Sea Protected Areas, Ahmed Ghallab, noted that some of these whale species are regularly present in the Red Sea, while others appear only intermittently as transient visitors from the Indian Ocean.

And the Director of the Northern Islands Protected Area, Abdallah Abed, emphasized that these frequent yet rare whale sightings necessitate the development of a more comprehensive national system for monitoring marine mammals in the Red Sea.

This would involve establishing a unified database to record the locations and dates of whale and dolphin sightings, as well as the species identified, he said.

The database would also archive photographs, video footage, and relevant data for each encounter, which would then be subject to specialized scientific review.

World.title: Egypt inaugurates 15th of May shelter for stray dogs – here’s everything you need to know
World.content:
In response to the prevalence of stray dogs on across Egypt’s streets, the Cairo Governorate has officially announced new measures to humanely address the issue through scientific means.

These efforts aim to protect citizens and mitigate health risks, while ensuring that animals are not harmed or subjected to arbitrary, unorganized handling.

The inauguration of a model shelter for stray dogs in the industrial zone of the 15th of May City marks a new step in the governorate’s strategy to manage the situation.

Plans are also underway to establish another shelter in the 5th Settlement area, with the goal of covering various parts of the capital and facilitating a more efficient response to reports from the public.

A Model Shelter

The Cairo Governorate opened its first model shelter for stray dogs in the industrial zone of 15 May City.

Spanning a total area of ​​5,000 square meters, the facility has a capacity of over 700 dogs and features specialized enclosures designed to house the animals and provide them with the necessary care.

The shelter includes fully equipped veterinary clinics for medical examinations, sterilization procedures, and rabies vaccinations. It also provides designated areas for treatment and temporary housing during recovery, alongside nutritional support and healthcare delivered by veterinarians and trained staff.

The shelter implements the trap-neuter-vaccinate-release program, which involves identifying, examining, vaccinating, and sterilizing stray dogs.

Once confirmed to be healthy, the animals are released back into their original environment, in accordance with established veterinary protocols.

Reporting Stray Dogs

In coordination with the Veterinary Medicine Directorate, the Cairo Governorate has designated hotlines for citizens to submit complaints or reports regarding groups of stray dogs, enabling the relevant authorities to intervene and address the situation appropriately.

World.title: Egypt to construct new solar power plant in Aswan’s Benban Complex for US$127 million
World.content:
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the German development finance institution DEG announced a joint financing package of up to US$ 127 million for the construction of a solar power plant equipped with a battery energy storage system at Benban complex in Aswan.

The EBRD’s share of the financing amounts to $ 63.5 million, with DEG providing the remainder, bringing the total value to $127 million.

The project aims to enhance Egypt’s clean energy production capacity and support the stability of the national electricity grid by storing solar energy generated during the day for use during evening peak hours.

This contributes to reducing reliance on conventional fuels and lowering carbon emissions.

One of the largest solar energy complexes

The Benban Solar Park in Aswan is one of the largest solar energy complexes in the world and stands as a key project within Egypt’s strategy to transition toward renewable energy, with the goal of increasing its share in the national energy mix to 42 percent by 2030.

This new funding comes as part of international institutions’ support for green finance in Egypt, aimed at strengthening public-private partnerships in sustainable infrastructure projects and attracting further foreign investment into the renewable energy sector.

The project is expected to create job opportunities during both the construction and operational phases, support national efforts to meet the growing demand for electricity—particularly in the governorates of Upper Egypt—and enhance the efficiency with which the abundant solar resources in Aswan are utilized.

World.title: Cool, rainy weather expected for Egypt on Tuesday
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) expects a noticeable drop in temperatures across the country on Tuesday. The weather will be mild—typical of autumn—during the day, turning cold at night and in the early morning.

These conditions coincide with a chance of rain along the northern coasts, while active winds will make the weather feel even colder, especially during the evening and nighttime hours.

Expected temperatures for Tuesday:

Greater Cairo: High 23C, Low 14C

High 23C, Low 14C Alexandria : High 23C, Low 17C

: High 23C, Low 17C Matrouh: High 21C, Low 16C

High 21C, Low 16C Sharm el-Sheikh: High 27C, Low 19C

High 27C, Low 19C Hurghada: High 26C, Low 18C

High 26C, Low 18C Fayoum: High 24C, Low 13C

High 24C, Low 13C Minya: High 25C, Low 11C

High 25C, Low 11C Assiut: High 24C, Low 12C

High 24C, Low 12C Luxor and Aswan: High 28C, Low 14C

Rains and Wind

The EMA forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of rain along the northern coasts and northern Lower Egypt. The rainfall is expected to be light, occasionally becoming moderate, with a probability of approximately 30 percent.

There is also a very slight 10 percent chance of light rain in scattered areas across southern Lower Egypt and Suez Canal cities, potentially extending to parts of Greater Cairo.

Winds will occasionally pick up, reaching speeds between 30-40 km/h across most regions, which will enhance the feeling of cold weather.

In parts of the Red Sea region and the New Valley, these winds may also stir up sand and dust.

Disruption to Maritime Navigation

The EMA issued a warning regarding disrupted maritime navigation along parts of the Red Sea coast, as well as the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba.

Wind speeds in these areas are expected to range between 40-70 km/h, with wave heights reaching 2.5 to 3.5 meters.

Conditions in the Mediterranean Sea will be moderate, with wave heights between 1.5 and two meters.

The EMA advises citizens to carry a jacket or extra clothing when going out at night or during late hours to avoid catching a cold, given the current weather fluctuations and chilly nighttime temperatures.

Furthermore, motorists are urged to exercise caution while driving during the morning hours due to the presence of mist, and to stay updated with the latest weather reports.
