World.title: Liberia: Ganta Delegates  Agreed and Signed  Resolution Setting Out Recommendations for a Broad National Review of Liberia’s  1986 Constitution
World.content:
GANTA, Nimba County — Delegates, who attended Liberia’s three-day National Constitutional Reform Symposium in Ganta City, Nimba County, have agreed and signed a resolution setting out their recommendations for a broad national review of the country’s 1986 Constitution.

By Franklin Doloquee

The proposed resolution will provide a basis for wider consultations on whether Liberia should amend specific constitutional provisions or pursue a more comprehensive rewriting of the 40-year-old document.



The agreement to prepare the resolution does not in itself constitute a final national decision to replace the Constitution.

Once finalized, the document is expected to be presented for consideration by the Executive Branch, the Judiciary, the House of Representatives, the Senate, civil-society organizations, traditional chiefs and elders, the media, youth organizations, women’s groups, People living with disability, organizations representing persons with disabilities, political parties representations, Superintendents Council representations, counties nine men council members and other stakeholders.

Delegates emphasized that the future of the Constitution should not be determined solely by political leaders, legal experts or participants at a single gathering.

Instead, they called for an inclusive, transparent, and nationally owned process that gives Liberians across all 15 counties a meaningful opportunity to contribute.

Building National Agreement

The symposium was convened by the Governance Commission and the Law Reform Commission, with support from the United Nations Development Programme, ( UNDP) under the theme: “Advancing Constitutional Reform through National Ownership, Inclusion and Democratic Governance.”

Participants included representatives of government ministries and agencies, lawmakers, lawyers, civil-society organizations, professional bodies, traditional authorities, women, young people and persons with disabilities.

Their agreement to develop a resolution marks a step toward consolidating the discussions into a common document.

The resolution is intended to bring together areas of agreement, identify questions requiring further examination and outline a possible direction for nationwide engagement.

At the center of the proposed national review is a fundamental question: can targeted amendments adequately address Liberia’s present governance challenges, or is a more comprehensive constitutional overhaul necessary?

That question remains open for wider public discussion and legal examination.

The delegates’ recommendations are, therefore, intended to inform a national decision, rather than substitute for one.

A Constitution at 40

As Liberia marks four decades under its 1986 Constitution, participants said the country must assess whether its constitutional framework adequately reflects contemporary political, social, economic and governance realities.

The discussions focused on preserving democratic principles while examining provisions that participants believe may require clarification, stronger safeguards, or reform.

Delegates linked the review to public concerns about accountability, citizen participation, local governance, institutional independence and the equitable management of national resources.

The Ganta gathering also forms part of a broader reform conversation. Earlier national discussions organized by the Governance Commission and Law Reform Commission examined the choice between targeted constitutional revision and a more comprehensive overhaul.

Priorities for Reform

During thematic discussions, delegates identified several areas for possible constitutional and legal review: Citizenship and property rights, Natural-resource governance and equitable benefit-sharing, Decentralization, local government and citizen participation.

The tenure, accountability and performance of elected officials. Traditional authority, customary rights, and their relationship with state institutions. Checks and balances among the Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary.

Fundamental rights, inclusion and public accountability. These issues extend beyond the wording of the Constitution.

They concern how public authority is exercised, how communities participate in decisions, how institutions are held accountable and how citizens benefit from the country’s resources.

Participants said the review should ultimately contribute to stronger democratic institutions, improved public-service delivery, social cohesion, and greater confidence in government.

Delegates stressed that consultation must reach beyond national institutions and urban centers.

Their call for participation across all 15 counties places communities, local leaders, and groups whose voices are often underrepresented at the center of the proposed process.

The inclusion of women, young people, persons with disabilities, traditional authorities and civil-society organizations is intended to broaden the range of experiences informing the review.

For that participation to be meaningful, the consultation process would need accessible information, understandable explanations of proposed changes, and opportunities for citizens to raise concerns before decisions are finalized.

The media would also have an important public-information role. At the Ganta symposium, the Press Union of Liberia called for an inclusive reform process and stronger constitutional protection for freedom of expression, press freedom and other fundamental rights.

Calls for Stronger Institutions

Governance Commission Acting Chairman Professor Alaric K. Tokpa has urged that constitutional reform remain nationally owned, inclusive, and focused on practical improvements in governance.

His emphasis on public participation reflects the broader argument that reform should strengthen the relationship between citizens and state institutions, rather than become an exercise confined to political and legal circles.

Civil Service Agency Director-General Dr. Josiah F. Joekai, who delivered the symposium’s keynote address, called for reforms addressing excessive political influence, institutional weaknesses, and inadequate accountability.

He identified stronger checks and balances, decentralization, protection of fundamental rights, inclusive participation, and responsible management of public resources as priorities, while advocating nationwide consultations and technical review of proposed amendments.

From Resolution to Reform

The proposed Ganta resolution is expected to guide further consultations, stakeholder engagement and technical legal review. It would provide a platform for national institutions and the public to consider both the substance of reform and the appropriate process for pursuing it.

However, a symposium resolution cannot itself amend the Constitution. Article 91 requires a proposed amendment to receive the support of two-thirds of the membership of each legislative chamber and subsequent approval by two-thirds of registered voters voting in a referendum held no sooner than one year after legislative action.

Citizens may also initiate the process through a petition signed by at least 10,000 citizens, but the proposal must still secure the required legislative concurrence and referendum approval.

Article 92 further requires proposed amendments to be published, explained to the public, and presented separately when more than one amendment is submitted for a referendum.

Any proposal for a comprehensive rewriting would therefore require careful legal examination; the delegates’ agreement to draft a resolution should not be presented as authorization to replace the Constitution. For the Ganta participants, the immediate task is to turn their discussions into a document that Liberians can examine, debate, and help shape.

Their stated objective is a constitutional framework that responses to present-day needs while protecting democratic values, national unity, the rule of law and the long-term interests of the Liberian people.

World.title: BRE calls for cattle vaccination in Western
World.content:
The Barotse Royal Establishment (BRE) has expressed concern over the low levels of cattle vaccination in Western Province.

BRE Induna Meimanene, says preventable livestock diseases continue to threaten the region’s cattle population and the livelihoods of farmers.

Induna Meimanene said cattle remains one of the major sources of income and livelihood for many people in the province stating that regular vaccination is essential to safeguarding the livestock sector.

Speaking shortly after Western Province Provincial Minister Kapelwa Mbangweta paid a courtesy call on the Limulunga Kuta, Induna Meimanene observed that despite Government’s efforts to promote increased beef production, some farmers continue to lose their animals to preventable diseases.

He has, therefore, called for strengthened veterinary services and increased vaccination coverage to protect livestock and support the growth of the livestock industry in the province.

Meanwhile, Mr Mbangweta has reaffirmed Government’s commitment to working closely with traditional leadership in advancing development across the province.

He said traditional leaders play an important role in mobilising communities and promoting national development, adding that their involvement was essential to achieving the country’s economic growth aspirations under the Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda.

Mr Mbangweta said Government recognises the importance of traditional institutions as key partners in implementing development programmes and improving the welfare of local communities.

After paying a courtesy call at the Kuta, Mr Mbangweta later interacted with United Party for National Development (UPND) members at the Limulunga Market.

During the interaction, Mr Mbangweta thanked the people of Limulunga for their continued support and for re-electing President Hakainde Hichilema in the August 13, 2026 general elections.

He urged party members to remain united and work together in supporting Government’s development agenda.

And UPND member, Lungowe Munalula expressed happiness over Mr Mbangweta’s reappointment as Provincial Minister, pledging her support and commitment to working with him in promoting development in the province.

World.title: Mwanakampwe urges increased support to small-scale miners
World.content:
Central Province Permanent Secretary, Milner Mwanakampwe has called for increased support towards artisanal and small-scale miners to enable them contribute meaningfully to economic growth and national development.

Dr Mwanakampwe, says the subsector has the potential to increase mineral production, create employment, reduce poverty and promote economic diversification if challenges affecting its operations are addressed.

He said this through Central Provincial Assistant Director of Planning, Justin Kapenda, during the opening of the stakeholders’ consultative meeting on the Draft guidelines for the artisanal and small scale mining fund in Kabwe.

Dr Mwanakampwe said artisanal and small-scale mining plays an important role in creating economic opportunities, particularly for citizens in rural and mineral-rich communities, by providing livelihoods and supporting local economic activities.

He stated that limited access to affordable financing, inadequate mining equipment, insufficient technical and geological information, and low levels of mechanisation are among the major challenges affecting the artisanal miners.

World.title: Tambatamba urges ZCCM-IH employees to work hard
World.content:
Minister of Mines and Minerals Development, Brenda Tambatamba has called on ZCCM-IH employees to work collectively towards achieving the country’s target of producing three (3) million metric tons of Copper.

Ms Tambatamba says teamwork, right mindset and effective coordination among employees are critical to translating the Grow Zambia Agenda into tangible results.

She said this during a familiarisation visit to ZCCM-IH offices in Lusaka, where she called for teamwork and accountability.

Ms Tambatamba noted that ZCCM-IH, as an important institution in the country’s mining sector, has a significant responsibility to contribute to the government’s economic aspirations.

The Minister commended ZCCM-IH for its resilience and contribution to the mining sector, expressing confidence in its capacity to support the three million metric tons Copper target.

“Every one of us has a role to play to take ownership of the responsibilities in advancing the national development agenda,” she said.

Speaking at the same event, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development, Hapenga Kabeta, explained that clear strategies are essential in providing direction and ensuring institutions contribute to national development.

Dr Kabeta stressed that institutions and individuals must work towards a common national vision, noting that every task should support the Growth Zambia Agenda.

“If what you are doing is not contributing to the Grow Zambia Agenda, you are in the wrong place,” he said.

He urged employees to create an enabling environment that supports the implementation of institutional strategies and national priorities.

Meanwhile, ZCCM-IH Chief Executive Officer, Kakenenwa Muyangwa, disclosed that ZCCM-IH is expected to adopt a 10-year strategic plan next week aimed at repositioning the company for greater growth and an expanded role in the mining and energy sectors.

Chief Executive Officer added that the strategy will strengthen the company’s capacity to contribute to national development and support the government’s Growth Zambia Agenda.

“We have a 10-year strategy which will position this company at a different scale and stature,” he said.

World.title: Traditional leaders urged to support Lumezi dam project
World.content:
Lumezi District Commissioner (DC), Patrick Mtonga, says the Lumezi dam project in Chamtowa ward is expected to unlock economic opportunities for local communities through fish farming, crop irrigation and livestock farming.

Brigadier General Mtonga (Retired) has urged headmen in the area to identify and release suitable portions of land around the dam for the development of fish ponds, irrigated crop fields and designated livestock watering points.

The DC said this during a community engagement meeting attended by officials from the Ministry of Water Development and Sanitation under the Provincial Administration.

He said the land identification exercise should be guided by a participatory land-use planning approach to ensure that local communities actively contribute to maximising the benefits of the dam.

“You must be aware that the land being identified is not intended for the District Administration or unintended for individuals to benefit but should be utilised by local communities to support their economic activities and livelihoods,” he said.

He said the target community already expressed willingness to participate in initiatives aimed at ensuring that the district derives maximum benefits from the investment.

Meanwhile, Chief Zumwanda’s Induna, Alfred Phiri, urged headmen to convene a meeting and expedite the identification of suitable land for the proposed activities.

Mr Phiri said the development will benefit locals, calling on traditional leaders to act swiftly to ensure that the planned initiatives were implemented.

World.title: Barbra Banda toasts FIFPRO Women honour
World.content:
Zambia’s Copper Queens striker and skipper Barbra Banda says she feels extra special Happy to have made it to the 2026 FIFPRO Women’s World11.

Banda is the only African in the World best 11 and the only player based outside England and Spain to have made the cut.

It’s her 3rd consecutive FIFPRO Women’s World11 selection – the first African woman to achieve that feat.

Posting on her official Facebook page, Banda said she was grateful for the recognition by fellow players.

“Happy to have made it to the 2026 FIFPRO Women’s World11,” Banda wrote.

“It’s extra special given that it is chosen by 6,511 professional women’s footballers worldwide. Thank you, I am grateful,” she reacted.

England and Spain dominate the team with 5 players each, with Hannah Hampton in goal, Lucy Bronze making a record ninth appearance, and Barcelona stars Bonmatí and Putellas in midfield.

It’s the only global football award voted exclusively by players.

The 2026 FIFPRO Women’s World11, chosen by 6,511 professional women’s footballers worldwide.

World.title: One plastic bottle, four cigarettes: what the 2027 Budget forgot
World.content:
One plastic bottle, four cigarettes: what the 2027 Budget forgot

By Dennis Tembo

On Friday afternoon, as the Minister of Finance rose to read the 2027 Budget, somewhere in Lusaka a boy was on his way to write an exam paper, with a few coins in his pocket, the kind meant for a fritter or a freezit, the kind the older boys at the corner know he carries. “Mwaiche, give us chi coin,” they said, and he handed it over, because that is how it goes. He walked into the exam room with empty pockets, and by evening that coin had become a single cigarette, bought loose a few steps from the school gate. The Budget had nothing to say to him.

It had something to say about almost everything else. From January, a kilogram of sugar will carry an excise duty of K1, chocolates and sweets will be taxed at 20 percent, and every plastic bottle will pay 80 ngwee, because these things harm our health and our environment. VAT rises to 16.5 percent from 16 percent and the mobile money levy goes up across all bands. The cigarette, which harms health more surely than any of them, was not mentioned once.

That silence has a history. Since January 2016, under the Customs and Excise (Amendment) Act No. 18 of 2015, cigarettes made in Zambia have paid only a quarter of the full excise rate, with no conditions and no end date. Today the full rate is K750 per 1,000 sticks, K15 on a pack of 20, while a locally made pack pays K3.75. Break it down to the single stick the boy at the corner buys, and the excise is about 19 ngwee, which means that from January, one plastic bottle will carry more excise than four locally made cigarettes.

These are the cigarettes most Zambians smoke. Tracing the excise from 2008 to 2025 through Zambia’s own legislation and World Health Organization data shows that the tax on the most sold brand lost 79 percent of its real value between 2008 and 2024, and by 2024 made up just 5 percent of its price, against the 70 percent the WHO recommends. The pack stayed at about K20 for years, so the discount never reached smokers as a lower price; it stayed with the industry, and the Treasury went without.

Inflation finished what the discount started. The same 2015 Act gave the Commissioner-General power to adjust specific duties for inflation, a power that has never been used. In 2025, Parliament finally moved, adjusting the rate for inflation in January and raising it by 66 percent in August. But the adjustment was not repeated in 2026, and Friday’s Budget proposes none for 2027, even with inflation down to 6.3 percent, when adjusting the rate is easiest. Meanwhile every increase widens the gap: the August rise added K7 of excise to an imported pack and only K1.75 to a local one.

A 2024 survey of 475 retailers near schools, playgrounds and game zones in Lusaka and Chongwe found that 93 percent sold single sticks. A child does not buy a pack. A child buys one stick, with whatever coins they have, or with the coins someone took from them on the way.

Kenya chose another road, taxing all cigarettes at one rate and adjusting it for inflation, and smoking among Kenyan men fell by about a third between 2014 and 2022, while in Zambia it fell only modestly. Tax is not the whole story, but it is a large part of it.

None of this needs new money, only three decisions. End the discount for local manufacturers; at August 2025 rates, charging the most sold brand the full rate would multiply the excise collected on it by about 3.5, even after smokers cut back. Index every specific rate to inflation and income growth every year, by rule rather than by mood. And when Parliament reconsiders the Tobacco Control Bill, ban the sale of single sticks.

The Customs and Excise (Amendment) Bill that will carry Friday’s measures has not yet passed, and there is still room in it for one more line. A Government ready to tax a packet of sweets to protect our health can surely tax the cigarette sold at the school gate, before the boy with the coins becomes the man who cannot stop.

Dennis Tembo is an economics graduate of the University of Zambia, an independent tobacco control researcher and a spoken word poet based in Lusaka.

World.title: State’s Undisclosed Objection Stalls Mundubile, Makebi Sedition Bail As Sikota Cries Delay
World.content:
The Lusaka High Court has adjourned to Monday the bail application of opposition leader Mr Brian Mundubile and his former running mate Mr Makebi Zulu. The State asked to raise a preliminary objection first, without saying what it was.

The two, who are charged with two counts of seditious practices over statements on the outcome of the presidential election, remain in custody while the bail application and jurisdictional issues are resolved.

When the matter came up in chambers before a three-judge panel led by Justice Geoffrey Mulenga, the State told the court it intended to raise preliminary issues before the bail application could be heard.

The State gave no indication of the grounds it intends to argue. The court granted its request, directed it to file its preliminary application, and set the matter down for hearing on Monday.

Defence lawyer Mr Sakwiba Sikota, State Counsel, expressed concern at the failure to proceed with the substantive bail hearing. He said the application had been before the court but had not yet been heard.

Mr Sikota went further, accusing the State of employing delaying tactics in the matter.

The sedition charges are brought under Section 57 of the Penal Code. They arise from events on August 14, 2026, the day after polling.

The prosecution alleges that the two acted together and published material through livestreams on their respective Facebook pages. In those broadcasts, they allegedly claimed that their Parallel Voter Tabulation (PVT) showed their party had won the presidential election and a majority of parliamentary seats.

In the first count, Mr Mundubile is alleged to have called on the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) to announce the winner of the election using the PVT results.

The second count is directed at Mr Zulu. He is alleged to have announced on Facebook that Mr Mundubile would address the nation at a scheduled time.

The State further alleges that the pair questioned the delay in the announcement and verification of the presidential results and called for their immediate publication. They are also accused of demanding access to electoral records to allow the results to be verified independently.

The case has already travelled across two provinces before reaching the capital. Mr Mundubile and Mr Zulu were first arraigned before a magistrate’s court in Solwezi, North-Western Province.

Before trial could begin, the defence challenged the court’s jurisdiction. They argued that the alleged offences were committed in Lusaka and that both men were arrested in the capital.

Solwezi Principal Resident Magistrate Mr Mambwe Mukonde referred the question to the High Court. On November 5, Solwezi High Court Judge Mr Edward Musona ordered that the matter be moved to the Lusaka High Court, after establishing that both accused were Lusaka residents who had been arrested in Lusaka.

The transfer brought the bail application before the three-judge panel in Lusaka. It has now stalled again at the first hurdle.

The sedition case is one of two legal fronts facing the opposition leaders. Mr Mundubile and Mr Zulu are also among 18 people facing treason-related charges, in which they have separately applied to the High Court for constitutional bail.

Their detention has drawn in others from the opposition camp. Former Zambian Ambassador to Switzerland Ms Martha Lungu Mwitumwa, who was active in the Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance campaign team, has been charged with treason, as has her daughter Ms Esther Mwitumwa, an administrator at the Tonse Alliance Secretariat.

For now, the sedition bail application turns on the State’s yet-to-be-filed objection. Once it is filed, the defence will see for the first time the grounds on which the State wants the bail application stopped before it is heard.

Mr Mundubile and Mr Zulu return to the Lusaka High Court on Monday, when the panel led by Justice Mulenga is due to hear the State’s preliminary application.

World.title: EU Offers To Back National Dialogue And Reconciliation, Presses Government On Access To Justice
World.content:
The European Union (EU) has offered to support a nationally led dialogue and reconciliation process in Zambia. It also told Government it remains concerned about access to justice, civic space and respect for fundamental freedoms following the August elections.

The offer was made in Lusaka at the extraordinary Zambia-EU Partnership Dialogue at Mulungushi International Conference Centre. Zambia requested the meeting to address challenges arising from the general elections and from a European Parliament resolution on the electoral process.

European External Action Service (EEAS) Director for Africa Ms Francesca Di Mauro said any such process would be Zambia’s to own, with the EU offering support only on terms set by the country’s own institutions.

“Should the Zambian authorities consider it useful, the EU would be ready to support a nationally led process for dialogue and reconciliation, in full respect of Zambia’s ownership, institutions and democratic processes,” Ms Di Mauro said.

The offer came with a clear statement of where Brussels stands. Ms Di Mauro said the EU remained concerned about issues raised at home and abroad over access to justice, transparency, civic space and respect for fundamental freedoms.

She said the bloc recognised that there were no perfect democracies, but stressed that disputes from the polls must be settled openly before impartial courts.

“We strongly believe that electoral grievances should be addressed with transparency through fair and impartial judicial process, in full respect of constitutional rights and responsibilities of citizens and institutions involved,” she said.

Justice Minister Mr Jack Mwiimbu and Home Affairs and Internal Security Minister Mr Clement Andeleki attended the meeting, which Ms Di Mauro described as an opportunity for an open exchange on electoral governance and the post-election situation.

The EU envoy also stood by the work of its Election Observation Mission (EOM). She said it had delivered an independent and impartial assessment of the electoral process, with recommendations aimed at correcting identified shortcomings before future elections.

“The EOM chief observer visited Zambia last week and presented the final report and the recommendations to the government and the electoral stakeholders,” Ms Di Mauro said.

She said the EU was ready to help Government and other electoral players implement the recommendations of its mission, as well as those of other observer missions, to strengthen democratic institutions.

Responding for Government, Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Minister Mr Mulambo Haimbe said Zambia valued the mission’s findings. He said Government would, however, have preferred a formal opportunity to review them before the report went public.

“We wish to underscore the importance of continued engagement between the mission and the government of the Republic of Zambia, including the opportunity for the government to formally consider and provide observations on the findings and recommendations of the Final Report prior to its public release,” Mr Haimbe said.

The minister said such an arrangement would have encouraged constructive engagement and ensured that Government’s perspectives and clarifications were considered in assessing the country’s electoral environment.

“We believe that such engagement would contribute to a balanced appreciation of the electoral environment,” he said.

Mr Haimbe said the findings were important in identifying areas that needed improvement, particularly electoral administration, institutional capacity, transparency and public confidence in the electoral process.

He said Government was ready to engage the EU in good faith on the recommendations. Any changes, he said, must be guided by the Constitution, national laws and the country’s international obligations.

“It is our expectation that this engagement will continue to be guided by mutual respect, transparency and a shared commitment to strengthening democratic governance and institutions in Zambia,” Mr Haimbe said.

Earlier, Ministry of Foreign Affairs Permanent Secretary for International Relations and Cooperation Ms Etambuyu Gundersen said the August elections had demonstrated the maturity of Zambia’s democracy and the resilience of its institutions.

Beyond the electoral questions, Mr Haimbe said Zambia regarded the EU as a strategic partner in advancing the Grow Zambia Agenda, with room for deeper collaboration in mining, agriculture, energy, tourism, manufacturing and infrastructure.

He said Government wanted to work with the bloc and its member states to mobilise investment, improve market access for Zambian products, facilitate technology transfer and develop sustainable value chains, in line with the EU’s Global Gateway Strategy.

Ms Di Mauro congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election for a second term and welcomed the newly appointed and returning Cabinet and parliamentary members.

She said the EU remained a reliable, long-term partner whose relationship with Zambia, spanning more than 50 years, was anchored in democracy, the rule of law, transparency and respect for human rights. Team Europe invests more than €200 million in Zambia every year, and the EU has provided over €650 million in grants between 2021 and 2027.

The reconciliation offer now rests with Government. The EU has said it will back a dialogue process only if Zambian authorities consider it useful. Lusaka has committed to continued engagement on the mission’s recommendations, within the bounds of the Constitution and national law.

World.title: Two ZIMRA officers arrested over fraudulent clearance of luxury vehicles
World.content:
TWO Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) officers stationed at the Plumtree Border Post have been arrested by the Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission (ZACC) for allegedly falsifying border exit documents to cover up for two smuggled ultra-luxury vehicles recovered in Harare last week.

Edwin Mhondiwa Chabuda and Upenyu Chaurura face serious charges of criminal abuse of duty as public officers.

According to details released by ZACC, the duo fraudulently processed and certified that a high-performance Lamborghini Urus and a Mercedes-Benz GLE 53 had exited Zimbabwe through the Plumtree Border Post.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 10, 2026
World.content:
Nine Zimbabweans Arrested Over Alleged Russia-Ukraine War Recruitment

Nine Zimbabwean nationals have been arrested in South Africa on suspicion of attempting to travel abroad to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war. The suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in Johannesburg. Five were detained at OR Tambo International Airport and four at a hotel in Bruma. They face charges under South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which prohibits unauthorised mercenary activities. Authorities have not disclosed whether the group intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine, or which organisations allegedly facilitated their recruitment. The arrests come amid growing concern over the recruitment of African nationals into the conflict. Zimbabwe previously reported that several of its citizens had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia. South Africa has also helped repatriate citizens allegedly tricked into joining the war.

Kenya Seizes $27 Million Methamphetamine Haul in Major Drug Bust

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Kenyan authorities have seized 454 kilograms of methamphetamine worth an estimated 27 million dollars in an operation targeting international drug trafficking networks. Three suspects, two Tanzanians and a Ugandan, were arrested in the coastal region following a joint intelligence-led operation involving Kenyan and Tanzanian anti-narcotics officers. Investigations suggest the network operates across several African countries, including Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa and Mozambique, as well as Afghanistan and the United Arab Emirates. Authorities believe some of the drugs seized in Tanzania may have entered through Kenya's port of Mombasa. The latest seizure is among the largest in Kenya's history and comes amid growing concerns about East Africa's role as both a transit route and destination for illegal drugs. Police said that investigations are continuing, with further arrests possible.

U.S. Deports Rwandan Genocide Suspect Jean Léonard Teganya

The United States has deported Rwandan genocide suspect Jean Léonard Teganya, who was handed over to authorities in Kigali and arrested. The 55-year-old is accused of participating in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, including alleged killings at a hospital and student dormitory in Butare. Teganya was previously convicted in the US in 2019 of immigration fraud and perjury after concealing his alleged involvement in the genocide. Rwanda's National Public Prosecution Authority said that he is the eighth genocide fugitive to be deported to the country from the US since 2007. His American trial focused on immigration offences. However, prosecutors presented evidence linking him to the Interahamwe militia and alleged involvement in the killings. Rwandan authorities say his deportation forms part of ongoing international efforts to ensure accountability for genocide crimes.

21 Killed in Bus and Truck Collision in Tanzania

At least 21 people, including two young boys, have been killed and five others injured in a road crash in Tanzania's Iringa Region. The collision involved a passenger minibus and a cargo truck at Kiponzero Junction along the Iringa-Njombe Highway. Police said that preliminary investigations suggest the minibus driver entered the main highway from a feeder road without ensuring it was safe, resulting in the crash. President Samia Suluhu Hassan has sent condolences to the bereaved families, while the injured are receiving medical treatment. The fatalities comprised 10 men, nine women and two boys aged between three and five. Two of the injured have been transferred to Iringa Regional Referral Hospital for further treatment, while the others remain at a local dispensary.

Ethiopian Families Fleeing to Kenya Face Food, Water and Shelter Shortages

Around 50,000 people have fled violent clashes in Ethiopia and crossed into Kenya's northern Moyale region since late October, prompting calls for urgent humanitarian assistance. The displaced are facing severe shortages of food, clean water, shelter and healthcare, according to an assessment by Kenyan authorities and humanitarian partners. An assessment found that 80 percent of households said their most urgent need was food and 44% did not have adequate access to drinking water. More than half of the displaced are children, adding pressure to already stretched host communities. Most of the arrivals have fled Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regions, with nine in ten households reporting that their entire villages had been displaced. Humanitarian agencies warn that urgent funding is needed to support both the displaced families and the communities hosting them.

Close 

Malawi Unveils Strategy to Tackle Transnational Organised Crime

Malawi is developing a new national strategy to combat organised crime, including human trafficking, cybercrime and cross-border criminal networks. Homeland Security Minister Peter Mukhito says the government will strengthen cooperation between law enforcement agencies and international partners to tackle increasingly sophisticated criminal operations. The proposed strategy includes establishing a National Task Force and developing a clear implementation plan. Police Chief Richard Luhanga says authorities are also investing in specialised training to equip officers to tackle emerging threats, particularly cybercrime. Malawi is among only six countries to develop a dedicated national strategy against transnational organised crime. The government says the framework will provide a coordinated, long-term response to criminal networks that threaten national security, economic stability and public safety.

World.title: South Africa: Matlala Blames Medication for R500K Bribery Claims - South African News Briefs - November 10, 2026
World.content:
press review

Matlala Claims Medication Affected R500K Bribery Statement

Alleged crime kingpin Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala has told the Madlanga Commission that he was heavily medicated and not mentally well when he made statements alleging he paid former police deputy commissioner Shadrack Sibiya R500,000, reports EWN. Matlala has denied making the payments, claiming he gave Sibiya only R50,000 during the SAPS Excellence Awards in KwaZulu-Natal. The statements were part of a failed plea agreement in a R360 million tender fraud case involving his company, Medicare24. Matlala is set to return to the witness stand.

Senzo Meyiwa Trial Continues



Defence witness Thabiso Buthelezi is set to continue testifying in the Senzo Meyiwa murder trial at the Pretoria High Court, reports SABC News. Buthelezi has told the court that his late uncle, Simphiwe Buthelezi, was seriously ill and mentally incapacitated when police allegedly obtained a statement from him in June 2020. He claimed his uncle could barely speak, feed himself, or hold a conversation and therefore was not in a condition to make or sign a statement. The defence is challenging the circumstances surrounding the alleged statement.

UK Triple-Murder Suspect Seeks to Withdraw Guilty Plea

UK fugitive Ndodana Tshuma is set to appear in the Johannesburg Magistrates Court as his extradition to Britain remains delayed, reports EWN. Tshuma, who is wanted over the alleged murders of his wife and two daughters at their London home in July, is seeking to withdraw his guilty plea to charges of possessing an unlicensed firearm and contravening immigration laws. He previously told his lawyer he could not remember signing the plea and sentence agreement, despite weeks of negotiations. The proceedings are expected to determine whether the court will allow him to retract his plea, further affecting the extradition process.
