How Small-Scale Miners Reacted

The federation, which represents small-scale mining groups, welcomed the change. Its president, Joseph Mwansa, said the cut will encourage small-scale miners to sell their gold through legal channels.

The Zambia Revenue Authority, the national tax collector, says in its summary of the budget that the measure is meant to promote participation in the formal gold value chain and to support the growth of the small-scale gold subsector. It sets no target for how much gold should move to approved buyers.

A fountain and office towers in central Lusaka, Zambia’s capital, in December 2013. Photo: Matthew Grollnek / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Why the Condition Matters

The government is using the tax rate as an incentive: miners pay half as much if their gold passes through an approved buyer. As we reported in September, an official at Zambia’s Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development said Zambia was considering a cut in the value added tax (VAT) on gold for the same purpose.

The saving only helps miners who can reach an approved aggregator and who are offered a fair price. We found no published figure for how much gold small miners now sell through such buyers, so the size of the shift is not known.

What Else Is in the Budget for Mining

The same budget proposes a 15% withholding tax on dividends paid by mining companies, up from 0%, and a 5% export duty on zinc concentrates. Our report on the budget covers the wider tax package, including a value added tax (VAT, a sales tax on goods and services) rising to 16.5% from 16%.

For investors in Zambian mining, the budget cuts the cost of one small gold stream while adding costs for larger producers. Background on the country is in our guide to Zambia.

What Is Not Known

The tax document says the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development approves aggregators, but reports do not say how many will operate by January. They also do not say whether the rate for other sales changes.

The budget measures are proposals until Parliament approves the related tax legislation, so the 3% rate could change. More Zambian news is on our Zambia page.

What to Watch Next

The first checkpoint is parliamentary approval of the tax legislation behind the budget, ahead of the planned 1 January 2027 start. The second is the rollout of approved aggregators, which will show whether the lower rate reaches miners in practice.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Zambia changing about gold tax?

Zambia proposes cutting the gold royalty for artisanal and small-scale miners from 6% to 3%. The lower rate applies only to gold sold to government-approved aggregators.

When would the cut start?

The budget’s tax measures are planned to start on 1 January 2027. They are proposals until Zambia’s parliament approves them.

Who benefits from the lower royalty?

Small-scale gold miners who sell to approved aggregators would pay half as much royalty. Miners who sell elsewhere would not get the cut.

World.title: Alleged Tanzanian Drug Kingpin Held in Kenya
World.content:
A container ship unloads at a quay in Tanzania in 2020. Photo: Yeluma Ntali / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

TANZANIA DRUGS

Tanzania’s drug agency says a Tanzanian businessman it calls a key figure in an international trafficking network was arrested in Kenya on Saturday 7 November 2026. The agency names him as Saleh Khamis Baseleman, known as Mbwiga, and says he lives in Mombasa and sourced drugs from Afghanistan.

The agency says he was detained in Kwale County, on Kenya’s Indian Ocean coast, in a joint operation that also seized a large haul of suspected methamphetamine. It describes everyone held as a suspect, and no court has ruled on the allegations.

Key Facts Who: Saleh Khamis Baseleman, known as Mbwiga, a Mombasa businessman, arrested on 7 November 2026, the agency says.

Haul in Kenya: Kenyan police report 454 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine, worth about US$28 million (3.6 billion Kenyan shillings).

Haul in Tanzania: 299 packets of methamphetamine and heroin were found in two Ford Ranger vehicles in Dar es Salaam.

Network: Tanzania’s drug agency says it spans Afghanistan, South Africa, Mozambique, Zambia, Malawi, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Dubai.

Not known: The charges, the court that will try him, and whether he will be sent to Tanzania.

Seven people were arrested after linked raids in Tanzania and Kenya, according to Tanzania’s drug agency. Kenyan police report three arrests linked to the Kwale operation.

Rio Times membership Read everything we publish for US$1 in the first month. Then US$8.99 a month. Cancel anytime. Start for US$1

What Tanzanian Officials Announced

Aretas Lyimo, Commissioner General of Tanzania’s Drug Control and Enforcement Authority (DCEA), briefed the press in Dar es Salaam on Monday 9 November 2026. He said seven people were arrested in a special operation that ran across Tanzania and Kenya.

The case began in Dar es Salaam, where DCEA officers found 299 packets hidden in two Ford Ranger vehicles. Lyimo said 275 packets held methamphetamine, a synthetic stimulant, and 24 held heroin.

Four suspects were arrested there: a Ugandan man and three Tanzanians from Dar es Salaam. Lyimo said they told investigators they had collected the drugs in Mombasa and brought them into Tanzania through the Horohoro border post, on the Kenya–Tanzania border in the Tanga Region.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Raid on the Kenyan Coast

Lyimo said the DCEA then worked with Kenyan authorities to trace the source of the drugs. He said that on 7 November the two sides seized 454 packages of methamphetamine in Kwale County and arrested three more people, including Baseleman.

Kenya’s national police report 454 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine recovered in Kwale County, worth 3.6 billion Kenyan shillings (about US$28 million at 128.89 shillings per US$1, the 6 November close). They say the operation was carried out within a multi-agency framework.

In Plain English The DCEA is Tanzania’s national agency for fighting illegal drugs.

Methamphetamine is a strong synthetic stimulant, often sold as crystal or powder.

A suspect is a person held for investigation who has not been convicted.

What Tanzania Says About Mbwiga

The DCEA accuses Baseleman of ordering drugs directly from Afghanistan and shipping them by sea to the coast near Mombasa. From there, Lyimo said, they were sent on to several countries, including Tanzania.

Lyimo also linked him to a seizure of 3.5 tonnes of narcotics in December 2023 in Kigamboni, a district of Dar es Salaam, and in the Iringa Region, in southern Tanzania. The DCEA says the wider network reaches Afghanistan, South Africa, Mozambique, Zambia, Malawi, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Dubai.

A lane in Mombasa’s Old Town, Kenya, photographed on 9 January 2010. Photo: Mutisya Maingi / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

What Is Not Known

We found no statement from either government on what charges Baseleman faces, which country’s courts will hear the case, or whether he will be moved to Tanzania. The DCEA says only that legal procedures between Tanzania and Kenya are continuing.

One Kenyan report says a 45-year-old man named Saleh Khamis was arrested by Tanzanian authorities on 5 November and handed to Kenyan police at the Lunga Lunga–Horohoro border crossing. We could not confirm that he is the same man as Baseleman, so the Kwale arrest rests on the DCEA’s account.

The two sides also count the Kenyan haul in different units, 454 packages and 454 kilograms, so the weight of each package is not known. We found no announced court date.

What to Watch Next

The first checkpoint is any announcement of charges or of the court that will hear the case. The second is whether Tanzania requests the transfer of the suspects held in Kenya.

For readers outside East Africa, the case shows two neighbours running linked raids across a shared border; our reports on drug cases in Cabo Verde and Mauritius show the same pattern elsewhere in Africa. Background is in our guides to Tanzania and Kenya, and more news is on our Tanzania page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was arrested in Kenya?

Tanzania’s drug agency says Saleh Khamis Baseleman, known as Mbwiga, a Tanzanian businessman living in Mombasa, was arrested on 7 November 2026. It calls him a key figure in an international network and describes him as a suspect.

How much was seized in Kenya?

Kenyan police report 454 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine worth 3.6 billion Kenyan shillings (about US$28 million). Tanzania’s drug agency counts the haul as 454 packages.

Has he been charged?

We found no announcement of charges from either country. Tanzania’s drug agency says legal procedures between the two countries are continuing.

World.title: Mbeki Urges Ruling Party to Put Survival First
World.content:
The same memorial seen from another angle on the Union Buildings terrace in Pretoria, South Africa. File photo: Ruby D-Brown / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

AFRICA · SOUTH AFRICA

Thabo Mbeki, South Africa’s president from 1999 to 2008, has told the African National Congress (ANC) to put its own survival ahead of governing every city. He spoke in a podcast interview on Monday 9 November 2026, days after the 4 November local elections.

The ANC, which has led South Africa since 1994, won about 31% of the vote, down from 45.59% in 2021. Who runs South Africa’s big cities decides water, power and business conditions, which matters to US investors there.

Key Facts Who Thabo Mbeki, South Africa’s president from 1999 to 2008, urged the ANC to put its survival first.

What He said the ANC should accept opposition benches where it is weak, and finally renew itself.

Numbers The ANC took about 31% on 4 November, down from 45.59% in 2021; turnout was 52%.

Next The ANC’s leadership body between conferences, the National Executive Committee (NEC), was due to meet in the coming week to set coalition strategy.

Prediction markets Polymarket, a real-money prediction market, gives Helen Zille, a veteran politician of the Democratic Alliance (DA), about 59% to be Johannesburg’s next mayor (5:27 a.m. ET, 10 November).

Mbeki Tells the ANC to Look After Itself

Mbeki said the result “liberates the ANC to a very good extent from the task of governing.” He asked why the party does not then turn to the question of its own survival.

Rio Times membership Read everything we publish for US$1 in the first month. Then US$8.99 a month. Cancel anytime. Start for US$1

Where the ANC lacks the support to lead, he said, it should consider opposition benches rather than govern at any cost. He cited the metros (big city councils) of Gauteng, the province that holds Johannesburg and Pretoria, as places where it could step aside and let other parties negotiate.

Where the ANC won the most votes, he said, it should respect voters’ choices and help form governments. He also urged the party to carry out its long-promised organisational renewal.

The Union Buildings in Pretoria, the seat of South Africa’s presidency. File photo: Ruby D-Brown / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0).

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Long Slide in Support

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC), which runs the country’s elections, declared the vote free and fair on Sunday 8 November 2026. It put the ANC’s share at about 31% and a national turnout of 52%, up from 45.9% in 2021, as set out in our earlier report on the election result.

Mbeki estimated that only about 10% of eligible adults voted ANC. He said support was about 70% of votes cast in 2004, about 40% in 2024 and about 30% in 2026.

He said the party’s own internal polling had projected about 28%. “That’s a disaster the ANC must deal with and deal with honestly,” he said.

Mbeki pointed to poor service delivery and to how some leaders are seen. “Some of your leaders are your problem,” he said.

Renewal Promised but Not Delivered

Mbeki said the ANC’s 2017 conference called renewal essential to survival and told the NEC to act. The 2022 conference reaffirmed it, he said, but little progress followed.

He cited a renewal proposal from the party’s Veterans League, a group of long-serving members, sent in before the 2022 conference. He said it was not acted on: “That document is still sitting in the office of the secretary-general, the party’s chief administrator.”

Mbeki on Ramaphosa and the Coalition Clock

Mbeki said that if reports that President Cyril Ramaphosa is considering stepping down are true, resigning would be right. Those reports remain unconfirmed.

Fikile Mbalula, the ANC secretary-general, denied the resignation reports. Whether the ANC follows Mbeki’s advice should become clear in the coming weeks.

At the results announcement on Sunday 8 November, President Cyril Ramaphosa urged parties to put communities first. The IEC says 127 of 213 councils are hung, meaning no party holds a majority, so coalitions are needed.

After the count, each council must choose its mayor and speaker. The ANC leads the Government of National Unity, a multi-party national government formed after the 2024 election, with the DA as its biggest partner, as our guide to who holds power in South Africa explains.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a real-money prediction market, gives Helen Zille, a veteran politician of the DA, the ANC’s biggest partner in national government, about 59% to be Johannesburg’s next mayor, with US$154,519 traded across the market as of 5:27 a.m. ET on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The other candidates on the list trail far behind her.

These prices are bets, not polls, and they can move quickly. They do not show whether the ANC will follow Mbeki’s advice.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

Who runs the Johannesburg and Tshwane (Pretoria) metros decides water, power and business conditions. The NEC meeting and the first mayoral votes are the next tests.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the NEC will adopt Mbeki’s opposition-bench idea. Nor is it known whether Ramaphosa will respond.

Which coalitions will form in the Gauteng metros is still open. The resignation reports remain unconfirmed, and the ANC denies them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Thabo Mbeki tell the ANC?

He urged the ANC to put its own survival first, even at the cost of municipal governing posts. He said it should consider opposition benches where it lacks the support to lead.

How did the ANC do in the 2026 local elections?

The ANC won about 31% of the vote on 4 November, down from 45.59% in 2021. National turnout was 52%, and the Electoral Commission declared the elections free and fair.

Is Cyril Ramaphosa resigning?

No resignation has been confirmed. Mbeki said stepping down would be right if the reports are true, while Fikile Mbalula, the ANC secretary-general, denied them.

Who might be Johannesburg’s next mayor?

Polymarket, a real-money prediction market, gave Helen Zille about 59% as of 5:27 a.m. ET on 10 November 2026. These prices are bets, not polls or official results.

Sources: Mbeki podcast interview, 9 November 2026; Electoral Commission of South Africa, declaration of results, 8 November 2026; statements by ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula; Polymarket market on the next mayor of Johannesburg (https://polymarket.com/event/next-mayor-of-johannesburg-20260609220245506), read 10 November 2026.

World.title: US Keeps South Sudan on Do Not Travel List
World.content:
A view over Juba, the capital of South Sudan. File photo, 2016. (Photo: Rigan123, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

AFRICA · TRAVEL

The US State Department, the American foreign ministry, still tells Americans not to travel to South Sudan for any reason. The warning is its highest, Level 4, and it is a continuation, not a new decision.

We found no change of level this week in the State Department’s advisory history. The warning has stood at Level 4 since at least March 2025.

The advice matters to Americans who work there, including aid workers, missionaries, oil and mining contractors and dual nationals (people who also hold another passport). It also affects anyone whose travel insurance depends on the level.

Key Facts Who The US State Department, which runs American diplomacy, rates South Sudan Level 4, “Do Not Travel”.

What Level 4 is the highest of four levels; the advice was reissued in May 2026.

Why The department cites unrest, crime, kidnapping, landmines and health threats, with limited emergency help for Americans.

Next Advisories at Level 3 (“Reconsider Travel”) and Level 4 are reviewed at least every six months; the next review is due in the coming weeks.

Prediction markets Polymarket, a real-money prediction market, gives South Sudan 22% to record a case of Ebola, a deadly viral disease, in 2026 (10 November, 5:29 a.m. ET).

What the Advisory Says Today

The State Department advises US citizens not to travel to South Sudan for any reason. It names unrest, crime, kidnapping, landmines and health threats as the reasons.

It also says the US government’s ability to give emergency consular help, meaning embassy aid to citizens in trouble, to Americans there is limited. Medical services in South Sudan are limited too.

Official US government travel outside Juba, the capital, is limited. Because of serious crime in Juba, walking is restricted to a small area near the US embassy during the day.

The terminal at Juba International Airport under construction in July 2011. File photo: City ren2002 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0).

Why This Is Not a New Warning

The department reissued the advisory at Level 4 on Thursday 13 November 2025 and again in May 2026. The level stayed at 4 each time.

In March 2025 the department ordered non-emergency US government staff to leave Juba. In May 2026 it reissued the advisory at Level 4, citing the higher health risk from an Ebola outbreak in the region.

These dates follow the State Department’s advisory history, and we found no new advisory text dated 9 November. The Level 4 status is therefore a continuation of an existing warning.

Advisories at Level 3 (“Reconsider Travel”) and Level 4 are reviewed at least every six months. Counting from the May 2026 update, the next review is due in the coming weeks.

Advice to Americans, Not a Ban

The advisory is guidance to US citizens, not a ban on South Sudanese or other nationals. Our earlier report on Ebola screening at South Sudan’s borders explains health checks at the border, and our report on election talks set to resume in Juba covers the politics.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a real-money prediction market, gives South Sudan 22% to record an Ebola case in 2026. The market, “Which countries will have an Ebola case in 2026?”, had US$81,614 traded across all countries as of 5:29 a.m. ET on Tuesday 10 November 2026.

These prices are bets, not polls. They will move as health news develops.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you or a relative plans to go, check travel.state.gov, the State Department’s travel website, for the current advisory before you book. Travel insurance often excludes Level 4 destinations, so check your policy.

For employers and families of Americans already in South Sudan, the practical point is the limited help available in an emergency. The wider context of Africa’s shifting travel and trade map is in our report on Africa’s new scramble.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the level will change at the next review. It is also not known whether the department will change the advisory wording.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is South Sudan on the US Do Not Travel list?

Yes, the State Department rates South Sudan Level 4, its highest of four levels. It advises US citizens not to travel there for any reason.

Is the South Sudan warning new this week?

No, it was reissued at Level 4 on 13 November 2025 and again in May 2026. We found no change of level this week.

Does Level 4 ban South Sudanese people from travelling?

No, it is advice to US citizens, not a ban on South Sudanese or other nationals. The advisory itself closes no border.

When is the next review of the South Sudan advisory?

Advisories at Level 3 and Level 4 are reviewed at least every six months. Counting from the May 2026 update, the next review is due in the coming weeks.

World.title: Tanzania Signs US$1.2 Billion Railway Loan
World.content:
File photo. The harbour of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, 2018. Photo: Rasheedhrasheed, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

AFRICA · TANZANIA

Tanzania has signed a US$1.2 billion commercial loan for a 411-kilometre electrified railway from Tabora to Kigoma, two towns in western Tanzania, the African Development Bank (AfDB, a multilateral lender based in Abidjan) announced on Wednesday 4 November. The line is meant to carry cargo between the port of Dar es Salaam and Lake Tanganyika.

The loan is one piece of a US$2.3 billion package for Tanzania’s Standard Gauge Railway (SGR), a modern electrified line with wider track than the old metre-gauge. Tanzania has asked AfDB to structure and raise up to US$3.2 billion for the wider regional railway programme.

The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is a mining country where the United States also backs a rail route to the sea. Tanzania’s line adds a second option for cargo from the east.

Rio Times membership Read everything we publish for US$1 in the first month. Then US$8.99 a month. Cancel anytime. Start for US$1

Key Facts Who Tanzania signed the loan, and AfDB, a lender based in Abidjan, arranged it.

What US$1.2 billion for the 411-kilometre Tabora to Kigoma railway, known as Lot 6, one section of the new railway.

Why The line links Dar es Salaam port to Lake Tanganyika and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Guarantee AfDB’s US$800 million guarantee, a pledge to repay lenders if Tanzania cannot, is its largest yet.

Unknown Builders, interest rate, loan term and completion date have not been announced.

In Plain English SGR Standard Gauge Railway, Tanzania’s new electrified line with wider track than the old one.

ECA an export credit agency, a state-backed lender that finances a country’s exports.

PCG a partial credit guarantee, a promise to repay lenders part of a loan if the borrower cannot.

Lloyd’s the London insurance market, where groups of insurers called syndicates share risk.

What Tanzania Signed

Tanzania signed a US$1.2 billion commercial financing facility for Lot 6, the Tabora to Kigoma section of its SGR, AfDB said. The bank gives the length of the electrified line as 411 kilometres, although other public figures give 506 kilometres, which includes about 95 kilometres of loops and sidings.

The package also includes a tranche from an export credit agency (ECA, a state-backed export lender) and a further tranche to be raised with a co-guarantor, a second institution that shares the repayment promise. AfDB first announced a US$1.2 billion syndication plan for the SGR in December 2024.

Tanzania has mandated AfDB to structure and mobilise up to US$3.2 billion for the wider programme. Syndication means spreading one loan across several banks.

A central street in Dodoma, Tanzania’s capital. File photo from the Rio Times photo library. photo. A street in central Dodoma, Tanzania's capital city, 2015. Photo: Victor Mikheev, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Tanzania Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Guarantee Works

AfDB, as Initial Mandated Lead Arranger (the bank that assembles the lending group), arranged a Partial Credit Guarantee (PCG) of US$800 million, its largest to date. The PCG is not priced at market rates and covers the principal of the covered tranche plus two years of interest.

AfDB remains Guarantor of Record, the party legally standing behind the guarantee. Texel, an insurance broker, arranged credit insurance that spreads US$405.5 million of exposure to international insurers, including syndicates at Lloyd’s, the London insurance market.

Max Ndiaye, Senior Director at the AfDB Group, said the deal unlocked the scale of financing required for the project. He said it reflects the New African Financial Architecture for Development (NAFAD).

Nine Banks Share the Lending

A nine-bank syndicate is co-arranged by Deutsche Bank and Société Générale. It also includes HSBC, Commerzbank, Nedbank (a South African bank), Stanbic Bank Tanzania (a local arm of South Africa’s Standard Bank group), First Abu Dhabi Bank, FirstBank UK and Bank of Africa United Kingdom.

Commitments are US$720 million of guaranteed lending and US$480 million of lending on a clean-risk basis to the sovereign, meaning with no guarantee. Together they make up the US$1.2 billion facility.

A Route to Lake Tanganyika

The line connects to Tanzania’s wider rail network and the port of Dar es Salaam. AfDB expects it to support trade with the DRC through the Kigoma and Kalemie (a DRC port town) ports on Lake Tanganyika, a large lake that borders both countries.

The wider programme will link to Burundi and eastern DRC. Our earlier report on the Dar es Salaam port rail target of 1,500 containers a day covers the port end of this route.

Mike Salawou, Director of AfDB’s Infrastructure and Urban Development Department, said the bank wants the financing to become a corridor that supports competitive industries, creates jobs and deepens regional integration. That is a stated goal, not a promise of completion.

What This Means for US Readers

The Lobito Corridor, a US-backed rail route from Angola’s Lobito port to mining areas in the DRC and Zambia, is a separate route to the sea. Tanzania’s line would serve eastern DRC from the Indian Ocean side.

Whether this line wins any of that cargo depends on construction and pricing that are not yet public. AfDB’s announcement gives no traffic forecast.

For readers who follow African debt, the structure is the story. A guarantee, insurance cover and a US$480 million unguaranteed slice sit side by side in one loan.

What Is Not Known

AfDB did not state who will build the line, the interest rate or the loan’s tenor, meaning how many years it runs. It also gave no completion date and did not say how much of the package has been drawn.

Readers should watch for the naming of contractors and the closing of the remaining tranches. Until then, the signing is a financing milestone rather than a construction one.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is Tanzania borrowing for the railway?

A US$1.2 billion commercial loan for Lot 6, part of a US$2.3 billion package. AfDB is mandated to raise up to US$3.2 billion for the wider programme.

Which railway is being financed?

Lot 6 of the Standard Gauge Railway, the Tabora to Kigoma section. AfDB gives its length as 411 kilometres.

What is the African Development Bank’s role?

AfDB arranged the loan and a US$800 million Partial Credit Guarantee, its largest to date. It remains Guarantor of Record.

Why does it matter to the United States?

The United States backs the Lobito Corridor, a separate rail route to the sea for DRC and Zambian mines. Tanzania’s line would serve eastern DRC from the Indian Ocean side.

Sources: African Development Bank announcement on the Tanzania SGR Lot 6 financing, 4 November 2026 (afdb.org).

World.title: Senegal’s President Meets Macron in Paris
World.content:
The Dakar coastline seen from the air, in a December 2010 photo. Photo: Jeff Attaway / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye was received by French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace, the French president’s official residence in Paris, on Monday 9 November 2026. The two leaders discussed trade, a planned joint government seminar and French help with the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the Olympic event for teenage athletes, according to Senegal’s presidency.

The meeting came as French troops left Senegal in 2025. For US readers, it shows how a West African democracy is managing its ties with its former colonial ruler.

Who: Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and France’s President Emmanuel Macron.

Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and France’s President Emmanuel Macron. When and where: Monday 9 November 2026, at the Élysée Palace, the French president’s seat in Paris.

Monday 9 November 2026, at the Élysée Palace, the French president’s seat in Paris. Topics: A joint government seminar, trade, and the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

A joint government seminar, trade, and the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Next: Faye is due at the Paris Peace Forum, a governance conference, then at the Francophonie summit in Cambodia.

Faye is due at the Paris Peace Forum, a governance conference, then at the Francophonie summit in Cambodia. As of: 10 November 2026, 10:30 GMT.

What We Know

Senegal’s presidency said the two men picked up the dialogue they began in September in New York. They reviewed bilateral files, in particular the preparation of the intergovernmental seminar and the growth of economic and trade exchanges, in the spirit of a renewed partnership.

The intergovernmental seminar is a joint meeting of ministers from both governments. The presidency said the leaders also discussed major international questions of common interest, and gave no further detail.

Faye thanked France for its support in organising the Youth Olympic Games, which run in Dakar until 13 November. He left Dakar on Monday for Paris to attend the Paris Peace Forum, an annual conference on global governance, the presidency said.

He then goes to Phnom Penh, Cambodia, for the Francophonie summit.

In Plain English

Élysée Palace: the official residence and office of the French president in Paris.

the official residence and office of the French president in Paris. Francophonie: an international organisation of French-speaking countries that holds leaders’ summits.

an international organisation of French-speaking countries that holds leaders’ summits. Youth Olympic Games: the Olympic event for teenage athletes, held in Dakar from 31 October to 13 November 2026.

Why It Matters

France withdrew its troops from Senegal in July 2025, after Faye said that sovereignty does not allow foreign military bases. The accounts of Monday’s talks do not mention a military presence.

Macron’s planned visit to Dakar on 30 and 31 October did not take place, and no new date has been announced. Faye and Macron last met in September in New York, the presidency said.

What To Watch Next

The Paris Peace Forum runs on 10 and 11 November. Faye then heads to Phnom Penh for the 20th Francophonie summit, which is scheduled for 15 and 16 November 2026.

No date has been announced for the intergovernmental seminar or for a rescheduled Macron visit to Dakar. Our report on the players in Senegal’s economy explains the debt pressure on Senegal’s economy.

Our explainer on France’s political crisis shows the pressure Macron faces at home.

What Is Not Known

The presidency’s account gives no detail on the international questions discussed. No deal, aid figure or date for the seminar has been announced.

What It Means for You

No trade, aid or investment decision came out of the meeting, so there is nothing for US investors or travellers to act on yet. A date for the seminar would be a concrete sign of what comes next.

For wider context, see our Senegal coverage and our report on the Lompoul migrant boat sinking in northern Senegal.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who met at the Élysée Palace on 9 November 2026?

Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye met France’s President Emmanuel Macron on Monday 9 November 2026. Faye was in Paris to attend the Paris Peace Forum, before the Francophonie summit in Cambodia.

What did Faye and Macron discuss?

Senegal’s presidency said they discussed the preparation of an intergovernmental seminar, economic and trade exchanges, and international questions. Faye also thanked France for supporting the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

Did French troops leave Senegal?

Yes. France completed the withdrawal of its troops from Senegal in 2025.

Sources: Presidency of the Republic of Senegal (account of the Faye and Macron meeting, 9 November 2026).

World.title: Nigeria Opposition Still Lacks One Candidate
World.content:
NIGERIA · POLITICS

Nigeria’s opposition says its search for one joint presidential candidate against President Bola Tinubu is still on course. On Tuesday 10 November 2026, no name had been agreed, and the main hopefuls showed no sign of stepping aside.

Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country and one of its largest economies, with a presidential vote due in 2027. A split opposition could ease the incumbent’s path, which matters to investors in Nigerian oil and assets.

Key Facts Status. No joint opposition candidate had been agreed on 10 November 2026.

Holdouts. The Nigeria Democratic Congress, an opposition party, says it will back only Peter Obi, a former Anambra governor and its candidate.

Process. A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) says the effort is on course and promises a briefing.

Next. A larger gathering is expected on Thursday 19 November, a date not confirmed.

Prediction markets. Polymarket, a crypto prediction market, prices Tinubu at 67.5% and Obi at 23.0% (10 Nov, 05:22 ET).

Nigeria’s opposition parties promised in April to unite behind a single challenger to Tinubu. By November the rival camps still disagree on who that should be.

What Happened

Eagle Square, the parade ground in central Abuja, in a file photo. Photo: Tofibobo2, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

The G100, an opposition coalition convened by Dr Salihu Lukman, has not reached consensus but has not abandoned the effort. It has consulted former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra governor Peter Obi and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde.

Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, national chairman of the People’s Redemption Party (PRP), said the coalition is weighing several options, with one candidate only one of them. He said: “The single candidate issue is only one out of many options that we have available.”

A spokesman for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) said the party will not step down for anyone from outside it. He said it will accept nobody but Obi, and that because Atiku, the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has not stepped down, the NDC will not either.

Ini Ememobong, national publicity secretary of the PDP faction led by Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, said the effort remains on course. He named Atiku, Obi, Makinde, the PRP and Donald Duke, a former Cross River State governor, as committed and not withdrawn.

Atiku’s own position is in doubt. On Thursday 5 November 2026 the Federal High Court in Abuja declared his nomination as ADC presidential candidate invalid, and it nullified the leadership of the ADC under David Mark, a former Senate President.

The ADC has said it will appeal. We could not open the judgment itself, so its exact terms are not independently confirmed here.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why It Matters

On 25 April 2026 in Ibadan, opposition parties resolved in a communiqué to “work towards fielding one Presidential Candidate for the 2027 elections”. Atiku, Obi and Makinde were among those present.

A divided field is the risk that the Ibadan pledge was meant to remove. Without one name, rival candidates compete for the same voters who want a change.

The strongest counter-view comes from the NDC, whose spokesman says the party will not drop Obi for a candidate from outside its ranks. He argues that Atiku has not stepped aside either.

On Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, traders had put US$155,009 into its Nigerian Presidential Election Winner market by 05:22 ET on 10 November. It priced Bola Tinubu at 67.5%, Peter Obi at 23.0% and Atiku Abubakar at 1.8%, and these are real-money bets, not polls.

What Happens Next

A bigger opposition gathering is expected on Thursday 19 November to unveil policy positions, a date reported but not confirmed. The Turaki faction’s media committee is due to brief within two weeks.

Earlier on this story: the court ruling on Atiku’s ADC candidacy and the ADC response to the ruling. See also Nigeria’s 2027 election race and who holds power in Nigeria.

What It Means for You

For investors, a fragmented opposition points to policy continuity under Tinubu, while a late consolidation would raise political risk. The coming weeks are worth tracking.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Nigeria’s opposition agreed a joint candidate?

Which parties are involved?

What do prediction markets say about 2027?

World.title: Costa Rica Paid $701 Million More for Fuel This Year as Diesel Soared
World.content:
Costa Rica paid about $701 million more for imported fuel in the first nine months of 2026 than in the same period last year, as higher international prices drove up the cost of every barrel, according to figures from the state fuel company, Recope. Fuel imports through September totaled $2,267 million, up 44.77% from $1,566 million a year earlier.

The volume imported grew only about 5.5%, from 18.81 million to 19.85 million barrels, so most of the increase came from higher prices. The average cost of a barrel rose 37.17%, from $83.27 to $114.22. Diesel was the largest single expense, at $961 million. Its average import price climbed from $90.79 to $135.82 per barrel, while jet fuel rose from $93.36 to $138.84. Karla Montero, Recope’s executive president, attributed the jump in diesel to attacks on Russian refineries.

The Central Bank of Costa Rica (BCCR) projects in its Monetary Policy Report that the country’s oil bill will close 2026 at $3,086 million, compared with $1,976 million in 2025. Montero said higher import costs reach consumers gradually, through the monthly price adjustments approved by the Public Services Regulatory Authority (Aresep). Diesel and regular gasoline currently sell for 808 colones per liter, about $1.80, or roughly $6.80 per gallon. Super gasoline sells for 806 colones per liter.

Diesel has historically been cheaper at the pump because it carries a lower single fuel tax, but international cost pressure has narrowed that gap. Diesel was up 17% in October’s inflation figures, as consumer prices rose for a second straight month. Alonso Alfaro, chief economist at the BCCR, said more expensive fuel adds inflationary pressure that could spread to other prices. He also said larger import payments increase demand for dollars and put pressure on the external deficit, although that demand has so far been met without instability.

The exchange rate has softened part of the blow. Recope said this year’s roughly 10% shift in the exchange rate has offset part of the increase in import costs, with the dollar now trading near 450 colones. Recope expects international prices to remain between $90 and $110 a barrel in the coming weeks. Pablo Guzmán, executive director of the Costa Rican Fuel Chamber, said Costa Rica is a price taker and that prices could ease or rise moderately in 2027.

Any relief next year depends on smoother oil shipments through the Middle East and a recovery in diesel supply. Recope said it has completed its annual tender for 2027 contracts, which fixes freight, insurance and supplier margins for the year.

World.title: Costa Rica Asks You to Cut Water Use as the El Niño Dry Season Begins
World.content:
Costa Rica’s national water utility is asking everyone to use less water as the dry season begins this week in Guanacaste and the Central Valley, with a strong El Niño expected to keep conditions drier and hotter than normal through January. The Costa Rican Institute of Aqueducts and Sewers (AyA) made the appeal on Monday. It is a request, not a restriction. AyA said it is not rationing water and has no plans to do so in the near future.

The reason is timing. The National Meteorological Institute (IMN) expects the dry season to start this week in the North Pacific and Central Valley, during Nov. 16–22 in the Central Pacific and during Nov. 23–29 in the South Pacific. Once the rain stops, the sources that feed many water systems stop recharging. IMN director Bernard Stolz said in May that AyA is among the institutions hit hardest by El Niño because rain stops falling in the high parts of the mountains. Water saved now helps carry systems through the driest months of the year.

Here is what AyA is asking you to do at home.

Take shorter showers, and turn off the tap while you soap up or shampoo.

Fix leaks, and check faucets, pipes and toilets for water running when it shouldn’t be.

Don’t hose down sidewalks, patios or driveways.

Reuse water for household jobs that don’t need drinking water.

Collect rainwater for plants and outdoor cleaning, but don’t drink it.

Run the washing machine only with a full load.

One thing AyA does not want you to do is stockpile. Drinking water stored too far in advance can lose quality and become contaminated, so there is no need to fill containers unless your provider announces a cut. This year has already tested the supply. Water rationing reached dozens of Pacific communities, and in October authorities issued the country’s first red alert at sea.

The Central Valley is exposed too. A national El Niño contingency strategy drawn up by the National Emergency Commission (CNE) with AyA and other institutions projected lower output from the surface and underground sources that supply the Greater Metropolitan Area. That plan listed at least 120,579 AyA customers in San José districts, including Pavas, Tibás, Goicoechea, Moravia and La Uruca, as facing possible supply impacts. It also set out tanker-truck service for critical areas such as La Carpio.

If your water comes from a local ASADA rather than AyA, as it does in many Guanacaste beach towns and rural communities, that provider sets its own schedules. Check its notices or social media pages for any changes. AyA’s appeal did not single out specific regions or set a consumption target. If supply does tighten, service schedules would come from AyA or from local providers.

World.title: Spot an Injured Animal on Route 27? Don’t Touch It. Here’s Who to Call
World.content:
If you see an injured animal on Route 27, the toll highway between San José and the central Pacific coast, don’t pull over and try to pick it up. Slow down, keep your distance and call the highway’s 24-hour control center at 2588-4040. That is the advice from Route 27’s operator, Globalvia, and from specialists at Refugio Animal de Costa Rica, a wildlife refuge in Santa Ana. The highway has recorded 299 animal rescues since 2015, according to Globalvia.

The total includes 149 dogs, 58 cats and 92 wild animals. Among the wildlife were sloths, snakes, turtles, iguanas, birds, coatis and ocelots. An animal that has been hit by a car may be stunned, in shock or carrying a fracture you can’t see. Even one that looks calm can bite or lash out when you get close, and handling it the wrong way can make its injuries worse. Snakes and other potentially dangerous species add another layer of risk.

Stopping suddenly is a danger of its own on one of the country’s busiest highways. Brake gradually, don’t swerve, and give the drivers behind you time to react. Rodolfo Vargas, a biologist at the refuge, advises alerting other motorists without making sudden maneuvers. Don’t try to touch, capture or carry a wild animal yourself. Report it instead, so trained staff can deal with it safely.

The Route 27 control center answers 24 hours a day at 2588-4040. If the animal or the situation puts other drivers in immediate danger, call 911. For specialist advice on what to do, you can reach Refugio Animal de Costa Rica at 8828-0324. When you call, give your location as precisely as you can, ideally the nearest kilometer marker, along with your direction of travel. Say whether the animal looks injured and whether it is blocking a lane.

Route 27 recently trained 15 of its staff with specialists from the refuge. The course covered how to identify potentially dangerous species, how to recognize injuries and fractures, and how to handle animals safely. Montserrat Courrau, Route 27’s director of communications and corporate social responsibility, said every animal presents its own situation, which is why staff need to know how to handle each one correctly.

Globalvia says the highway has run its animal assistance and staff training program for more than a decade. The rescues are a small window onto a wider problem, as wildlife deaths on Costa Rica’s roads continue to mount and a new law requires wildlife crossings on public infrastructure.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Marchamo Amnesty Is Off for 2027, So Pay by Dec. 31
World.content:
If you’re behind on your marchamo and hoping lawmakers would wipe the debt this year, don’t wait. The amnesty proposed for 2027 failed, and a new version wouldn’t help anyone until 2028. Your 2027 marchamo is due by Dec. 31. Any older years you haven’t paid still carry their interest and fines.

The original plan was simple. Bill 25.630, filed on June 22 by Liberación Nacional deputy Mangell McLean, would have forgiven every unpaid marchamo from 2026 and earlier, including interest, fines and penalties. All you had to do was pay the 2027 marchamo before Jan. 1, 2027.

To take effect in time for this year’s payments, the bill needed a fast track. On Sept. 8, lawmakers voted 29 to 20 against that, with the ruling Pueblo Soberano caucus opposed. Without the fast track, the bill went into the regular queue and can’t move quickly enough to cover your 2027 payment.

McLean has now filed a new bill, number 25.886. It moves everything forward a year. You would have to pay the 2028 marchamo before Jan. 1, 2028, and anything unpaid from 2027 and earlier would be forgiven. The new version is narrower. It covers only cars and motorcycles with a fiscal value of 13,020,000 colones (about $28,700) or less, so newer and higher-value vehicles would not qualify.

It is a proposal, not a law. It still has to clear committee and two floor votes, and it would need support from a ruling party that has so far opposed it. The debt behind the push is large. According to Finance Ministry data cited by McLean, 10.6 million unpaid marchamos piled up between 2015 and 2026. That figure counts unpaid years, not vehicles, because a single car can owe several.

McLean argues that an amnesty would turn debt the state can’t collect into immediate revenue and help families get their vehicles back on the road legally. Opponents in the ruling party argue that forgiving the debt would reward people who didn’t pay. Costa Rica has done this before. In January 2022, lawmakers forgave old marchamos for nearly a million vehicles, but only 108,785 of the 992,598 eligible vehicles took advantage. A second amnesty passed in September 2023.

Here is what to do now. Look up your total by license plate on the INS marchamo website or by calling 800-MARCHAMO (800-6272-4266). The breakdown shows each item, including any older years you still owe. Expect the mandatory SOA insurance in your marchamo to cost a little more. For a private car, it rises 5.4% to 31,881 colones (about $70). The SOA covers medical care for people injured in a crash, up to 6 million colones per person.

This is also the first year of the new digital sticker, which is meant to last up to 10 years. It carries a separate charge of about 1,200 colones. Motorcycles keep the traditional sticker for now. Before you pay, check your total for an optional add-on insurance policy. If you don’t want it, you can uncheck it and the amount will adjust.

Regular collection of the 2027 marchamo runs through Dec. 31. More than 2 million marchamos were issued for collection this cycle.

World.title: Guanacaste Town Hall Took 29 Million Colones in Cash Its Bank Refused
World.content:
A Guanacaste municipality accepted 29.3 million colones (about $64,600) in cash for a property tax bill after its bank refused to deposit the money. The municipality held the cash until judicial agents seized it, according to internal audit documents. The Municipality of Nandayure, on the Nicoya Peninsula, received the payment on March 4. A man came to the counter to pay a corporation’s property taxes on two properties, covering 2023 through the first quarter of 2026.

He paid in bundles made up mostly of 10,000- and 20,000-colón bills. He also handed over copies of his identification, a sworn statement, the company’s legal registration, a trust agreement, a loan contract and a promissory note. Municipal staff tried to deposit the cash at Banco Nacional that same day and again on March 6 at the bank’s Jicaral branch. Each time the bank turned it away and asked for a withdrawal slip or other proof of where the money came from.

On the March 6 trip, the cash went by municipal vehicle with no police escort and no transit insurance, the documents show. The money stayed under municipal control until March 10, when agents of the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) seized it. The municipality’s Internal Audit has since sent its documentation to the OIJ, which is working to establish the origin of the funds.

According to the audit findings, municipal accountant Xinia María Cambronero and cashier Lilliam Artavia warned that the cash should not be accepted without proof of its origin. Artavia told auditors she asked Mayor Teddy Zúñiga Sánchez directly what to do. She said he told her to accept the money and issue a receipt, and assured her she would not face problems. She described the situation as unprecedented at the municipality.

Cambronero said she warned the mayor the bank would likely reject the cash. She said he told staff to accept it because municipal taxes must be honored. The documents also note that the municipality had no security cameras, no permanent security staff and no protocol for handling large cash payments.

Zúñiga denied giving a specific order to the finance department or the accountant. In a written response, he described the matter as an institutional consultation for the responsible department to resolve. In other official communications, the mayor said he had asked for more documents, including a withdrawal slip, and that the cash should have stayed in the municipal safe. He argued that the municipality acts as a tax collector, not a financial institution.

Zúñiga also said he does not know the people involved and was not part of the receiving process. He said the municipality is cooperating with the investigation and has annulled the 29.3-million-colón receipt, so the tax debt is pending again. The mayor said the judicial case is against an unidentified person and that, as far as he knows, no criminal investigation targets municipal officials. He said the taxpayer may have filed a constitutional appeal but that he had not confirmed it.

The Public Prosecutor’s Office said in April that the case was being investigated against an unidentified person and did not involve municipal employees at that stage. That same month, the Comptroller General’s Office closed a separate administrative complaint over the payment because a judicial authority was already handling the matter.

The cash payment is one of two matters at the Nandayure municipality now before judicial authorities. On Nov. 4, the OIJ and prosecutors raided the town hall in an unrelated case and detained two officials. One is an inspector surnamed Venegas. The other works in the Maritime-Terrestrial Zone Department, which handles beachfront concessions.

The two are suspected of concusión, a crime in which a public official uses the position to demand an improper payment. According to the court file, the inspector allegedly used WhatsApp to ask a resident for 4 million colones (about $8,800) to speed up a land concession process. He allegedly also offered privileged information about other lots in the area.

The resident wanted to buy a lot from a third party and did not know it was a concession inside the maritime zone. The events date to June 12, and the case began with the resident’s complaint. The court file points to possible involvement by other officials, who have not been named.

The municipality confirmed the detentions and the seizure of files related to the case. It said it is cooperating with judicial authorities, recently made changes in the Maritime-Terrestrial Zone Department, and that procedures for concession holders and applicants will continue as normal.

No connection between the two cases has been reported. No one has been charged in either matter. Under Costa Rica’s maritime zone law, the strip of land within 200 meters (656 feet) of the high-tide line is public. The first 50 meters (164 feet) cannot be privately held, and local governments grant concessions on the remaining 150 meters (492 feet). That makes municipal concession offices one of the most consequential public counters along the country’s coast.

World.title: Driving South This Week? Térraba Bridge Closures Run Through November 14
World.content:
If you’re driving the Interamericana Sur through Palmar Norte this week, check the clock before you leave. The bridge over the Térraba River, between Palmar Norte and Palmar Sur in Osa, has partial closures every day from Monday, November 9 through Saturday, November 14. Tonight it closes completely.

Both lanes close from 10 p.m. tonight until 5 a.m. Tuesday, according to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MOPT). If you reach the bridge during those hours, you’ll have to wait until morning to cross. Today’s partial closures run from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. before the full overnight shutdown. From Tuesday through Friday, partial closures come in two blocks each day, from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. and again from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. On Saturday, partial closures run from 7 a.m. to noon.

Outside those hours, both lanes stay open as usual, MOPT said. This bridge is the gateway to everything south of Palmar Norte. That includes Palmar Sur and its airport, Sierpe, where boats leave for Drake Bay, the turnoff to Puerto Jiménez, Golfito, and the Paso Canoas border crossing into Panama. The Costanera Sur coastal highway joins the Interamericana Sur at Palmar Norte, so drivers coming down from Dominical and Uvita who are heading farther south cross it too.

If you have a flight out of Palmar Sur or a boat to catch in Sierpe, leave extra time during the daytime closure hours. If you’re driving to the Panama border tonight, plan to cross the bridge before 10 p.m. or after 5 a.m. MOPT hasn’t announced an alternate route, so your best option is to time your trip around the schedule.

MOPT says the work will raise the bridge’s clearance and let heavy trucks cross safely. Repairs began in late January, and a second phase is reinforcing the structure from underneath. The ministry reported the project was 70 percent complete in late October, up from 40 percent in March.

The rehabilitation costs more than $10 million and is funded through the government’s emergency infrastructure reconstruction program, known as Proeri. The bridge is one of the most important structures on the southern Interamericana. It opened on February 26, 1961, and MOPT’s historical records describe close to 161 metric tons (about 177 US tons) of reinforced steel in its frame and supports.

This week’s closures won’t be the last. MOPT said closures like these will continue into early 2027 and that it will announce new dates as the work moves forward. Check the schedule before any trip through the southern zone in the coming months.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Dry Season Starts This Week in Guanacaste and the Central Valley
World.content:
If you live in or are visiting Guanacaste or the Central Valley, the rain is about to switch off. Costa Rica’s dry season settles over the North Pacific and the Central Valley this week, and the rest of the Pacific coast follows within three weeks. That is the outlook from the National Meteorological Institute (IMN), whose four-week forecast goes from Nov. 9 to Dec. 6 and describes the dry season taking hold across the Pacific slope and the Central Valley under a pattern of below-normal rainfall.

With that said, here is the timeline. The North Pacific, which is Guanacaste and the Central Valley, home to San José, Alajuela, Heredia and Cartago, enter the dry season this week. The Central Pacific, including Quepos and Manuel Antonio, follows the week after.

The South Pacific, from Dominical and Uvita down to the Osa Peninsula, joins the week of Nov. 23 to 29. By Nov. 30, the IMN expects very dry conditions across the North Pacific, the Central Pacific and the Central Valley. Keep in mind, dry does not mean zero rain, at least not yet. For this week, the forecast still allows weekly totals of 1 to 70 millimeters (up to 2.8 inches) in the North Pacific and 5 to 80 millimeters (0.2 to 3.1 inches) in the Central Valley, mostly as isolated afternoon showers in the mountains.

The Central Pacific could also see 10 to 80 millimeters (0.4 to 3.1 inches) this week, and the South Pacific 20 to 80 millimeters (0.8 to 3.1 inches). Today is the hand-off. The low-pressure system that soaked the Pacific over the weekend is drifting west, away from the coast. Expect some early rain on the Guanacaste coast this morning, isolated afternoon showers in the mountains and stronger trade winds from the afternoon on but tonight should be dry.

The weekend left its mark first. Nosara recorded 51 millimeters (2 inches) of rain on Sunday, and parts of the eastern Central Valley reached 60 to 65 millimeters (2.4 to 2.6 inches), according to the IMN. That followed a Saturday when five regions were on yellow alert. Those afternoon winds are the real signal. Trade winds are the signature of the dry season in the Central Valley and Guanacaste as they bring cool, clear mornings and blue skies, but they also dry out pastures and forest quickly.

If you are on the Caribbean coast or in the Northern Zone, nothing changes. Those regions have no defined dry season but even so, the IMN expects rainfall there to run about 30 percent below normal from November through January. This year’s switch comes in the middle of a very strong El Niño, which the IMN expects to hold at that intensity through January. The institute has warned that temperatures could run up to 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit) above normal and may break records, in line with a December El Niño peak forecast by the World Meteorological Organization.

IMN climatologist Daniel Poleo said in October that the transition could be drier than normal, after a month the institute projected would end 40 to 60 percent short of normal rainfall in much of the country. Back in September, forecasters were already saying El Niño could end the rainy season early.

A drier-than-usual start matters most for water availability. Guanacaste enters the dry months after a year in which water rationing reached dozens of Pacific communities and authorities issued the country’s first red alert at sea. One caveat before you put the umbrella away. The hurricane season runs until Nov. 30 in both the Atlantic and the Pacific, and storms during the transition can still bring short, intense downpours. On Sunday, the US National Hurricane Center gave the weekend’s low a 20 percent chance of becoming a tropical depression within 48 hours.

Having said all that, what does this mean for you? Pack a light layer for windy Central Valley mornings, carry more water than you think you need on Pacific beaches, and keep an eye on afternoon clouds in the mountains for the rest of November. For most of Costa Rica, the change means clearer skies, cooler highland nights and long stretches of sunshine through April. It also starts the five-month stretch when every liter of water on the Pacific side counts.

World.title: Diesel Up 17% as Costa Rica Prices Rise for a Second Straight Month
World.content:
Costa Rica’s cost of living is climbing again. Consumer prices rose 0.39% in October, and the year-on-year rate reached 0.55%, the second straight month above zero after 16 months of annual declines, according to figures from the National Institute of Statistics and Census (INEC).

That October jump compares with 0.11% in September and 0.19% in October 2025. The interannual rate also climbed from 0.34% a month earlier. Transport drove most of the increase. INEC reported that the transport division rose 1.71% in a single month and accounted for 0.30 percentage points of the overall index, with diesel up 17.39%, gasoline up 3.10%, taxi fares up 5.73% and bus fares up 2.02%.

Nelson Castillo Mendoza, coordinator of the INEC price index unit, said the main upward pressure came from fuel and public transport fares. He noted that those prices are set by the Public Services Regulatory Authority (Aresep) and moved in line with international fuel prices during the month.

The rise follows September’s warnings of higher fuel prices as oil climbed back above $100 a barrel. Regulated goods and services rose 1.99% in October, according to INEC data, while unregulated items rose just 0.16%. Energy prices as a group rose 2.75%. Entertainment also cost more. The recreation, sport and culture division rose 0.96%, which INEC attributed mainly to higher ticket prices for events. Eggs rose 4.09%.

Some grocery staples moved the other way. Onions fell 10.73%, potatoes 3.50%, ground beef 2.44% and chicken breast 1.73%, and food and non-alcoholic beverages as a whole rose only 0.09%. Of the 293 goods and services in the basket, 45% rose, 33% fell and 22% were unchanged, with 10 of 13 spending divisions moving higher.

The longer view still shows Costa Rica with unusually low inflation. Cumulative inflation from January through October was -0.01%, essentially flat, compared with a 1.77% decline over the same period of 2025. Full-year 2025 inflation was -1.23%.

That keeps Costa Rica well below the Central Bank of Costa Rica (BCCR) target of 3%, with a tolerance band of one percentage point in either direction. The October reading sits 1.45 points below the bottom of that range, and inflation has now been below target for 42 consecutive months. The last time it was inside the band was April 2023.

The BCCR expects that gap to close. In its October Monetary Policy Report, the bank projected headline inflation near 2.7% in the second half of 2027, higher than its July forecast, and tied the revision to expected higher hydrocarbon prices. It kept its monetary policy rate at 3% and said it would adjust its stance if conditions or risks change.

The central bank listed extreme weather, including El Niño, geopolitical conflict and higher oil and grain prices among the risks that could push inflation up faster. A stronger colón and weaker global growth were among the factors that could hold it down. For households, the October figures arrive alongside other pressures. Earlier this month, INEC data showed unemployment climbing to 6.5%, while the exchange rate has left dollar earners with fewer colones than in January.

Rents have also been outpacing general inflation for months. The return of rising prices ends a long stretch of falling prices in Costa Rica. Whether the shift becomes a steady climb back toward target or a short fuel-driven spike will depend largely on oil markets and on the next round of regulated price adjustments, which anyone who fills a tank, rides a bus or takes a taxi in Costa Rica will feel first.

World.title: Charles Middleton dies from injuries sustained in Taylor’s Alley Halloween night shooting
World.content:
Charles Middleton dies from injuries sustained in Taylor’s Alley Halloween night shooting

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Breaking Belize News has received information that 29-year-old Charles Middleton has succumbed to gunshot injuries sustained during a shooting in the Taylor’s Alley area of Belize City on October 31, 2026.

Middleton was among four men who came under gunfire while socializing near Cemetery Road when a gunman reportedly opened fire on the group from a black Chevrolet.

The shooting initially claimed the life of 31-year-old Charles Nolberto, while Middleton and two other men, Cesario Choco and Clifford Olivera, sustained injuries.

Police had previously reported that the three surviving victims were in stable condition following the attack.

However, information received by Breaking Belize News from a police source on Monday night, November 9, indicates that Middleton has since succumbed to his injuries.

His death brings the number of fatalities from the shooting to two.

Police had previously indicated that the attack was believed to be connected to ongoing gang-related tensions in Belize City.

Investigations into the shooting remain ongoing.

World.title: San Felipe man charged with two counts of attempted murder after machete attacks on tortilla man and hammock man

San Felipe man charged with two counts of attempted murder after machete attacks on tortilla man and hammock man

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have formally arrested and charged 26-year-old Dwight Hernandez of San Felipe Village, Orange Walk District, with two counts of attempted murder following a pair of machete attacks that left two men injured on Friday, November 6.

According to police, the incidents occurred shortly before 6:00 p.m. when Hernandez allegedly confronted 51-year-old Cesar Bolaños, a tortilla factory owner, on an unnamed road in San Felipe Village and inflicted several chop wounds before fleeing.

Investigators say Hernandez then travelled approximately three blocks away, where he allegedly attacked a second man, identified as 50-year-old Jorge Murillo, who was lying in a hammock. Murillo also sustained chop wounds during the attack.

Police subsequently launched an operation to locate Hernandez, with assistance from residents of the community. He was eventually apprehended and taken into custody.

Both victims were reported to be in stable condition as of Monday’s police briefing.

Investigators also disclosed that Hernandez and Bolaños had reportedly been involved in a previous altercation. Police further indicated that they are examining information concerning the suspect’s alleged substance use and behaviour, although the precise motive for the attacks has not been established.

The incident had previously sparked alarm in San Felipe Village, where residents reportedly assisted in searching for the alleged attacker. Reports from Friday night indicated that villagers beat Hernandez to subdue him.

Hernandez has now been charged with two counts of attempted murder as investigations continue.

World.title: Migrant caravan sets off in southern Mexico after Trump’s midterm losses, and Belize is watching
World.content:
Migrant caravan sets off in southern Mexico after Trump’s midterm losses, and Belize is watching

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Hundreds of migrants, most of them from Honduras, have set off on foot in a caravan through southern Mexico, saying they believe US President Donald Trump’s tough immigration policies will soften after his party’s losses in last week’s midterm elections.

According to Reuters, the group left the Mexican border town of Metapa de Dominguez and walked to the city of Tapachula in Chiapas state, near the border with Guatemala.

Migrants told Reuters they expect Trump’s anti migrant measures to weaken now that Democrats control the US Senate. Some said they were happy to see the President’s party suffer losses.

“I think we’re all people who want to work,” one migrant said.

The caravan’s journey is a reminder of how closely Belize is tied to migration in the region. Belize borders both Mexico and Guatemala, and many Central Americans pass through or settle in Belize while searching for work and safety. Communities across Belize are home to large numbers of Honduran, Guatemalan and Salvadoran families.

Thousands of Belizeans also live in the United States, and many households here rely on the money they send home. Any change in how Washington treats migrants could affect those families directly.

Democrats flipped six Republican held Senate seats on November 3. However, immigration enforcement remains largely in the hands of the White House, and it is not yet clear whether the vote will lead to real change.

World.content:
Shiloh Coleman found murdered near Mile 8 on George Price Highway after being reported missing

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the murder of 19-year-old Shiloh Coleman of Belize City, whose decomposing body was discovered shortly before midday on Monday, November 9, approximately one and a half miles into the Western Paradise community near Mile 8 on the George Price Highway.

According to police, Coleman’s body was already showing signs of decomposition and had apparent gunshot wounds when investigators arrived at the scene.

Coleman had been reported missing by his mother at approximately 5:30 p.m. on Sunday, November 8. She told investigators that she last communicated with her son shortly before 9:00 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, after noticing that his vehicle was not parked at home.

She reportedly sent him a message asking about his whereabouts, and he responded that he would return home. However, when she received no further communication from him the following day, she contacted police.

During Monday’s press briefing, police confirmed that investigators are pursuing two possible motives for the killing but declined to disclose either, citing the ongoing investigation.

Authorities also confirmed that Coleman’s vehicle had not yet been recovered, although investigators have received information about its possible whereabouts and are following leads with assistance from the Crime Fusion Centre and surveillance camera operators.

Police have not disclosed whether any suspects have been identified or whether the killing is connected to the recent wave of gang-related violence in Belize City.

The investigation remains ongoing.

World.title: Guilty after jury fury
World.content:
A photo of Andre Ruddock captured while he lay on the ground at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James on the night of October 17, 2021, after he cut the throat of fellow church member Taneka Gardner.

POLICE personnel were forced to rush in and restore order in the jury room at the Supreme Court on Monday after tensions boiled over following a split in their verdict during deliberations in the Andre Ruddock murder trial.

Eventually, after two hours of deliberations, the jury ultimately found Ruddock guilty of murder in the gruesome killing of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner, whose throat was cut at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James on October 17, 2021, in what was said to be a human sacrifice ritual.

Earlier, after trial judge Justice Leighton Pusey completed his summation, the jurors were sent off to deliberate at 12:46 pm.

At 1:25 pm police who were guarding the jury room indicated to the court registrar that the panel was ready to deliver the verdict. They were readmitted into the courtroom at 1:37 pm

— 51 minutes after retiring

— at which time the registrar asked the lead juror if they had arrived at a unanimous verdict. The lead juror indicated that they had not, pointing out that five among them believed Ruddock was guilty while two jurors weren’t satisfied beyond a reasonable doubt that he had killed Gardner.

Justice Pusey informed the jurors that they would have to spend at least two hours in deliberations before they could return to the courtroom and deliver the verdict. They were subsequently sent back to the jury room by the judge.

At 1:49 pm the registrar again indicated that the jurors were ready to deliver their verdict, leaving everyone inside the courtroom to believe that they had arrived at a unanimous verdict. However, when they entered the jury box and the lead juror was asked if a unanimous verdict had been reached, she again said ‘No’, prompting the judge to explain to them that if the verdict was not unanimous, they would have to spend two hours or more deliberating. Pusey again sent them back to the jury room.

At approximately 2:09 pm, about five members of the Jamaica Constabulary Force were spotted rushing into the jury room where a heated argument was unfolding.

One juror was heard blurting out: “You want to be the boss of everything!” The police managed to cool the tension, then exited to give the jurors space to arrive at a final decision.

However, additional police personnel were called in to join the two who were already standing guard outside the door of the jury room.

At 2:52 pm, the jurors returned to the jury box where the lead juror indicated that there was a slight change in the decision, pointing out that six among them were convinced that Ruddock was guilty of killing Gardner and only one was not so convinced.

Judge Pusey then thanked the jurors for their service before dismissing them. The judge ordered that a social enquiry be done on Ruddock, with a report to be produced in the next six weeks.

Ruddock is to return for sentencing on January 22, 2027.

Lead prosecutor Latoya Bernard told the media that she would not be making any extensive comments on the matter following the verdict. All she offered was that, “The jury has spoken.”

Bernard was supported by prosecutor Carolyn Wright, while Venice Brown supported lead defence attorney Anthony Williams.

After the verdict, Williams breathed a sigh of relief saying, “Boy, the case is finally over.”

“The prosecution’s case essentially is that Mr Ruddock was the one who slashed the throat of Miss Taneka Gardner with a knife on instructions of Mr Kevin Smith. They also alleged that Mr Ruddock gave a caution statement as well as a question and answer document. We contend that, in the first place, it was Mr Kevin Smith who was the person who actually slit or cut Taneka Gardener’s throat.

“We denied it vehemently and that was the defence. We also say that the alleged caution statement and question and answer were, in fact, done under duress. He was forced and intimidated by a policeman in question who held him on the compound of the church. We made very, very heavy waters in this case. It was a very tough case. The jury retired once, it was a 5-2 verdict. They retired twice and in the end they came back with a 6-1 verdict of guilty,” the attorney pointed out.

Williams said the defence was proud of its performance and had given Ruddock the best possible representation in a very challenging case.

“We felt very optimistic of a not guilty verdict, and I say that because of the intensive cross-examination we did of the main witness in particular, as well as the other prosecution witnesses. They were discredited, undermined, and we think we made very good progress. At the end of the day, the jurors are the judges of the fact, and they have concluded that our expectation was not theirs,” Williams said.

Ruddock cut Gardner’s throat on the compound of Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries allegedly on instructions from his now deceased pastor, Kevin Smith. It was disclosed during the trial, through a witness, that Gardner’s name appeared on a piece of paper alongside other names. The witness said that Gardner was called onto the compound of the church and instructed by the pastor to write 999 beside her name.

The pastor then told her that she would have to die because her blood was unclean. He then proceeded to ask her if she believed that he could bring her back to life if her throat was to be cut. Gardner reportedly told the pastor “Yes” in response to his question. Smith then instructed a male member of the church to cut her throat. When that member hesitated, Ruddock took a knife from him and carried out the pastor’s order.

Pastor Smith died on October 25, 2021 in a motor vehicle crash on the Linstead bypass in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston by police to face charges.

Authorities reported that he died along with Constable Orlando Irons, who was among the lawmen transporting the cult pastor.

In May 2024 a coroner’s inquest found that the crash did not occur because of excess speed and as such the policemen, who were placed before the inquest, were credible witnesses.

The inquest found that Smith assaulted the cops who were transporting him, and the judge ruled that his actions were unlawful, dangerous, and caused the death of Constable Irons.

KINGSTON, Jamaica—Jurors brought in a majority guilty verdict for Andre Ruddock in his murder murder trial Monday, following deliberations in the Home Circuit Court.

Ruddock is on trial for murder in relation to the October 17, 2021 killing of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner. Six of the seven jurors found him guilty of the offence.

It is alleged that Ruddock cut Gardner’s throat at the Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St. James on instructions from his then-pastor, Kevin Smith.

The defence team comprises Anthony Williams and Venice Brown.

On the prosecution’s side, LaToya Bernard and Carolyn Wright represented the Crown.
