World.title: Gulf states to base joint forces in Kuwait after Iranian attacks
World.content:
DUBAI: Gulf Cooperation Council defense ministers have agreed to set up a forward military command in Kuwait with forces assigned to the site, GCC Secretary-General Jassim Al-Budaiwi said on Tuesday.

A forward command is a headquarters placed closer to potential flashpoints than a military’s main command. It allows more efficient coordination and faster deployment of forces. Kuwait sits at the northern tip of the Gulf, bordering Iraq and Saudi Arabia, and facing Iran across the water.

The new command will come under the GCC’s Unified Military Command, the joint force that brings together the armed forces of the six member states.

The decision was taken at the 23rd session of the GCC Joint Defense Council in Manama, chaired by Bahraini Minister of Defense Affairs Lt. Gen. Abdullah bin Hassan Al-Nuaimi.

Al-Budaiwi said the meeting followed directives issued by GCC leaders at their extraordinary summit in Jeddah in April to strengthen joint military action and boost the bloc’s ability to face common threats.

He praised the level of military cooperation and coordination among member states in responding to what he described as Iranian aggression in the region, saying it showed that the security of Gulf countries was a shared responsibility.

Al-Budaiwi condemned in the strongest terms the Iranian attacks that had hit GCC states and damaged civilian sites and infrastructure. He also paid tribute to the armed forces of member states and offered condolences for those killed, wishing the injured a swift recovery.

He also condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including the targeting of holy sites, calling them a blatant violation of the Kingdom’s security and sovereignty.

The GCC states stand in full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support all measures the Kingdom takes to protect its security, stability and territory, he said, adding that “the security of the Kingdom is an integral part of the security of all GCC countries.”

Al-Budaiwi said the council had also adopted a number of other decisions that would take Gulf military cooperation to a broader level of integration.

World.title: Saudi Energy’s 9-month profit rises 4.3% to $3.2bn
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Energy’s net profit rose 4.3 percent year on year to SR12.1 billion ($3.2 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, supported by an expanding regulated asset base and higher project-related revenue.

Revenue increased 11.5 percent to SR87.2 billion, which the company attributed to higher regulated revenue, including pass-through costs, increased income from project development and management contracts, and customer growth.

The results come as Saudi Arabia reshapes its electricity sector, targeting a generation mix of approximately 50 percent renewable energy and 50 percent natural gas by 2030, as it gradually phases out liquid fuels used in power generation.

“With 22 GWh (gigawatt-hour) of battery storage now energized, we achieved our 2026 target, supporting a more flexible grid and greater renewable integration,” CEO Khalid Al-Ghamdi said.

Saudi Energy’s regulated asset base, which determines its permitted revenue, reached SR278.8 billion at the end of September, up 16.6 percent year on year, as completed transmission and distribution projects entered service

Quarterly performance

Third-quarter net profit edged up 0.4 percent to SR5.4 billion, while revenue increased 12.9 percent to SR35 billion.

Higher gross profit, lower expected credit-loss provisions and increased earnings from equity-accounted investments supported the quarterly result. These gains were partly offset by lower other income, higher administrative expenses and increased net financing costs.

For the nine-month period, operating profit rose 4.7 percent to SR16.9 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization increased 6.6 percent to SR34.7 billion.

Electricity investment

Adjusted capital expenditure stood at SR59.6 billion, excluding accruals and customer-funded transmission and distribution projects.

Spending focused on transmission expansion, battery storage, generation and distribution infrastructure.

The company reported that the Kingdom’s peak electricity load reached 79,045 megawatts, 2.5 percent above the 2025 peak.

Grid-connected renewable capacity reached approximately 19.3 GW by the end of September.

Across the sector, Saudi Power Procurement Co. signed agreements in August for four battery-storage projects involving investment exceeding SR4.35 billion.

Their combined power capacity is 2,000 MW, with four-hour storage duration.

Three projects were awarded to a consortium including Saudi Energy, Acwa and Al Sharif Contracting and Commercial Development Co., while the fourth went to an ENGIE-led consortium.

The projects are intended to support renewable integration and electricity supply reliability.

Saudi Energy connected 237,762 new customers during the nine months, bringing its customer base to about 11.7 million. Electricity sales increased 1 percent to 276.9 terawatt-hours.

The results precede electricity tariff adjustments taking effect on Jan. 1.

Saudi Energy said it did not expect a material financial impact because its regulated asset base and required-revenue framework remained unchanged.

World.title: Zelensky holds air defense, energy security talks with Nordic leaders
World.content:
COPENHAGEN: Denmark said Tuesday it was hosting talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Nordic leaders to discuss military support, air defense and energy infrastructure security.

The meetings came as direct Ukraine-Russia talks, under US mediation, began in Abu Dhabi.

Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said his country was planning to donate 4.8 billion kroner ($720 million) in military aid to Ukraine.

Another 150 million kroner would be donated to Ukraine’s energy sector, Rasmussen told reporters.

“I am proud to welcome President Zelensky and the Nordic leaders to Denmark. The Ukrainians’ fight for a free Ukraine and a free Europe continues,” Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said in a statement.

A large police presence could be seen outside the Danish prime minister’s office in Copenhagen.

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and his Norwegian and Finnish counterparts Jonas Gahr Store and Petteri Orpo were also to travel to Copenhagen.

The Nordic countries are key supporters of Ukraine and Zelensky traveled to Oslo at the end of October to meet with American envoys.

After that meeting, Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb had a 90-minute phone call with Russia’s President Vladimir Putin — which Frederiksen slammed and said had not been coordinated with Nordic neighbors.

Stubb said the talk with Putin had been “frank and substantive.”

“Almost five years after the full-scale invasion, the rain of bombs targeting civilians, relief centers, and water and heating plants continues. That is why we must stand firm,” Frederiksen said Tuesday.

Copenhagen police announced that they would increase security for coming days. They have introduced a ban on the use of drones over the capital until November 12.

World.title: India, GCC diplomats, business leaders to meet in Kochi for AI, energy talks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Policymakers, diplomats and tech experts from across Gulf Cooperation Council countries and India will meet next week for talks on artificial intelligence, energy and logistics cooperation at the Kochi Dialogue diplomacy conclave.

Themed “Towards an Innovative and Integrated India-GCC Partnership: Resilience, Reinvention, Redefinition,” the forum will be hosted on Nov. 18-20 by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs and the Centre for Public Policy Research think tank in Kochi, southern Kerala state.

It will bring together government officials and business leaders from India, as well as delegates from the GCC countries — Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

“Kochi Dialogue aims to strengthen relations between India and the GCC by bringing together all key stakeholders … It provides a platform for meaningful engagement and a deeper understanding of the opportunities and challenges shaping India–GCC relations,” Dr. Dhanuraj, chairman of the Centre for Public Policy Research, told Arab News on Tuesday.

“Our objective is to strike a balance between bilateral engagements and multilateral discussions, recognizing the importance of both in shaping a stronger partnership.”

The conclave’s first edition was held in January 2025, focusing on trade and regulatory barriers. In 2026, the main issues will be capital flows, energy, security, connectivity and innovation.

“The expected outcomes of Kochi Dialogue 2026 include stronger engagement on investment opportunities, trade facilitation, strategic cooperation and institutional partnerships between India and the GCC. The Dialogue aims to identify areas of mutual interest, address existing barriers and encourage collaboration across emerging sectors such as energy, healthcare, technology, connectivity and food security,” said Dr. Dhritishree Bordalai, senior research associate at the center.

“The discussions are expected to generate opportunities for sustained engagement between governments, businesses and institutions, contributing to a more resilient and diversified India-GCC partnership.”

Millions of Indians have economic, professional and family connections with Gulf countries. Kerala, in particular, has strong links with the Gulf, and has historically been the largest source state of Indian migrants to the region.

The Gulf is also a major economic partner of India, accounting for over 15 percent of its global trade.

India-GCC bilateral trade stood at $179 billion in the fiscal year 2024-25, while cumulative GCC investments in India exceeded $21.14 billion as of September 2025.

The forum’s organizers say the event also reflects the increasing importance of strengthening the long-established India-GCC ties in the current geopolitical setup.

“Strengthening India-GCC ties is increasingly important amid geopolitical uncertainty, regional conflicts and disruptions to critical trade routes and global supply chains,” Bordalai said.

“The region is also home to nearly 10 million Indians, reinforcing the economic and people-to-people linkages. These interdependencies make cooperation essential for strengthening energy and food security, diversifying trade and investment partnerships, improving supply chain resilience and addressing emerging regional challenges.”

World.title: Egypt’s annual urban inflation eases to 12.7% in October
World.content:
RIYADH: Egypt’s annual urban inflation slowed to a nine-month low of 12.7 percent in October, down from 13.9 percent in September, partly reflecting favourable base effects, official data showed.

The monthly urban headline consumer price index, released by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics, rose 0.7 percent in October, compared with 1.8 percent in the same month last year and 1.3 percent in September.

The Central Bank of Egypt raised its key interest rates by 100 basis points on Oct. 29, taking the overnight deposit rate to 20 percent and the lending rate to 21 percent.

The bank said the move aimed to anchor inflation expectations and safeguard the disinflation trajectory amid challenging external conditions.

In its latest economic outlook, the central bank projected headline inflation to average 16.6 percent in fiscal year 2026/27, before easing to 8.1 percent in 2027/28.

It expects inflation to return to single digits in the second half of 2027, supported by tight monetary policy, although the outlook remains subject to regional developments and their impact on domestic prices.

“Following the CBE’s October 100-basis-point increase in the overnight deposit rate to 20.0 percent, we expect rates to remain unchanged at the December meeting and through the start of next year, with easing resuming toward mid-2027,” retail banking firm Emirates NBD said in a statement.

It added: “Our baseline remains for 400bps of cuts next year, taking the deposit rate to 16.0 percent by year-end, provided external pressures stabilise. Renewed pound weakness, higher import costs, and a potential January fuel-price hike remain the principal upside risks to inflation.”

Core inflation moderates

The data further showed that core inflation, which excludes volatile items, also moderated on an annual basis, declining to 13.1 percent in October from 14.1 percent in September, according to figures calculated by the Central Bank of Egypt.

On a monthly basis, core CPI inflation rose 1.2 percent in October, compared with 2 percent in October 2025 and 0.8 percent in September 2026.

October’s S&P Global PMI survey also pointed to persistent cost pressures, with private-sector firms raising selling prices at the fastest pace since June as input costs continued to climb.

World.title: Canada reimposes sanctions against 11 Iranian companies: statement
World.content:
PARIS: Canada on Tuesday said it was reimposing sanctions against 11 Iranian companies in the energy and banking sectors for contributing to the Islamic republic’s nuclear drive, ballistic missile program or the financing of “malign activities.”

The companies, which include the National Iranian Oil Company and leading banks Mellat and Melli, were delisted from Canadian sanctions in 2016. But the measures have now been reimposed “to disrupt Iranian financial networks supporting its nuclear program,” the Canadian foreign ministry said in a statement on the sidelines of the G7 meeting in Paris.

World.title: Saudi Arabia opens anti-dumping probe into steel imports from China, Turkiye
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Foreign Trade has announced the initiation of an anti-dumping investigation into the Kingdom’s imports of “hot-rolled iron or steel structural sections, angles, and shapes (light and medium categories)” originating in or exported from China and Turkiye.

The decision to launch the investigation was made in accordance with the Trade Remedies Law in International Trade, issued on Nov. 23, 2022, the Saudi Press Agency reported.

Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the law stipulates that the authority is responsible for trade remedy functions, including conducting investigations and reviews, and imposing measures, in compliance with the Kingdom’s international commitments, specifically the Anti-Dumping Agreement, the Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures, and the Agreement on Safeguards.

The law aims to protect domestic industries from injury caused by dumped or subsidized imports, safeguard against increases in imports, and defend the Kingdom’s exports that may be subject to trade remedy measures by other nations.

World.title: NATO holds submarine-hunting drills in Baltic
World.content:
STOCKHOLM: Eight NATO countries have started five days of anti-submarine exercises in the Baltic sea and a top commander called the ultra-silent underwater vessels a constant “threat.”

Based in Sweden from Monday to Friday, the submarine-hunting drills also involve Britain, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany and the Netherlands. The Baltic has become a key venue for the so-called war of “hybrid” tactics that Western nations blame on Russia.

Several thousand naval forces, submarines from Germany and Sweden, surface vessels from several countries and air patrols will take part in the staged hunts for submarines, the alliance said.

NATO has stepped up its naval presence in the Baltic, where, military experts say, submarine signals — the key to tracking vessels — can be more easily hidden in its shallow waters crisscrossed by intense shipping traffic.

“The submarine is the only technology at this point that can dominate that undersea consistently,” Rear Admiral John Craddock, the NATO commander for submarines, told AFP.

“And so since that submarine can still dominate from the undersea, you have to be able to find them,” he added, highlighting that detecting submarines was “a perishable skill.”

“We’ve got to practice it all the time because until we can make the oceans truly transparent, submarines are going to be a threat.”

Rear Admiral Nicolas Molitor of the French navy said that the Baltic, with its many undersea cables and pipelines, faces other threats.

“There is also the threat from vehicles or robots that can operate under the sea,” Molitor told AFP on the sidelines of the exercises. He said that surface vessels that drag their anchor on the sea bed could damage “essential” infrastructure.

World.title: Iraq faces test as Baghdad confronts Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is approaching a crucial era as Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi increases pressure on Iran-backed armed organizations, while the ongoing US-Iran confrontation and interruptions in shipping via the Strait of Hormuz pose threats to the country’s security and economy.

Since the war started in February 2026, Iraq has been under increasing pressure to prevent armed groups from pulling the nation into a larger regional conflict.

The militias’ military activity and political influence have hampered Baghdad’s attempts to impose complete state authority over security decisions.

According to rumors, Al-Zaidi is contemplating arresting members of Iran-backed groups as part of his attempts to uphold government authority.

The disarmament process, which was originally scheduled to complete in September, has been extended until June 2027; however, numerous armed groups continue to refuse to relinquish their weapons.

The conflict has escalated after a series of diplomatic talks, including with US special envoy Tom Barrack.

On November 5, Barrack met with Al-Zaidi in Baghdad to discuss regional security, economic cooperation, and measures to prevent the crisis from spreading.

He also met with Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council President, Faiq Zaidan, and emphasized the necessity of strong institutions and the rule of law.

The Baghdad discussions came soon after al-Zaidi spoke with US President Donald Trump over the phone, during which the Iraqi leader repeated that his nation would not allow its land to be used to attack other governments.

Following the conversation and Barrack’s visit, Al-Zaidi made an unannounced visit to Tehran, which the Iraqi ambassador to Iran later confirmed.

According to Iranian media, the Prime Minister met with key officials, including Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, as Baghdad worked to ease tensions between Washington and Tehran.

The diplomatic action emphasizes Iraq’s delicate position between the US and Iran.

While Baghdad seeks to negotiate between the two nations, it is also under pressure to tackle armed organizations with long-standing links to Tehran.

The government has taken other efforts to curb militia involvement, including ordering the cancelation of three commercial contracts at Mosul International Airport due to alleged ties to armed groups.

As tensions with Iraq’s young Prime Minister rose, armed organizations such as Kataib Hezbollah condemned the decision.

Meanwhile, interruptions at the Strait of Hormuz have highlighted Iraq’s economic fragility.

The nation is significantly reliant on oil exports flowing through the vital canal, thus disruptions to shipping pose a direct danger to government income, public expenditure, and economic stability.

Attacks on key infrastructure, such as the Khor Mor gas field in the Kurdistan Region, have raised worries about the impact armed conflict may have on Iraq’s energy supply and business climate.

The latest attack’s perpetrator has yet to be identified definitively.

For Iraq, the task is no longer only balancing ties with Washington and Tehran.

It is now a question of whether Baghdad can prevent armed groups from making autonomous military choices, endanger national infrastructure, and undermine the legitimacy of political institutions.

The next several months will decide whether Iraq progresses toward a future in which the state controls all weapons and security choices or whether it remains subject to militia influence and regional crises beyond its control.

World.title: US dollar consolidates at 169,000 dinars across major Iraqi markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar consolidated at the 169,000 IQD threshold across major secondary markets on Tuesday morning, November 10, 2026, breaking roughly a week of price stability near 167,000 IQD per $100.

According to morning trading data compiled across regional financial centers, physical banknote rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange bureaus posted retail selling rates at 169,000 IQD against buying bids of 168,250 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Selling desks recorded 169,000 IQD alongside purchase offers of 168,500 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices quoted retail sales at 169,000 IQD and buying rates at 168,500 IQD per $100.

The uniform 169,000-dinar selling rate across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra underscores nationwide synchronization in parallel cash pricing.

The movement maintains a persistent 17,000-dinar premium over the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official benchmark rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar), reflecting enduring demand for physical greenbacks in secondary commercial clearing and cross-border cash transactions outside the formal banking window.

World.title: Baghdad to host ITL Iraq Expo 2026 with 100+ global transport & logistics firms
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad is finalizing preparations to host the second edition of the Iraq International Transportation, Airports, and Logistics Expo (ITL IRAQ EXPO 2026) from November 25 to 27 at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, featuring over 100 specialized international companies representing 25 countries alongside major public sector transport entities.

Organized under the patronage of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and backed by Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani, the three-day trade exhibition and conference serves as a key platform to showcase investment pipelines and public-private partnerships across Iraq’s maritime ports, commercial aviation, railways, and land transit infrastructure.

The gathering unfolds against the backdrop of Baghdad’s accelerated infrastructure drive, centered on the phased delivery of the Grand Faw Port and the multibillion-dollar Development Road strategic trade corridor linking southern maritime terminals via rail and highway networks to Turkey and Europe.

The event will host specialized sessions including the Second Iraqi Transport Sector Forum, dedicated panel discussions on airport modernization, and bilateral roundtables connecting international engineering conglomerates with Iraqi state-owned transport enterprises.

World.title: U.S. Envoy Tom Barrack meets Supreme Judicial Council Head Faiq Zaidan in London
World.content:
London (IraqiNews.com) – U.S. Envoy Tom Barrack met in London with a senior Iraqi delegation led by Dr. Faiq Zaidan, President of the Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq, to conduct high-level discussions on the future of bilateral relations and outline strategic pathways for long-term cooperation.

The high-ranking Iraqi delegation featured cross-sectoral leadership spanning the judiciary, state intelligence, monetary policy, and energy. Key attendees included Judge Ali Hussein Jafat, Head of the National Center for International Judicial Cooperation; Judge Diaa Jaafar, senior investigative judge with the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court; National Security Advisor Qasim Al-Aboudi; and Head of the National Security Agency Basim Al-Badri.

The economic and infrastructure portfolio was represented by Central Bank Governor Nizar Nasser and Minister of Electricity Ali Saadi Wahib.

In an official dispatch following the London talks, Barrack emphasized that the discussions explored broad cooperation across legal, economic, and security dimensions, spanning judicial alignment, rule of law enforcement, energy development, foreign investment facilitation, and regional stability.

Barrack underscored that robust, independent judicial institutions and enhanced institutional integration between American and Iraqi legal frameworks remain essential prerequisites for restoring investor confidence, advancing statutory transparency, and unlocking sustainable economic growth in Iraq.

The meeting comes at a critical juncture for U.S.-Iraq engagement, where structural reforms in commercial dispute resolution, contractual protections, and administrative predictability are increasingly viewed as decisive factors in attracting Western private capital and institutional investment beyond Iraq’s legacy energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi oil price for Asian markets reduced by $6 per barrel
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The price of Iraqi oil destined for Asian markets has seen a further reduction for December 2026 shipments, reflecting ongoing adjustments to official selling prices for crude in response to shifts in global oil markets.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has decided to reduce the price of Basra Medium crude by $6 per barrel compared to the November pricing, setting the discount at $8.80 per barrel relative to the Oman/Dubai crude benchmark.

The reduction also extended to Basra Heavy crude; SOMO set its price for December at a discount of $11.80 per barrel against the Oman/Dubai average, compared to a discount of $5.80 per barrel in November.

The decisions follow months of dramatic swings in Iraqi oil discounts, interruptions to Gulf shipping, and an increase in the cost of insurance and transportation.

SOMO announced on Monday a reduction in the official selling price for Basra Medium crude destined for Asia for the month of December.

The state-owned firm set the price for this crude at a discount of $8.80 per barrel relative to the Oman/Dubai average, compared to a discount of $2.80 per barrel in the November pricing.

The company also set the official selling price for Basra Heavy crude destined for Asia in December at a discount of $11.80 per barrel.

This significant reduction in the price of Iraqi crude reflects an effort to enhance the attractiveness of Basra crude in Asian markets, which serve as the primary destination for the country’s oil exports.

World.title: Iraqi PM secretly visits Iran following Trump phone call
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – As part of regional mediation efforts, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi made an unexpected, secret visit to Tehran on Friday to meet with Iranian parliament speaker and senior negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

To help resolve the conflict between Iran and the United States, al-Zaidi’s short journey concentrated on diplomatic initiatives and de-escalation efforts.

The visit came after a phone conversation between al-Zaidi and US President Donald Trump, with the Iraqi government attempting to prevent the country from being involved in a larger regional conflict, according to reports quoting official and media sources.

Iranian officials, including top negotiator Ghalibaf, presented Tehran’s two-day plan at the discussions, stressing that Washington must respect Iran’s fundamental rights, lift sanctions, end naval blockade, and free frozen assets as part of the negotiations.

Iraqi Ambassador to Iran Yasser al-Hajjaj confirmed that a recent visit to Tehran—involving an Iraqi delegation or Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi—was private and unannounced, coinciding with reports of regional diplomatic discussions.

World.title: Iraqi, KRG PMs discuss 2027 federal budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi received on Monday the Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), Masrour Barzani, in Baghdad to discuss Iraqi Kurdistan’s financial entitlements and its share in the draft 2027 federal budget.

The precise amount allocated to the Kurdistan region of Iraq is a major source of disagreement. Approximately 12.7 percent is what the first draft budget suggests.

The KRG, on the other hand, is strongly advocating for 14.14 percent, claiming that the budget has to take into account Iraqi Kurdistan’s real population statistics from the most recent census.

Barzani has openly said that any distribution that falls short of this population-based proportion is unfair.

The discussions included establishing conclusive procedures to address persistent delays in the payment of salaries for Iraqi Kurdistan’s civil servants.

Recently, al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s resolve to ensure that Kurdish public sector workers receive the same treatment as their colleagues in other Iraqi provinces.

The diplomatic effort tackles long-standing disagreements on constitutional rights, compliance with Iraqi Federal Court decisions, and oil income sharing.

The meeting takes place at a critical time. The Iraqi cabinet is scheduled to discuss and submit the finalized draft budget bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq approaches OPEC to raise oil output ceiling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said that Iraq seeks to negotiate with OPEC to raise its oil output and obtain a larger export cap.

Although the country’s production capacity differs from its export capability, Khudair stated that Baghdad was still committed to the export quota set by OPEC.

Iraq’s discussions with OPEC took into account the challenges the country has faced over the past 50 years, as noted by Khudair.

The Iraqi minister indicated that Iraq deserves a rise in output to secure the financial revenues needed to expand infrastructure and implement government goals.

Additionally, Khudair reiterated Iraq’s commitment to the 4.43 million barrels per day production cap set by OPEC.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

According to al-Zaidi, the Oil Ministry will invite major foreign oil firms to a conference to attract investments, expertise, and technologies.

World.title: 'Our ties enjoy bipartisan support': India's first reaction to US midterm results
World.content:
For India, the midterm outcome presents both opportunities and uncertainties.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In its first reaction to the US midterm election results, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Tuesday chose to emphasise the bipartisan nature of relations between the two countries while steering clear of commenting on the political outcome.The response comes against the backdrop of a significant political setback for US president Donald Trump, whose Republican Party lost control of both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections.Democrats secured a sweeping victory, winning control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, in a result that is expected to constrain Trump's legislative agenda during the final two years of his presidency.Responding to a question on the midterm results, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the elections were an internal matter of the United States and declined to offer any specific assessment."It is an internal matter of the United States. I have no specific comment on them beyond underlining that India and the United States' relationship enjoys bipartisan support in the United States. We continue to work to further strengthen our comprehensive global strategic partnership that we share with the US," Jaiswal said.The MEA said New Delhi remained committed to strengthening its comprehensive global strategic partnership with Washington, signalling that it expects ties to remain a priority irrespective of which party gains political ground in the US Congress. For India, the outcome presents both opportunities and uncertainties.The two countries have witnessed considerable turbulence in their relationship under Trump's second presidency, with disagreements over trade tariffs, India's purchases of Russian oil, immigration restrictions and Washington's approach towards Pakistan emerging as major irritants.The Democratic takeover of Congress could provide New Delhi with additional avenues to engage with lawmakers who have traditionally supported stronger India-US cooperation. It could also increase scrutiny of the Trump administration's policies, including its approach to trade negotiations and foreign relations. However, a Democrat-controlled Congress does not necessarily translate into an immediate change in Washington's policy towards India.The US president retains considerable authority over foreign policy and trade negotiations, meaning Trump will continue to play a central role in determining the trajectory of bilateral relations. At the same time, congressional oversight could influence decisions involving defence cooperation, technology transfers, immigration and trade.

World.title: Digital arrest scams: SC seeks prevention plan from WhatsApp & others, sends notice to RBI
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has asked

and other digital intermediaries to submit details of the measures they propose to take to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes, directing them to share their proposals with the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) as well.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued the direction in an order uploaded on the court's website following a hearing on October 29.

The matter has been listed for further hearing on November 23.

The case, taken up suo motu, is titled âIn Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documentsâ.

âWhatsApp LLC (A Meta company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes.



They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C,â the bench said.

SC wants banks to compensate digital fraud victims

The court also reiterated its concerns over the role of financial institutions in preventing digital fraud, saying banks must be held accountable where their failure to exercise due diligence contributes to such crimes.

In its October 29 order, the bench said the

's proposed regulatory measures must include provisions requiring financial institutions to compensate victims when an investigation establishes that fraud occurred due to their failure to prevent or report suspicious activity.





âWe reiterate and emphasize that the regulatory measures proposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must mandate and incorporate suitable provisions that require financial institutions to indemnify victims of digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds and pay suitable compensation not less than the amount lost by the customer,â the bench said.

World.title: 'Unfortunate': Govt condemns anti-India campaign by Chinese vloggers, urges Bangladesh to take action
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday condemned an alleged coordinated anti-India campaign by Chinese nationals who have reportedly been filming videos in slum areas of Dhaka for months and portraying the locations as parts of New Delhi during livestreams on Chinese social media platforms.

During the weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal termed the incident as "unfortunate" and said that attempts to project a distorted picture of a country only undermine the credibility of those involved and those backing them.

"We have seen media reports in this regard. Such efforts to present a distorted picture of any country are unfortunate," Jaiswal said.

"Insofar as efforts to buy foreign elements to portray Dhaka as Delhi are concerned, the peddling of false narratives only undermines the credibility of those who are undertaking such actions and those who are behind them.



And I would urge the authorities concerned to take action against such people," he added.

According to recent media reports, Chinese vloggers and livestreamers have been recording videos in impoverished neighbourhoods of Dhaka, Bangladesh, while falsely identifying the locations as parts of New Delhi.

The videos reportedly feature derogatory remarks about India's living conditions, sanitation, food habits and poverty.





According to Prothom Alo, the activity has been reported in Sector 12 of Uttara and the adjoining Tekpara area of Dhaka, where local residents estimate that more than 150 Chinese nationals have been recording videos.

The vloggers reportedly walk through streets and alleyways carrying two mobile phones, livestreaming for hours and, at times, entering people's homes to film. Their activities, which have continued for months, have increasingly angered residents, who remain unaware of where the footage is being published and how it is being presented.

A Chinese national identified as Fangyou told Prothom Alo that the livestreams were part of product promotion activities on WeChat. A Bangladeshi woman, Ritu Akhter, who works as a guide for the Chinese nationals, said they also earned money by posting videos on platforms such as Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.

"This is New Delhi. Their homes are extremely dirty. There isn't even a fan inside the tin-roofed houses.

This place is quite underdeveloped, dirty and unhygienic, and the law-and-order situation is poor," she said.

Apart from the misleading portrayal of their neighbourhoods, residents have raised concerns over repeated filming and alleged intrusions into their homes. Some claimed that the Chinese nationals entered houses and even bathrooms while recording.

"Sometimes they enter our homes and start filming. We are not always properly dressed inside our houses. Imagine how it feels when someone suddenly walks into your home and starts recording," resident Rozina Khatun told Prothom Alo.

World.content:
India's vaccination drive gains ground, but millions still miss their shots.

Vaccine protects against What it prevents Tuberculosis (BCG) Severe TB in children, including brain TB Diphtheria Throat infection that can damage the heart and nerves Pertussis Whooping cough, particularly dangerous for infants Tetanus Muscle stiffness and spasms caused by bacterial infection Polio Viral infection that can cause permanent paralysis Measles Highly contagious infection causing fever and rash Rubella Viral infection causing fever and rash Hepatitis B Liver infection that can become chronic Hib Serious infections, including meningitis and pneumonia Rotavirus Severe diarrhoea in infants Pneumococcal disease Pneumonia and other serious bacterial infections Japanese encephalitis Viral brain inflammation spread by mosquitoes

Grown-ups need shots too!

Gaps in the vaccination drive

Closing the vaccination gap

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: What began withhas grown into one of the world's largest vaccination drives. Now, smallpox is history, polio has been eliminated, and maternal and neonatal tetanus are no longer public health threats in India.That's quite a flex!India's vaccination story is one of ambitious campaigns, millions of doses and some remarkable public health victories. The country was declared polio-free in 2014. A year later, it eliminated maternal and neonatal tetanus as a public health problem. Then, during the Covid-19 pandemic, it administered over 200 crore vaccine doses, including indigenously developed and licensed vaccines manufactured in India.And the drive is far from over.Earlier this year, the government added another shot to India's public health armoury with a nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination campaign for 14-year-old girls, aimed at protecting them against cervical cancer. It also launched an indigenously manufactured tetanus-diphtheria (Td) vaccine. From fighting childhood infections to preventing cancer,India's vaccine drive is continuously levelling up. According to the Union health ministry, full immunisation coverage climbed from 62% in 2015 to 98.4% in January 2026.Last year, the figure stood at 97.9%.However, there is still a long way to go.Lakhs of children are missing essential shots with coverage remaining uneven across states. At the same time, many older adults are still largely missing from the vaccination picture.But if India has come this far, why are so many people still missing their shots?India's vaccination story goes back more than two centuries. The first smallpox vaccination in the country was administered in Mumbai on June 14, 1802, after vaccine lymph arrived from abroad. Nearly a century later, in 1897, Dr Waldemar Haffkine developed India's first indigenous vaccine against plague, also in Bombay.The government's efforts to make immunisation more organised gathered pace in 1962 with the launch of the national BCG programme to control tuberculosis. This was followed by the Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) in 1978, which marked another step towards wider vaccine coverage.However, 1985 proved to be a bigger turning point. India launched the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), bringing free vaccines against 12 preventable diseases to children and pregnant women. The initiative laid the foundation for what has since grown into one of the world's largest publicly funded vaccination programmes.The scale of the operation today is enormous. Every year, the UIP reaches 2.9 crore pregnant women and 2.54 crore newborns every year, free of cost . A vast network of government healthcare centres, frontline health workers, cold-chain facilities and digital systems supports the delivery and tracking of these doses.The programme's vaccine basket has also grown over the years. What initially focused on diseases such as tuberculosis, polio and tetanus now offers protection against a wider range of infections, including rotavirus diarrhoea, rubella and serious illnesses caused by pneumococcal bacteria.Alongside this expansion came some major public health victories. India eliminated smallpox, yaws, polio and maternal and neonatal tetanus as public health threats. Immunisation has also contributed to lower child mortality and reduced the burden of diseases such as measles and rubella.One campaign, in particular, became a defining moment in this journey. Launched in 1995, the Pulse Polio Programme took vaccination beyond healthcare centres and turned it into a nationwide public movement. Its now-familiar slogan,, helped bring millions of people into the campaign. The last reported case of wild polio in India was recorded on January 13, 2011, in Howrah, West Bengal. In 2014, the country was certified polio-free.But maintaining high vaccination coverage is an ongoing exercise. Full immunisation coverage stood at 94.7% in 2022-23, slipped to 93.7% in 2023-24, rose to 98.3% in 2024-25 and eased to 97.9% in 2025-26.India has also made progress in reaching children who have not received any routine vaccines, commonly referred to as zero-dose children. Their share declined from 0.11% in 2023 to 0.06% in 2024.Vaccination is not a one-and-done exercise. Some shots are given at birth, others follow at carefully spaced intervals, and a few need boosters to keep protection going. But what exactly do these jabs do?A vaccine essentially prepares the immune system for an encounter with a disease-causing germ. It teaches the body to recognise the threat and respond faster if it comes into contact with it later. This reduces the risk of infection and, in many cases, prevents severe illness.In India, this protection begins at birth. Newborns receive vaccines against tuberculosis (BCG), polio and hepatitis B. The hepatitis B birth dose is particularly time-sensitive and should ideally be administered within the first 24 hours.The next round begins when the baby is six weeks old, with follow-up doses at ten and fourteen weeks. These vaccines protect against diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, hepatitis B, polio, rotavirus diarrhoea and infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae type B (Hib).Pneumococcal vaccines are also included in the schedule to protect infants against serious infections, including certain types of pneumonia and meningitis.The vaccination calendar does not stop once babies become toddlers. Between nine and 12 months, children receive their first measles-rubella dose, followed by a second at 16-24 months. Japanese encephalitis vaccines are also offered in endemic districts.As children get older, booster doses become part of the routine. DPT boosters are given during early childhood, followed by tetanus-diphtheria (Td) shots at the ages of ten and 16 to maintain protection.The schedule is also expanding beyond childhood infections, with cancer prevention entering the picture.On February 28, 2026, the government launched a nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination campaign, offering a free, voluntary, single-dose vaccine to around 1.2 crore girls aged 14. The campaign aims to protect them against HPV infections that can lead to cervical cancer.The rollout has gathered pace, too. By September 11, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered, with Uttar Pradesh accounting for the highest number at over 22 lakh.From a newborn's first vaccines to an adolescent's HPV shot, India's immunisation schedule covers several stages of life. But having vaccines on the calendar is only half the job. Ensuring that every eligible beneficiary receives the right dose at the right time remains the bigger challenge.The latest WHO-UNICEF estimates for 2025 suggest that India is making steady progress in getting more children vaccinated. Around 97% received the first dose of the diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis (DTP) vaccine, while 95% completed all three doses. Measles vaccination coverage was equally encouraging, with 98% of children receiving the first dose and 95% getting the second.There is another milestone worth celebrating. The number of zero-dose children, those who have not received even the first dose of a DTP-containing vaccine, fell from around 9.09 lakh in 2024 to 6.79 lakh in 2025. That's a decline of nearly 25% in just one year.India also achieved a significant first. For the first time since WHO-UNICEF estimates began in 2001, it dropped out of the world's top ten countries with the highest number of children missing measles vaccination.In this case, slipping down the rankings is actually good news!However, the progress is not uniform. WHO's 2025 estimates show that only 70% of newborns received the hepatitis B birth dose within 24 hours, while rotavirus vaccine coverage stood at 91%.India has made steady progress towards universal immunisation, with full vaccination coverage among children aged 12-23 months rising from 83.8% to 87.1%, according to vaccination card records.The household survey also brings out a gap that national averages can easily mask: differences between states. Full vaccination coverage among children aged 12-23 months ranged from 93.8% in Goa to just 64.3% in Nagaland, a gap of nearly 30 percentage points.The divide is visible in hepatitis B vaccination, too. While 91.9% of newborns in Goa received the birth dose, the figure was only 46.4% in Nagaland.In other words, India's vaccination report card may be improving, but the marks are far from evenly distributed. Where a child is born can still make a significant difference to the protection they receive.So, if childhood vaccines are free, why are so many children still missing their shots?The answer lies in barriers that go beyond the availability of vaccines. From caregiver hesitation to migration and poor access to healthcare, several factors can leave children partially or completely unvaccinated.A WHO report from April 2026 offers some insight. Under its TrackVac initiative, the vaccination status of 2,24,698 children was assessed across 143 priority districts in 11 states during 2025. Among children who remained unvaccinated, caregiver refusal accounted for 39% of cases, while migration was responsible for 34%.While these findings are based on targeted districts and do not represent a nationwide survey, they highlight two major hurdles in India's immunisation efforts: vaccine hesitancy and disruptions in access to healthcare.Migration, in particular, can interrupt a child's vaccination schedule. A family moving from one city to another for work may get its baby the first dose but miss subsequent appointments after relocating. In remote villages and underserved urban settlements, long distances, transport costs, limited awareness and the loss of a day's wages can also discourage families from returning for the next dose.Misinformation and fears about side effects add to the challenge. With several vaccines requiring multiple doses, missing even one appointment can leave a child only partially protected.The challenge, therefore, is not just to make vaccines free but also to ensure that families can access them easily, understand their importance and complete the recommended vaccination schedule.For many Indians, the vaccination chapter quietly ends with school, but adults need those shots too!Depending on age, health and vaccination history, adults may benefit from vaccines against influenza, pneumococcal disease, hepatitis B, shingles and other infections.Tetanus-diphtheria boosters still matter, and pregnant women receive tetanus-diphtheria vaccination under India's public immunisation programme. Older adults and people with chronic health conditions face higher risks from certain infections, so age-appropriate vaccination is especially relevant for them.Yet adult vaccination has mostly stayed in the shadows. According to an earlier TOI report, citing older Longitudinal Ageing Study in India data, highlighted strikingly low uptake among older Indians: just 1.59% had received the influenza vaccine, 0.74% the pneumococcal vaccine, 1.82% the hepatitis B vaccine, and 2.75% the tetanus-diphtheria vaccine. These are historical survey figures rather than fresh 2026 measurements, but they show how thin adult coverage has been.India's Covid-19 campaign, which delivered more than 220 crore doses, proved that mass adult immunisation can be done. Yet unlike childhood vaccination, there's still no comparable universal routine programme for older adults.But things are starting to change.In September 2026, Goa became India's first state to adopt a dedicated life-course immunisation policy for 2026-2036, initially focusing on influenza, pneumococcal and hepatitis B vaccines for eligible high-risk adults.Turns out vaccination isn't just a childhood routing but also needs to continue well into adulthood.Finding children who have missed their vaccines is only half the battle. Ensuring they receive every due dose on time remains the bigger challenge.The government has stepped up efforts to close this gap through initiatives such as Mission Indradhanush, which has vaccinated over 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women. The U-WIN portal, which had 11.87 crore children registered as of March 2026, is another step towards better tracking, helping health workers monitor vaccination schedules and send reminders for missed doses.WHO's TrackVac initiative also highlights how targeted follow-ups can make a difference. About 85% of the children whose records were verified were already listed in health workers' registers, while 53% were subsequently vaccinated.However, migration, misinformation and vaccine hesitancy continue to pose challenges, making community outreach and regular follow-ups just as important as vaccine availability.The challenge does not end with just childhood immunisation.Limited awareness, high costs and poor access continue to hold back adult vaccination, particularly among senior citizens. Experts call for India-specific adult immunisation guidelines, with routine vaccination against influenza, pneumococcal disease, shingles and tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis, as well as hepatitis B shots for high-risk groups.Clearly, closing the vaccination gap will require more than free doses and digital records. Timely follow-ups, better awareness and easier access must go hand in hand to ensure people do not miss out on protection.The goal is to make vaccination a lifelong priority, not just a childhood routine.

World.title: ‘No order required’: Delhi HC on Central Secretariat Club’s plea against de-recognition after Centre rules out fresh allotment
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Tuesday said no order was required on a petition challenging the directive to vacate the Central Secretariat Club after the Centre informed the court that it had no plans to allot the premises to anyone at present.

The central government made the submission during an earlier hearing of a petition seeking an interim stay on its decision to de-recognise the club, formerly known as Talkatora Club.

Taking note of the submission, the court ruled no order was required to be passed.

"Considering the above, no order is required to be passed. The petitioners are permitted to take away their belongings in the next one week. List on the date already fixed, that is, December 21, 2026," PTI quoted Justice Amit Mahajan as saying.



The high court was hearing an application filed by the Central Secretariat Club seeking an ad interim stay on the July 14 de-recognition order and the July 17 eviction order.

During the hearing on November 5, the Centreâs counsel submitted that there was no proposal to allot the premises to any party at this stage.

The court had earlier issued notice to the central government and sought its response to the petition.

What's the case

The bench of Justice Mahajan was hearing the clubâs challenge to the governmentâs de-recognition order and the eviction notice issued by the estate officer, directing it to vacate its premises in the Presidentâs Estate.





In its petition, the club alleged that the Department of Personnel and Training, through its July 14 order, had "arbitrarily, illegally and unconstitutionally" withdrawn the recognition granted to it.

The petitioner contended that instead of acting on its complaints about alleged irregularities during the tenure of the ad hoc committee managing its affairs, the authorities withdrew its recognition in February without issuing a show-cause notice.

Following the high courtâs intervention, the club was granted a hearing, after which a fresh de-recognition order was issued on July 14.

Manmohan Singh

had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country.

"Rahul ji, thank Modi ji for eliminating the Armed Maoists. Former PM Dr Manmohan Singh ji had famously described Left-Wing Extremism and Naxalism as 'The single biggest internal security threat' to India," Rijiju said.

"Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals," he added.

This comes a day after Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.



In a post on X addressed to CRPF personnel who attended PM Modi's Diwali event in Bastar, Rahul said, "Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals."

"My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place," he said, adding, "My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won't have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again."

The war of words began after PM Modi, while celebrating Diwali with security personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, said that although armed Naxalites had been wiped out from forests, "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated several organisations and political parties and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy.





The Prime Minister also accused previous governments of restricting the freedom of security personnel engaged in anti-Naxal operations, saying his government had given them the authority to take necessary decisions.

"We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," PM Modi said.

The remarks came months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism, following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.

World.title: 'Why are we becoming Vishwaguru in air pollution?' Congress questions PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress president

on Tuesday targeted the BJP-led government at the Centre over rising air pollution in Delhi, asking why the national capital was becoming a âVishwaguruâ in pollution.

In a post on X, Kharge said that clean air is a fundamental right, not a privilege to be granted by the Government.

âWhy are we becoming a âVishwaguruâ in air pollution? Piecemeal measures, PR stunts, broken promises and blame games have become the hallmark of the BJP,â he said.

Delhi has been witnessing deteriorating air quality following Diwali, with pollution from multiple sources, including stubble burning in neighbouring states, adding to the crisis.



Kharge on X

Kharge flags missing PM2.5 readings at 36 monitoring stations

The Congress chief alleged that discrepancies in air quality monitoring had raised further questions over the government's handling of pollution.

Referring to last year's allegations of water tankers spraying water around air quality monitoring stations to bring down recorded pollution levels, Kharge claimed that this year PM2.5 readings had disappeared from 36 of Delhi's 59 monitoring stations as pollution peaked.





He accused the Modi government of failing to address the problem despite identifying air pollution as a major challenge in 2019.

Kharge cites pollution-linked deaths, unspent funds

The Congress president also cited estimates of deaths linked to air pollution to underline the scale of the public health crisis.

According to figures cited in his post, an estimated 17,188 deaths in Delhi in 2023 were attributable to particulate air pollution, accounting for nearly 15% of all deaths, based on Global Burden of Disease and Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air estimates.

He also referred to the State of Global Air 2024 report, which estimated that 1,69,400 children under the age of five died from air-pollution-related causes across India in 2021.

Kharge further questioned the utilisation of funds earmarked for tackling pollution in Delhi.

Citing a September 2026 RTI response, he said Rs 1,154 crore, nearly 60% of Delhi's environmental compensation collections, remained unspent.

He also claimed that the city had utilised only 17% of the National Clean Air Programme funds released up to December 2025.

Kharge invokes Supreme Court deadline for states

Kharge also pointed to the Supreme Court's direction to BJP-ruled Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to submit detailed responses and proposed measures to tackle the pollution crisis within two weeks.

He said the same pattern of toxic air, assurances and blame-shifting returned every year, particularly between October and February.

âYear after year, particularly from October to February, the same toxic haze returns, accompanied by the same assurances and the same finger-pointing. Spend the funds. Cut emissions. Enforce the rules,â he said.

Kharge ended his post by challenging the Prime Minister to account for the government's efforts to improve air quality.

âWill Modi ji dare to give the nation 'Hawa Ka Hisaab'?â he asked.

World.title: Why has Tamil Nadu opted for an expensive electricity purchase agreement? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) recently signed a power purchase agreement at over ₹30 per unit. This has been criticised by various Opposition parties, which have condemned the rate the State has to pay, drawing comparisons with other States that are paying much lower rates for power purchase agreements.

The government has clarified that due to the high demand for electricity in the State this time, thanks to a prolonged summer-like situation, it has had to opt for such an agreement. Energy Resources Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar has claimed that at the moment, only gas power is available for purchase, and attributed the high cost of the power purchase agreement to the same.

World.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led govt. in Tamil Nadu enjoys public goodwill despite concerns on being directionless
World.content:
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government in Tamil Nadu, which completed six months in office on Monday (November 9, 2026), appears to be largely enjoying the goodwill of people, even though concerns are being raised about the regime’s tendency to be directionless.

Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an “empty coffer,” the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures. The “precarious” financial condition did not come in the way of his government carrying out some other steps such as the extension of the breakfast scheme for school students, the provision of gold rings to babies born at government hospitals, the distribution of eight-gram gold coins and silk saris to eligible women, and the expansion of free travel for women on buses of the State Transport Corporations.

Reports of a “marked reduction“ in corruption regarding government appointments, transfers, and public services have impressed many observers including former Union Minister P. Chidambaram and UN diplomat-turned-political writer R. Kannan.

‘Transparency, strongest asset’

In an interview with this newspaper a couple of months ago, Mr. Chidambaram stated: “I also understand that sanctions for the appointment of teachers in [government-aided] schools and colleges have been sent by post.”

According to Mr. Kannan, “transparency remains the Vijay administration’s strongest asset.” The ruling party’s national spokesperson, Americai V. Narayanan, says: “He [Mr. Vijay] does not do things to please others or earn applause. He does them because he genuinely believes in them. In politics, where symbolism often outweighs conviction, that distinction matters.”

Areas of criticism

Notwithstanding the general perception about the government‘s integrity, the two Dravidian majors — the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) — have been unsparing. One of the areas of their attack is on the power front, where the current regime had, ironically, begun with the increase in the quantum of free power to 200 units bimonthly to domestic consumers subject to the overall consumption not exceeding 500 units. The regime’s plans for power purchase on a short-term basis at a higher cost has raised questions about the government’s competence.

DMK president M.K. Stalin and AIADMK’s Amma Peravai secretary R.B. Udhayakumar wondered when Keralam could buy electricity at lower price, why Tamil Nadu has not been able to procure at comparable rates. Besides, even the lower price has triggered a controversy in the neighbouring State.

It is not only on the power front where the government is found on a weak wicket but also on many other policy matters. On the issue of wooing industrial investment, the Opposition’s attack has not been firmly rebutted by the government. As for the TVK regime’s project of building a new Secretariat complex, there has not been any categorical statement from the Chief Minister on the controversy triggered by it, though his Ministerial colleagues, at times, make different observations.

Govt. appears directionless: Kannan

“The new government often appears directionless, evidenced by hasty decision-making and conspicuous silence on controversial issues,“ Mr. Kannan observes. He adds that moving forward, the priority must shift from perpetual campaigning to effective governance.

A senior citizen, who calls himself a “well wisher“ of the ruling party, points out that “a structured, periodic forum for district and block-level leaders would help. Without it, the party could pay a price in the forthcoming local body elections.”

Even as the TVK government faces a host of challenges in sustained governance, it is also expected to fulfil its key electoral promises such as the increase in the monthly assistance for women to ₹2,500.

World.title: Chennai police arrest 36 persons in citywide crackdown on ‘rowdies’
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Police arrested 36 persons, including 16 history-sheeters, during a citywide crackdown on “rowdies” conducted on Monday (November 9, 2026).

On the instructions of Greater Chennai Police Commissioner A. Amalraj, police teams led by inspectors conducted intensive checks, interrogations, and search operations across all police districts under the supervision of Deputy Commissioners of Police.

During the operation, the police apprehended and questioned 222 persons, including 185 persons classified as “rowdies” with criminal backgrounds and history sheets maintained at various police stations in Chennai. Of them, 36 persons, including 16 history-sheeters, were arrested and remanded in judicial custody.

The police are continuing their investigation into the current criminal activities of the remaining 186 persons, including 169 history-sheeters.

Mr. Amalraj warned that legal action would be taken against those involved in criminal activities or acts that threaten law and order.

Special drive against ‘rowdies’ in Avadi

A special drive to verify the antecedents and activities of “rowdies” was conducted on Tuesday in Avadi and Red Hills police districts under the Avadi Police Commissionerate.

During the operation, 339 “rowdies” were checked, of whom 48 were arrested. Another 258 were sent away after being warned, while bonds for good behaviour were obtained from 16 persons.

The special drive was conducted to prevent criminal activities and maintain law and order in the commissionerate, said Avadi City Police Commissioner T.Senthil Kumar.

World.title: Students present solutions to tackle food waste, nutrition and climate change at STHIRA 2026
World.content:
The third edition of STHIRA 2026, a sustainable food innovation challenge, was jointly hosted by Foodwize and the University of Gastronomic Sciences of Pollenzo, Italy recently at BIC Bengaluru. The competition saw participants from over 80+ teams from across 16 States in India under various disciplines of education, from chefs and engineers to humanities students.

The finale of STHIRA 2026 brought together 11 finalist teams from universities across India. The participating teams exhibited their prototypes and presented their innovations within the given time limit. The five-member jury evaluated the teams based on various factors including nutrition, cultural influence and climate resilience.

The four themes for this edition are access to nutrition, better livelihoods for small scale farmers, shaping urban food futures and reviving indigenous ingredients and traditional practices.

Incorporated in 2023 by Srijata Sengupta and Priya Joshi, Foodwize is a social initiative focusing on food systems, food cultures, transformation, development and experience design. Talking about the finale, Srijata says, “The purpose behind STHIRA was to encourage students to find solutions for some of the complex problems in our food systems today.”

The three winning teams receive a cash prize. “The winners will also receive hand-painted plates as trophies. We’ve been following this design so that our trophy is not just another cup but something deeply rooted with food and culinary traditions,” says Priya.

The presented prototypes included food solutions for artificial food colouring, exhibited as a solution through extracted natural pigmentation from beetroots and dragon fruit peels. A prototype focused on gut health and fighting heat through a traditional Odisha drink, Tanka Torani traditionally prepared as an offering for Lord Jagannath.

Further innovative ideas included nutritious food choices for present day college students who skip breakfast. A reintroduction of the traditional podi used to enhance tastes of various dishes or consumed with southern Indian breakfast staples including idli and dosa.

Abria Koshy, a student from IHM Aurangabad says, “STHIRA gave us an opportunity to come up with sustainable idea for present-day food challenges. My team, Rasa Roots focuses on making condiments through regional ingredients from Kerala and Mizoram.”

STHIRA and Foodwize also present multiple opportunities to all the finalist participants in taking their innovation forward. Their MOU with IIM Bengaluru helps the participants get an opportunity to enter the NSRCEL startup incubator programme.

“We are starting this incubator program to nurture food enterprises that are committed to sustainable food products and services,” says Priya “They also focus on the livelihoods of people in the supply chain, on the environmental impact of their business and their contribution to protecting and preserving food cultures.” The incubator is designed to provide six months of mentoring capability development and nurturing support.

One of the winning teams, Waste to Wax by Saranya Warrier of Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetaam, focused on converting jackfruit processing residues into natural coatings.

Full Circle Feed Co. by Anushka Sahu, Antman Deshpande, Aditya Kannojia of IIM, Indore, also a winning entry, addresses organic food waste and rising animal feed costs by converting market waste into locally produced feed.

Poshan Plate by Suhas Bhat, Sahana Shetty, Rohit Rawal of Alliance University, working to improve nutritional quality and dietary diversity in institutional meals was another winner.

Jury member, K L Mukesh says, “Initiatives like this will introduce more entrepreneurs in the ecosystem. Fresh start-ups and small businesses will create a lot of new employment opportunities with diversity.”

World.title: In veiled dig at Satheesan, UDF convener Adoor Prakash questions delay in convening meeting of ruling front
World.content:
In a veiled dig at Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, senior Congress leader and United Democratic Front (UDF) convenor Adoor Prakash on Tuesday questioned the delay in convening a meeting of the ruling front, signalling continuing differences within the coalition.

When reporters asked why the UDF had not met recently, Mr. Prakash said the question should be directed to its chairman, a post held by Mr. Satheesan. “This question should be asked to the UDF chairman,” he said.

However, the senior leader denied that he had expressed dissatisfaction with the functioning of the government recently, saying he had only voiced certain opinions and remained firm on them. “I have not expressed any dissatisfaction. I only voiced certain opinions, and I stand by them,” he told reporters.

He also said that it was not necessary for him to be informed about every matter being taken by the Cabinet in his capacity as UDF convenor.

Responding to Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president Sunny Joseph’s reported remark that he was learning about certain developments through the media, Mr. Prakash said the question should be directed to Mr. Joseph, adding that he might have made the observation in his capacity as a Minister.

“What is emerging now is proof of collective responsibility in the Cabinet,” he said, adding that a decision on appointments to chairperson posts in boards and corporations should be taken without further delay.

His remarks come a month after he publicly expressed displeasure over the functioning of the ruling front and the Chief Minister, alleging that he was being kept out of several important decisions and had to learn about them through the media.

Prakash, a senior Lok Sabha MP and former minister, had then described the situation as “serious neglect” of the UDF convenor and said he would formally convey his strong dissatisfaction to the AICC.

“A convenor of a front, holding a responsible position, having to learn about important government policies and decisions through news reports in newspapers and television channels amounts to serious neglect,” he had said.

World.title: Palaniswami, Dhinakaran demand probe into TVK Kallakurichi MLA’s alleged harassment of Collector
World.content:
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami and AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran demanded a probe into the allegation that Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh, who belonged to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), had sent an inappropriate message to Kallakurichi District Collector J.E. Padmaja and behaved in an indecent manner under the influence of alcohol at the official residence of the Collector. [The legislator has denied the charge.]

In their respective social media handles, the two leaders questioned the government’s commitment to the security of women when the District Collector herself was being harassed. Mr. Palaniswami demanded the arrest of the MLA and asked the ruing party whether it would indulge in a “cover-up” of this event, as it did in respect of Srivaikuntam legislator G. Saravanan, who was also reported to have been involved in an incident of sexual harassment.

Mr. Dhinakaran wanted an elaborate investigation to be conducted into the matter and said that if the legislator was found guilty, he should be given the maximum punishment.

World.title: CISCE announces ICSE and ISC 2027 examination timetable
World.content:
The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) announced the examination schedules for the ICSE (Class 10) and ISC (Class 12) 2027 examinations.

The ICSE examination will commence on February 15 (Monday) and conclude on March 31 (Wednesday). The ISC examination will begin on February 9 (Tuesday) and conclude on April 8 (Thursday).

Website to check subject-wise timetables

The distribution of admission cards for examinations will begin in mid-December. Candidates can access the subject-wise timetables through the official CISCE website: https://cisce.org/

According to CISCE, a total of 3,79,980 candidates (about 2.70 lakh for ICSE and over 1.1 lakh for ISC) are expected to appear across 2,835 examination centres in India and overseas.

Change in examination timings

A major operational change for the ICSE 2027 examinations concerns the examination timings. The reading time will begin at 10 a.m., followed by the writing examination at 10.15 a.m. Previously, these timings were 10.45 a.m. and 11 a.m., respectively. Candidates must be seated in their examination halls by 9.45 a.m.

The ICSE Class 10 examination will cover 76 subjects/papers, while the ISC examination will include 60 subjects.

States with the highest number of ICSE and ISC students

As per enrolment figures, the CISCE said Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of candidates in both examinations, with 51,168 ICSE and 34,702 ISC candidates. West Bengal follows with 46,521 ICSE and 30,235 ISC candidates. Other States with significant ICSE enrolment include Karnataka, Maharashtra, Punjab and Jharkhand.

CISCE Chief Executive and Secretary Joseph Emmanuel stated that the council remains committed to ensuring transparency, fairness and integrity in the examination process. He also highlighted the importance of competency-oriented assessment in encouraging students to apply their knowledge, think critically, solve problems and respond creatively to real-world situations, in line with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

World.title: Telangana directs Gram Panchayats to open separate bank accounts for own revenue
World.content:
The Telangana government has initiated steps to enable gram panchayats to manage their own revenue through dedicated bank accounts, with the Panchayat Raj Department directing all District Panchayat Officers (DPOs) to ensure the opening of separate zero-balance savings accounts for gram panchayats across the State.

The move follows an amendment to Section 70(3) of the Telangana Panchayat Raj Act, 2018, through the Telangana Panchayat Raj (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2026. The government issued orders recently notifying October 9, 2026, as the date of commencement of the amendment.

Commissioner of Panchayat Raj and Rural Employment Divya Devarajan instructed DPOs to facilitate the opening of dedicated accounts for all receipts and expenditure relating to the Own Source Revenue (OSR) of gram panchayats.

The accounts will be opened in the name of ‘OSR Account – [Gram Panchayat Name]’ at designated branches of the State Bank of India (SBI) and Union Bank of India (UBI).

The department has announced designated SBI branches for gram panchayats in 15 districts, including Mahbubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Narayanpet, Sangareddy, Siddipet, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Khammam, Rangareddy and Vikarabad.

UBI branches were assigned to 16 districts, including Adilabad, Nirmal, Karimnagar, Nizamabad, Kamareddy, Hanumakonda, Warangal, Mulugu, Jangaon and Mahabubabad.

The Commissioner said the banks were already requested to issue instructions to their branches to facilitate the opening and configuration of the accounts on a priority basis. The memorandum specified that the accounts should be used exclusively for receipts and expenditure under the Gram Panchayats own revenue sources.

Under the amended provision, all funds received by Gram Panchayats, including those under Central and State government schemes, must be deposited promptly in the nearest nationalised bank, cooperative bank or post office in the prescribed manner. Earlier, Gram Panchayats were required to route their own-source revenue through the government treasury.

World.title: £190m corruption case: IHC adjourns hearing for 10 days, orders meeting between Imran and legal team
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday adjourned for 10 days the hearing of appeals filed by PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, against their convictions in the £190 million reference.

The couple is serving prison sentences in the £190m corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. An accountability court had sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years.

The IHC also directed the authorities to facilitate meetings between Imran and his legal team.
